choices.explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration uses AWS edge locations to accelerate uploads into a single S3 bucket from globally distributed sites. Multipart upload is appropriate for very large objects and keeps the design operationally simple.
Regional staging buckets add replication configuration, intermediate storage, and cleanup. That is more operational work than uploading directly to the destination bucket with Transfer Acceleration.
Physical devices must be ordered, loaded, and shipped. Daily device jobs add logistical delays and operational work despite the sites already having high-speed internet connections.
EBS snapshots restore block volumes, not objects in the destination S3 bucket. This also adds EC2 management, snapshot copying, and another transfer step before the data reaches S3.
Loading the logs into Redshift introduces a separate data-loading pipeline and warehouse configuration. Simple on-demand SQL over the existing S3 files does not require that additional architecture.
The logs would need to be ingested into CloudWatch Logs first. Even though CloudWatch supports query languages, moving the existing S3 data introduces changes that direct Athena queries avoid.
Amazon Athena queries data directly in S3 with standard SQL and is serverless, so it requires the least architectural change and operational overhead for simple on-demand queries.
The Glue catalog can help describe the data, but provisioning and operating an EMR Spark cluster is unnecessary for these simple queries. Athena can query the existing S3 files without a cluster.

choices.solution: Add the aws:PrincipalOrgID global condition key with a reference to the organization ID to the S3 bucket policy.

choices.explanation: PrincipalOrgPaths can restrict access by organizational path, but creating departmental OUs and maintaining path conditions is unnecessary when the requirement is simply organization-wide membership.

CloudTrail reports account changes; it does not itself enforce bucket access. Maintaining a custom policy-update process for membership events adds overhead and potential delays before access is revoked.

Principal tags identify attributes assigned to principals, not organization membership. Tagging every user adds ongoing administration and does not automatically exclude an account that leaves the organization.
Exporting logs changes where the data is stored but does not give the EC2 application a private network route to its existing S3 bucket.
An instance profile grants permissions. It does not provide network connectivity, so the instance still needs a reachable S3 endpoint.
API Gateway is not a direct VPC endpoint for S3. A private API requires additional integration configuration; the proposed private link alone does not provide the required S3 connection.
A one-time copy aligns the volumes only temporarily. New uploads can still reach different servers and leave their independent EBS volumes inconsistent.
Session affinity can keep a user on one server, but it does not combine documents stored on both servers. A server failure or a different session can expose the same inconsistency.
An Application Load Balancer forwards each request to a selected target; it does not broadcast the request and merge documents from multiple responses.
Copying all 70 TB over the network consumes the very bandwidth the requirement seeks to minimize. Granting an IAM role does not reduce the transfer volume.

AWS Snowball Edge is designed for offline bulk transfer of tens of terabytes. It moves the 70 TB without consuming the company's network bandwidth, which directly satisfies the requirement to use the least possible network bandwidth. Historical-service limitation: Snowball Edge is available only to eligible existing customers since November 7, 2025; new customers need a current physical-transfer or online-transfer alternative.
File Gateway uploads data to S3 over the network. It does not avoid transmitting the 70 TB, and deploying a gateway adds work for a one-time migration.

Direct Connect still transfers all 70 TB over a network connection and requires connection provisioning and gateway setup. It does not meet the least-network-bandwidth objective of an offline device transfer.

Kinesis Data Analytics processes streams; it is not a persistent fan-out message queue for each consumer. The option omits the independent message buffers needed to decouple all the consuming applications.
Scaling the ingestion servers addresses compute capacity but does not provide durable buffering or decouple producers from the dozens of consumers.

One provisioned Kinesis shard cannot accept a burst of 100,000 records per second. Preprocessing into DynamoDB also introduces extra components instead of providing an independent delivery queue for each consumer.

choices.solution: Publish the messages to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic with multiple Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) subscriptions. Configure the consumer applications to process the messages from the queues.
choices.explanation: SNS fans out messages to independent SQS standard queues, decoupling each consumer and buffering bursts. Standard SQS queues support nearly unlimited API throughput. SNS publish quotas are Regional, so provision sufficient throughput and make consumers idempotent.
Scheduled scaling follows predetermined times, so it cannot reliably respond to an unpredictable backlog. Queue-based scaling adjusts worker capacity to the outstanding jobs.
CloudTrail records AWS API activity; it is not a destination for application jobs. Retaining the coordinating primary server also preserves a central point of failure.

This retains the coordinating primary server instead of replacing it with a durable work queue. EventBridge event routing alone does not supply the proposed workers with an SQS-style backlog for resilient job processing.

DataSync copies files but does not provide a local cache-backed SMB interface or automatic S3 lifecycle management. Copying older files also does not by itself reclaim the original file-server capacity.
FSx for Windows supplies SMB storage, but this option does not retain a local cache for low-latency on-premises access or define the requested archival lifecycle.
Per-user S3 utilities replace the existing SMB access pattern and require client administration. Direct S3 access does not provide the local cache needed for low-latency access to recent files.
The option specifies an ordinary SNS topic, which does not guarantee the FIFO ordering required here. A directly subscribed Lambda consumer does not add that ordering guarantee.
A FIFO queue preserves order within each message group. A Lambda event source mapping polls the queue and processes each group in order; use one group if strict order across all orders is required.

An API Gateway authorizer decides whether a request is authorized; it is not an order-processing lock or queue. Blocking requests would reject orders instead of durably preserving their arrival order.
SQS standard queues provide best-effort ordering, so messages can be delivered out of order. The application requires a FIFO queue with a consistent message group for ordered processing.

Parameter Store can store encrypted values but does not provide a built-in switch for automatic database-password rotation. Implementing rotation separately adds the operational work this requirement seeks to avoid.
S3 and KMS protect the stored credential file but do not rotate the database password or synchronize the application with a new value. Credential lifecycle management remains a custom responsibility.
EBS encryption protects the volume at rest but leaves separate credential files on the instances. Password rotation and updating every copy still require additional management.
An S3 bucket is not a supported Global Accelerator endpoint. The static-content portion of this design therefore cannot be configured as proposed.
CloudFront distributions are not supported Global Accelerator endpoints. The accelerator can target the ALB, but not the proposed CloudFront distribution.
Global Accelerator cannot use an S3 bucket as an endpoint. Adding separate domain names does not resolve that service limitation or provide edge caching for the static S3 content.
Parameter Store does not offer the Secrets Manager combination of multi-Region secret replication and managed database-secret rotation. Those behaviors would require additional custom automation.
Encrypted S3 storage does not manage database credentials. A custom Lambda rotation process must update the database, stored credentials, and application access, increasing operational overhead.

KMS multi-Region keys manage encryption keys, not database-password rotation. DynamoDB global tables and custom Lambda logic introduce a separate credential-management system instead of using managed secret replication and rotation.
Redshift is an analytical warehouse, not a drop-in MySQL transactional database. A single-node design also does not supply the requested highly available, automatically scaled read replicas.
The proposed database is Single-AZ, so it lacks the requested high availability. Ordinary RDS MySQL does not provide Aurora Auto Scaling's automatic addition and removal of reader instances.

Memcached is a cache, not a durable replacement for the transactional MySQL database. Spot capacity can be interrupted and does not establish a highly available database with automatically scaled readers.
GuardDuty detects suspicious activity and produces findings; it does not sit inline to filter and block the VPC's traffic.
Traffic Mirroring copies traffic for analysis. A mirrored copy cannot itself block or filter the original packets traveling through the VPC.
Firewall Manager centrally manages security policies, but it is not the packet-inspection engine. AWS Network Firewall provides the actual network inspection and filtering requested here.
QuickSight dashboard sharing is configured for QuickSight users and groups. IAM roles control AWS permissions and federation but are not the dashboard-sharing recipients proposed here.
Glue crawlers and ETL jobs prepare and transform data; they do not provide the requested interactive visualization and audience-based dashboard sharing. This option also omits the PostgreSQL source.
Federated Athena queries can combine sources, but exporting query results to S3 does not provide an interactive visualization dashboard with QuickSight-style user and group sharing.
IAM policies are attached to IAM identities, not directly to EC2 instances. The policy must belong to an IAM role delivered to EC2 through an instance profile.
IAM groups contain IAM users; an EC2 instance cannot assume or attach an IAM group. An instance role is the appropriate way to supply temporary credentials.
An IAM user cannot be attached to an EC2 instance. Using that user's long-lived credentials would also create unnecessary secret distribution and rotation responsibilities.
S3 object-created notifications put image-processing jobs into a durable SQS queue, decoupling uploads from processing.

choices.solution: Configure an SQS event source mapping for the Lambda function. Allow Lambda to delete messages from the queue after successful processing.
choices.explanation: A Lambda event source mapping polls SQS, invokes the function, and deletes messages after successful processing. Failed messages become visible again; processing must be idempotent.
Lambda does not continuously monitor S3 as a persistent process. An in-memory text file is not durable across execution environments, so it cannot reliably track processing or preserve pending work.
The EC2 instance and its local tracking file add state and a failure point. Lambda's SQS event source mapping already performs managed polling without a dedicated monitoring server.

Sending an email asks a person to process the image; it does not automatically invoke the compression workflow. EventBridge could route to compute targets, but this option specifies an email destination instead.

An NLB distributes transport-layer connections but does not provide Gateway Load Balancer's transparent insertion and encapsulation for IP inspection appliances. Additional custom network integration would be required.
An ALB handles HTTP and HTTPS requests, not transparent inspection of arbitrary IP packets. It is not a substitute for a Gateway Load Balancer appliance integration.
A transit gateway routes traffic between attached networks; it does not by itself load-balance inspection appliances or supply the appliance endpoint integration specified in the correct design.

Gateway Load Balancer is purpose-built for inserting and scaling third-party virtual network appliances such as firewalls. A GWLB endpoint transparently steers application traffic to the inspection VPC before it reaches the web servers.
EBS snapshots restore to EBS volumes, not directly to EC2 instance-store volumes. Copying restored data into instance store would add a separate transfer and initialization step.
Multi-Attach exposes the same production volume to multiple instances. Test writes could therefore alter production data, directly violating the isolation requirement.

A volume is created from a snapshot; there is no subsequent in-place snapshot restore into an already created and attached blank volume. Manually reading restored blocks also takes time that fast snapshot restore avoids.

EBS Fast Snapshot Restore creates volumes from snapshots that are fully initialized at creation, eliminating first-read latency and immediately delivering provisioned performance. That directly matches the need to clone data quickly while keeping production and test volumes independent.
S3 static website hosting cannot run the dynamic order-processing APIs. Storing orders as S3 objects does not supply the low-latency transactional backend proposed by the serverless design.

This requires managing EC2 fleets, operating systems, load balancers, and database capacity. It can host the application, but adds significantly more infrastructure administration than the serverless option.
EKS introduces Kubernetes cluster and workload administration. The Cluster Autoscaler adjusts worker-node capacity, not the number of application pods as stated in this option.
S3 Standard provides multi-AZ durability, but keeps every object at the frequent-access storage price. It does not automatically reduce storage cost for the unpredictably cold files.

Standard-IA charges retrieval fees and assumes objects are accessed infrequently. Files that unexpectedly become hot can incur additional retrieval costs instead of being automatically moved between access tiers.
One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone, so it does not meet the requirement to withstand the loss of an Availability Zone.

Intelligent-Tiering is intended for uncertain access patterns. Here the archive date is already known, so a direct lifecycle transition to Deep Archive avoids unnecessary tier monitoring and intermediate storage.
Standard-IA keeps data immediately accessible at a higher storage price than Deep Archive. That extra retrieval readiness is unnecessary for files that are never accessed after the first month.
One Zone-IA still costs more to store than Deep Archive and sacrifices multi-AZ resilience. Its immediate access capability does not help an indefinitely retained archive with no expected reads.
Budgets tracks spending against configured limits and produces budget-oriented reports. Cost Explorer is the direct tool for interactive historical cost breakdowns by instance type.

Cost Explorer filters historical costs by service, instance type, and usage type to identify the effect of larger EC2 instances. Use CloudTrail to identify who changed an instance type; cost data alone does not identify the actor.

The billing dashboard provides summary views rather than the granular instance-type filtering needed for the investigation. Cost Explorer supplies that detail without creating a separate reporting system.

Cost and Usage Reports can support detailed analysis, but configuring report delivery and a QuickSight dataset adds setup and maintenance. The requested two-month comparison can be made directly in Cost Explorer.
Rewriting the function as a Tomcat application adds server provisioning, scaling, patching, and code migration. It does not introduce a managed buffer between ingestion and database writes.
Replacing Aurora with DynamoDB requires a database and application redesign. DAX accelerates DynamoDB reads; it does not solve the Aurora ingestion bottleneck described here.

An SNS subscription invokes processing as messages arrive rather than providing a separately managed SQS work backlog. SQS allows database-writing consumers to process and retry buffered work at a controlled rate.
Trusted Advisor provides selected best-practice checks, not a configurable history and rule evaluation of S3 configuration changes. It is not the required configuration-compliance monitoring service.
Inspector assesses supported workloads for vulnerabilities and exposure. It does not evaluate arbitrary S3 bucket configuration changes against AWS Config rules.

S3 server access logs record requests to objects and buckets; they are not a configuration-history and compliance engine. Adding EventBridge does not replace the missing configuration recorder and rules.

CloudWatchReadOnlyAccess grants access to more CloudWatch resources than this single dashboard. Creating and distributing IAM-user credentials is unnecessary when dashboard sharing supports the external viewer.
Sharing a single IAM account prevents individual accountability and grants broad viewing permissions. It exceeds the product manager's requirement to view one specific dashboard.
A bastion server and cached AWS credentials add server management and expose a reusable AWS session. They are unnecessary and broader than a shared link limited to the dashboard.
The AWS Managed Microsoft AD integration with IAM Identity Center requires a two-way trust with the self-managed directory. The proposed one-way trust does not meet that integration requirement.
The trust establishes directory connectivity but does not configure IAM Identity Center account assignments and single sign-on across the organization's AWS accounts.

Simply enabling IAM Identity Center and installing an identity provider does not configure the federation or directory integration. The option omits how the existing Active Directory users and groups become the SSO identity source.
An Application Load Balancer supports HTTP and HTTPS, not the UDP traffic used by this VoIP service. Global Accelerator cannot make an ALB handle an unsupported protocol.
CloudFront is an HTTP and HTTPS content distribution service; it cannot proxy this UDP VoIP traffic. Putting a latency-based DNS record behind CloudFront does not resolve that limitation.
Both ALB and CloudFront are unsuitable for UDP VoIP traffic. A weighted Route 53 policy also divides traffic by weights rather than choosing the lowest-latency Region.
A stopped RDS DB instance automatically restarts after seven days. With tests occurring only once a month, it would resume incurring compute charges well before the next test.

RDS for MySQL does not offer the proposed policy that automatically shuts down or scales the instance for this test schedule. Ordinary RDS storage autoscaling does not remove idle DB-instance compute charges.

RDS automatically restarts a stopped instance after seven days, so stopping alone does not avoid compute charges for the entire month. Keep a manual snapshot, delete the instance after testing, and restore it before the next run. Snapshot storage and restore time still apply.

A smaller instance still incurs compute charges throughout the idle period. Snapshotting and deleting the unused instance avoids those idle compute charges while restoring the required instance size for the next test.
Cost Explorer analyzes billing data rather than continuously evaluating every resource's tagging compliance. Manually checking and tagging resources adds ongoing effort.
A custom EC2 polling process requires code, server administration, scheduling, and maintenance. AWS Config provides the required tagging evaluation without that custom system.
Lambda avoids a polling server, but the team still has to develop and maintain its own tagging checks. A managed Config rule requires less implementation work.
Fargate runs containers, so it introduces compute charges and deployment management for content that needs no server-side execution.
An EC2 web server adds instance charges, patching, and administration. S3 can serve these static files without a running server.
An ALB and Lambda-based web server add request-processing components and costs that are unnecessary for serving static HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and images.

DynamoDB does not have the proposed built-in rule that removes sensitive fields before a write. Streams record changes after storage, so this option also stores the sensitive transaction before the required sanitization.
DynamoDB is not a native Firehose delivery destination as proposed here. Reading delivered S3 objects also substitutes buffered files for the independent near-real-time stream consumers.

Kinesis Data Streams durably ingests high-volume transactions and allows independent consumers. Lambda transforms records and writes sanitized data to DynamoDB. Downstream applications must consume sanitized output if they are not authorized to see the original sensitive stream.

Batching transactions into S3 files introduces delay and requires each consumer to discover and process files. That is a weaker fit for the required near-real-time sharing than a multi-consumer stream.
The service responsibilities are reversed. Config records resource configuration state; CloudTrail records the API events that explain who performed actions.
CloudWatch handles metrics, logs, and alarms but does not automatically supply the required history of AWS API calls. CloudTrail must record those events.
CloudTrail records API activity, but this design omits Config's resource configuration history. CloudWatch does not replace the API-audit role of CloudTrail either.
GuardDuty identifies suspicious behavior and raises findings; it does not supply the Shield Advanced protection and response capabilities for a large-scale DDoS attack on the load balancer.
Inspector identifies software vulnerabilities and exposure. It is not a DDoS traffic-mitigation service.

The application's DNS is hosted by a third party, so a Route 53 resource is not the application's exposed endpoint in this design. Protecting the actual ELB with Shield Advanced addresses the stated architecture.
SSE-S3 uses S3-managed keys, not the required customer-managed KMS key. Replication does not change that encryption-key ownership.
Although this option creates KMS keys, it configures SSE-S3 and therefore does not use them to encrypt the bucket objects.

Separately created regional KMS keys have independent key material. S3 replication with SSE-KMS decrypts and re-encrypts under the destination key rather than preserving ciphertext encrypted with the same multi-Region key material.
The serial console is primarily for troubleshooting boot and network problems. It is not the scalable, routine remote-administration workflow requested for all workloads.
A bastion host requires patching, availability management, network access rules, and SSH-key distribution. Session Manager avoids that additional host and key-management infrastructure.
A VPN introduces network provisioning and SSH-key administration. It can provide connectivity, but requires more operational setup than managed sessions authorized through instance IAM roles.
Replicating the entire site to every Region creates extra copies and routing administration. Geolocation selects a regional origin but does not provide CloudFront's distributed edge cache.
S3 buckets are not supported Global Accelerator endpoints, so the proposed accelerator cannot target the website bucket.
Transfer Acceleration is for accelerated S3 object transfers, not a website CDN that caches content near visitors. An S3 static website cannot simply be replaced with an accelerated website endpoint.
The diagnosed bottleneck is storage I/O, not memory capacity. A memory-optimized instance does not directly provision the required disk IOPS.
A burstable instance changes the CPU-capacity model, not the underlying storage performance. It does not address slow inserts caused by the storage bottleneck.
Read replicas offload reads, but inserts still write to the primary database's storage. Replication does not directly increase the primary volume's IOPS.
The EC2 ingestion fleet and storage script require server provisioning, patching, scaling, and maintenance. This conflicts with the requirement not to manage additional infrastructure.
An OpenSearch cluster adds an unnecessary search system and capacity management. Manual daily snapshots also fail the goal of a simple automated archival lifecycle.

SQS is a message buffer, not a queryable historical data store. Messages expire at the retention limit, and custom consumers must race expiration to archive them and implement their own analysis pipeline.
Scaling EC2 and moving notifications to SNS can improve throughput, but the team still operates ingestion servers and custom SaaS integrations. AppFlow removes more of that operational work.
A regular EventBridge rule cannot use an S3 bucket as the direct target proposed here. Event routing also does not itself perform the bulk SaaS-to-S3 transfer provided by AppFlow.
Moving the application into a container does not remove its custom integration work. Container Insights monitors workloads; it does not itself emit an S3 upload-completion notification as proposed.
A NAT gateway in each AZ can avoid cross-AZ NAT routing charges, but NAT gateway hourly and data-processing charges remain. An S3 gateway endpoint avoids the NAT path for this traffic.
A NAT instance adds compute charges and administration, and cross-AZ routing can still incur Regional transfer charges. It is unnecessary for privately reaching S3 through a gateway endpoint.
A Dedicated Host changes EC2 tenancy, not the network route to S3. The NAT traffic and associated transfer charges would remain.

Site-to-Site VPN uses the existing network path and does not remove the application's impact on internet bandwidth. S3 gateway endpoints also cannot be accessed directly from an on-premises VPN connection.
Physical device delivery and return shipping introduce delays that are unsuitable for a recurring, time-sensitive backup stream. A dedicated connection supplies continuous transfer capacity.
The bottleneck is the company's internet connection, not an S3 account service limit. Changing an S3 quota cannot increase the on-premises network's available bandwidth.
Versioning preserves earlier object versions so accidental overwrites or deletions can be recovered.
MFA Delete requires MFA for permanent deletion of object versions or changes to the versioning state. Ordinary deletes can still create delete markers.

Creating a bucket policy without defining a suitable explicit deny does not establish deletion protection. It also does not provide the version recovery and extra authentication supplied by the selected combination.
Default encryption protects confidentiality at rest; it does not stop an authorized delete operation or recover a deleted object version.
Lifecycle rules manage object transitions and expiration. They can themselves delete objects and do not provide protection from accidental manual deletion.
Lambda already operates across multiple Availability Zones as a managed service. Choosing more AZs does not add the missing durable work buffer for failed ingestion attempts.
An SQS subscription buffers SNS notifications durably while the downstream system is unavailable.
More CPU and memory can improve function execution, but they do not preserve messages that need retry after a connectivity failure.
Lambda uses concurrency controls rather than the proposed provisioned-throughput setting. Increasing execution capacity does not replace a durable queue with retryable pending work.
A Lambda event source mapping processes queued notifications and retries failures, decoupling ingestion from delivery.
Inspector detects vulnerabilities in supported workloads, not PII inside arbitrary S3 objects. A lifecycle rule also does not discover sensitive content before selecting objects to remove.

Writing and maintaining a PII-detection algorithm adds substantially more development effort than using Macie's managed sensitive-data discovery. Large files also require careful handling within Lambda's execution limits.

Custom PII scanning requires additional development, and an S3 lifecycle policy does not immediately remove objects based on scanned content without further tagging or automation. SES notifications do not supply that remediation logic.
Regional Reserved Instances provide a billing discount but do not reserve capacity in the three specific Availability Zones.
An On-Demand Capacity Reservation is scoped to a particular Availability Zone, not the Region as a whole. The requirement spans three AZs and needs one reservation in each.

Zonal Reserved Instances can reserve capacity, but require a one-year or three-year commitment. That commitment is unnecessarily long for this one-week event compared with cancellable On-Demand Capacity Reservations.

choices.solution: Create separate On-Demand Capacity Reservations in each of the three required Availability Zones in the specified Region.
choices.explanation: An On-Demand Capacity Reservation reserves matching EC2 capacity in one Availability Zone. Create one in each required zone and retain it for the event; a single reservation cannot span three zones.

ElastiCache for Redis is designed as an in-memory data store and cache. This option does not specify the persistence and replica configuration needed to make the catalog a durable, highly available primary store.
A larger instance store is still temporary storage tied to the instance. Its data can be lost when the instance is stopped or terminated, so increasing its size does not provide durability.
Deep Archive requires an asynchronous restore before objects can be read. That retrieval delay makes it unsuitable for a live website catalog that must remain readily available.

Object tags are not an SQL-queryable index of transcript content. Instant Retrieval provides low-latency object access but does not supply the requested transcript query engine or an automatic archive transition after a year.

choices.solution: Store individual files in S3 Intelligent-Tiering and catalog supported transcript formats for Amazon Athena. Transition them to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 year. Restore archived files to S3 before querying or retrieving them.
choices.explanation: Intelligent-Tiering suits changing access patterns during the first year. Athena can query supported formats in accessible S3 storage, but it cannot query objects still archived in Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Restore archived objects before querying; Glacier Select refers to the separate legacy vault service, not S3 Glacier storage-class objects.

Keeping every first-year object in Standard lacks Intelligent-Tiering's cost adaptation to random access. Searching metadata stored as S3 objects also needs an additional indexing or query mechanism that this option does not define.

A separate RDS metadata database requires a custom ingestion and indexing pipeline and additional database operation. It adds more infrastructure than cataloging supported S3 transcript formats for serverless Athena queries.
A custom Lambda orchestrator requires development and permissions for remote execution, and its runtime is limited. Systems Manager Run Command already performs managed fleet-wide command execution.

Patch Manager installs patches supported by the configured operating-system repositories and baselines. The question does not establish that the third-party software's fix is available through that mechanism; a custom Run Command can invoke its required installer directly.

A maintenance window is a scheduling mechanism, not the patch operation itself. Waiting for a scheduled window does not meet the requirement to apply this critical third-party patch as quickly as possible.
Firehose delivers streaming data; it does not schedule REST queries or send formatted email reports.
SES delivers the report by email; the application or Lambda function prepares the report content.
A Glue job adds unnecessary ETL infrastructure for a small scheduled REST request.
An EventBridge schedule invokes Lambda to query the application API and generate the report without maintaining a scheduler server.
An S3 notification supplies event metadata, not the required formatted daily HTML report.
S3 exposes objects rather than the standard mounted filesystem required here.
EBS volumes are AZ-scoped and need capacity management; EKS adds cluster administration.
Multi-AZ EC2 Auto Scaling replaces failed instances and adjusts capacity. EFS supplies shared file storage that remains accessible to instances in different Availability Zones.
EBS is AZ-scoped block storage, not an automatically growing shared multi-AZ filesystem.
Glacier archives require restoration, and an administrator can change an access policy permitting deletion.
IAM policies are mutable; administrators can remove the deletion restriction before ten years.
Deep Archive reduces long-term storage costs after the first year. Object Lock compliance mode protects each retained version for ten years even against privileged deletion.
Governance retention can be bypassed with permission; One Zone-IA also sacrifices multi-AZ resilience.
S3 object access replaces the existing Windows SMB file-sharing interface.
This keeps the EC2 file servers and their availability management instead of replacing them.
FSx for Windows File Server provides managed SMB shares and Active Directory integration. A Multi-AZ file system provides a standby and automatic failover.
EFS uses NFS, not the Windows SMB protocol the users already require.
VPC-local routing connects the subnets; route tables are not the appropriate application access-control boundary.
Security groups have allow rules only; an explicit deny rule cannot be configured.
A database security group can reference the application instances' security group so only that tier can establish database connections.
Peering connects separate VPCs, not subnets inside this single VPC.
Stage variables configure integrations; they cannot replace the API's public hostname or TLS certificate.
A Regional custom domain needs its certificate in ca-central-1, not us-east-1.
The certificate is in the wrong Region; an A record pointing to itself also cannot route traffic.
Comprehend analyzes text, not uploaded images for visual moderation.
Rekognition moderation detects potentially inappropriate image or video content. Route uncertain results for human review rather than assuming every low-confidence detection is definitive.
Training and maintaining a custom SageMaker model requires more development than managed Rekognition moderation.
A custom model on Fargate adds development, training, deployment, and container-operation responsibilities.
Installing Docker on EC2 still leaves server provisioning, patching, and capacity management to the company.
ECS manages orchestration but EC2 worker hosts still require infrastructure management.
Fargate runs ECS containers without provisioning or patching EC2 hosts, reducing operational work while preserving the container packaging.
An optimized AMI simplifies setup but does not remove EC2 host-management responsibilities.
Data Pipeline batch orchestration does not supply the scalable event-ingestion stream required for clickstream collection.
A custom EC2 ingestion fleet introduces server management and scaling instead of using managed streaming ingestion.
CloudFront caches delivered content; it is not a destination for persisting clickstream events.

Kinesis Data Streams handles ingestion, Firehose buffers and delivers data to S3, and Redshift provides warehouse analytics. Firehose delivery is near-real-time rather than immediate per-record delivery.
Blocking HTTP drops requests instead of redirecting clients to HTTPS.
Replacing URL text alone does not return the HTTP redirect clients need; configure an ALB redirect action.
An ALB HTTP listener can redirect requests to an HTTPS listener without changing the application servers. Configure a valid certificate on the HTTPS listener.
An NLB does not perform HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects; SNI selects TLS certificates rather than redirecting requests.
Instance metadata is not a managed secret store; custom rotation and metadata updates add operational work.
Encrypted S3 files still need custom code to coordinate database and credential-file rotation.
Secrets Manager securely stores and rotates database credentials. The EC2 instance role grants the application access without embedding long-lived AWS credentials.
Parameter Store does not offer automatic database-secret rotation as a built-in setting.
An ACM-issued certificate does not satisfy the requirement for issuance by an external CA.
Importing external key material is not part of requesting an ACM-issued certificate; imported certificates lack managed renewal.
A private CA certificate is not the required externally issued, publicly trusted certificate.

Import the third-party certificate into ACM and attach it to the ALB. Imported certificates are not automatically renewed by ACM; monitor approaching expiration with EventBridge and replace them manually.
S3 object-created notifications invoke Lambda promptly. Lambda converts the PDF and writes the JPEG back to S3; filter prefixes or suffixes to avoid recursively triggering on its own outputs.
A 5 MB PDF exceeds DynamoDB's 400 KB item limit.
EC2 conversion fleets add idle compute and maintenance costs; independent EBS volumes also complicate shared storage.
This adds container/server management, and the option still saves outputs to EBS instead of its proposed shared EFS.
On-premises users read across the VPN without a local cache, increasing access latency.
Cloud workloads would access an on-premises gateway across the VPN instead of their local AWS filesystem.
Direct S3 access changes Windows SMB access patterns instead of preserving the filesystem interface.

FSx for Windows File Server provides cloud SMB storage, and FSx File Gateway historically provided local caching for on-premises clients. FSx File Gateway has been unavailable to new customers since October 28, 2024; this choice applies only to eligible existing customers.
Custom extraction and PHI-detection libraries require more development and maintenance than managed services.
SageMaker requires building or deploying a PHI model; Comprehend Medical supplies managed PHI detection.
Textract extracts text from scanned documents and Comprehend Medical detects medical entities and protected health information in that text.
Rekognition text detection does not provide Textract's PDF document-extraction workflow.
Glacier Flexible Retrieval requires restoration, violating continuous immediate accessibility.
One Zone-IA cannot withstand an AZ loss; these critical files are not readily reproducible.
S3 Lifecycle moves eligible objects to Standard-IA after its 30-day minimum age and expires them after the required four-year retention period.
Archiving after four years adds ongoing storage instead of deleting data after the required retention period.
Creating another queue does not fix messages becoming visible before processing finishes.
Queue permissions control access, not concurrent delivery of an in-flight message.
Long polling controls empty receive requests, not the visibility timeout protecting an in-flight message.

Extend message visibility while processing and delete the message only after success. This prevents a long-running task from making the message visible too early, but standard SQS queues still provide at-least-once delivery; consumers must be idempotent.
Direct Connect provides the primary dedicated path with consistent network performance. A Site-to-Site VPN supplies a cheaper backup path over the internet if that connection fails.
VPN traffic traverses the internet and cannot provide Direct Connect's consistent primary-path latency.
A second dedicated connection costs more than the slower VPN backup the company accepts.
Direct Connect has no CLI failover attribute that automatically provisions a physical backup connection.
Cross-Region application and database recovery adds complexity beyond a multi-AZ design within one Region.

A Multi-AZ application group and Aurora Replica in another zone provide failover at both tiers. RDS Proxy pools connections and helps applications reconnect during database failover; it does not replace database redundancy.
A single AZ remains a failure point; hourly snapshots allow data loss and require restoration downtime.
An Auto Scaling group is Regional; an S3-to-Lambda database-write pipeline also adds unnecessary failure modes.
NLB HTTP health checks can detect errors, but this option omits automatic replacement of unhealthy instances.
A cron-based restart script violates the requirement to avoid custom scripts or code.

An ALB supports HTTP-aware health checks and removes unhealthy targets from routing. Enable Elastic Load Balancing health checks on the Auto Scaling group so unhealthy instances are also replaced. NLBs can support HTTP health checks too, so an NLB is not intrinsically unable to detect HTTP failures.
An alarm on TCP-based unhealthy-host results cannot detect HTTP failures that the NLB is missing.
Global tables replicate corrupt writes too; switching Regions does not recover an earlier uncorrupted state.

DynamoDB point-in-time recovery restores a new table to a selected time within its configured recovery window, with second-level recovery points. Restore duration depends on table size and indexes, so a one-hour RTO must be tested rather than assumed.
Daily exports cannot meet a 15-minute RPO; Glacier restoration also delays recovery.
DynamoDB tables are not customer-managed EBS volumes and cannot be recovered using EBS snapshots.
API Gateway is not a subnet routing appliance for S3 API traffic.
A NAT gateway adds processing charges and does not accept an S3 endpoint policy.
Public routing requires internet-facing instance connectivity; the endpoint avoids NAT charges while preserving private access.
An S3 gateway endpoint avoids NAT processing charges for same-Region S3 access. An endpoint policy limits allowed API access but does not itself grant permissions.
This prevents administrators from reaching the bastion from the on-premises internet connection.
Internet traffic arrives with the company's external source address, not its private internal range.
Allow inbound SSH to the public bastion only from the company's external IP range.
Allow inbound SSH to private application instances only from the bastion's private IP address. A security-group reference is also suitable where supported.
Bastion-to-application traffic inside the VPC uses the bastion's private IP address.
Allow public HTTPS on TCP port 443 to the web servers.
Outbound HTTPS permission does not let public clients initiate inbound connections to the web tier.
Allow SQL Server traffic on TCP port 1433 to the database only from instances associated with the web tier security group.
Outbound database rules do not authorize incoming SQL connections; security groups already allow established response traffic.
Opening HTTPS on the database grants an unnecessary port beyond the SQL Server connection requirement.
API Gateway and Lambda provide managed API processing, while SQS durably buffers inter-service work so an overloaded consumer does not cause dropped transactions.
Larger instances do not buffer transactions or decouple tiers when a downstream service becomes overloaded.
SNS does not expose a work-queue backlog to scale against; published-message count is not outstanding work.
SQS helps buffering, but EC2 fleets require more administration than managed API Gateway and Lambda.
Public-internet transfer remains subject to the bandwidth variability affecting this sustained 10 TB daily flow.
DataSync automates validated, encrypted data transfer, while Direct Connect provides a dedicated network path. Direct Connect alone does not encrypt traffic, but DataSync uses TLS.
DMS migrates database data, not arbitrary JSON files stored on a SAN.
Direct Connect improves transport but does not make DMS a SAN-file transfer service.
An EC2-hosted API adds server patching and scaling compared with managed API Gateway.
Disabling source/destination checks does not create a streaming Glue ingestion API; EC2 adds administration too.
API Gateway sends records to Kinesis Data Streams. Firehose invokes Lambda transformations and delivers buffered output to S3 with managed retries and scaling.
Sending API calls to Glue alone omits the defined stream-ingestion and Firehose delivery mechanism.
DynamoDB PITR retains at most 35 days of recovery history, not seven years.
AWS Backup schedules DynamoDB recovery points and applies seven-year retention, avoiding custom backup scripts. Backup retention does not itself delete live items from the table.
DynamoDB on-demand backups are managed backups, not files manually placed in a customer S3 bucket.
Custom Lambda export and retention automation requires more maintenance than an AWS Backup plan.
DynamoDB on-demand capacity bills for actual read and write requests and handles variable traffic without maintaining provisioned capacity during idle periods.
A secondary index supports queries and incurs capacity charges; it does not solve unpredictable table capacity.
Provisioned autoscaling reacts after demand changes and maintains capacity charges during idle periods.
Global tables add regional replication costs and do not resolve the proposed provisioned-capacity scaling delay.
Encrypted AMIs cannot be shared publicly; public availability would also exceed the partner-only requirement.
Share the AMI launch permission only with the partner account and authorize that account to use the customer managed KMS key protecting the EBS snapshots.
Key policies grant principals access; trusting another KMS key does not decrypt snapshots under the original key.
AMI export is not the secure cross-account launch-sharing mechanism for this encrypted EBS-backed AMI.
SNS is not the durable pending-job queue required here, and CPU does not measure backlog.
Network utilization can vary independently of pending jobs; queue depth directly measures the required scaling workload.

SQS retains pending jobs independently of the worker fleet. Auto Scaling adds and removes stateless workers as backlog changes; backlog per instance is preferable to raw queue depth for target tracking.
SNS publish count measures incoming events, not durably queued unfinished jobs.
ACM does not provide the proposed configurable rule that directly publishes custom daily SNS messages.
Trusted Advisor is not the configurable ACM expiration-compliance rule engine specified for this alert threshold.
EventBridge can match ACM events, but it does not itself inspect certificate dates without a defined source event or checker.
Migrating to another US origin does not add nearby European edge delivery and consumes launch time.
S3 cannot run the dynamic website backend, which must remain on premises.
CloudFront supports an HTTPS custom origin on premises, serving content from edge locations while keeping the backend in the United States.
Changing DNS routing to the same US servers does not add caching or shorten the origin network path.
Spot interruptions are unsuitable for this steady production workload; Reserved Instances charge during stopped test periods.
Reserved Instances discount the steady production baseline. On-Demand instances can be stopped outside development and testing hours without a long-term usage commitment.
Spot blocks are not a continuous 24-hour production solution; test reservations still incur idle commitment charges.
On-Demand pricing misses production's steady-use discount; Spot blocks are unavailable for the proposed test purchase.

S3 Object Lock protects object versions against permanent deletion and alteration during retention. Use compliance mode for non-bypassable regulatory retention and apply the required retention period.
Lifecycle archiving changes storage class but does not prohibit modification or deletion.
ACL permissions can be changed and do not enforce immutable object retention.
A read-only client mount can be remounted writable; it is not a storage-enforced WORM retention policy.
Secrets Manager stores the database credentials and supports automatic rotation. Authorize the web-server role to retrieve only the required secret and configure rotation explicitly.
OpsCenter manages operational issues, not securely distributed database secrets with scheduled rotation.
S3 encryption protects storage but does not automatically rotate the database credentials.
Local encrypted files still require updating every server when the password rotates.
RDS Proxy manages connections and failover, but does not durably queue writes throughout database unavailability.
Retries are bounded by Lambda's execution timeout and do not durably preserve data beyond an invocation.
Lambda local storage is ephemeral and isolated per execution environment; another function cannot scan it reliably.
SQS retains customer events while the database is unavailable. A separate Lambda consumer retries database writes after upgrades; make writes idempotent because messages may be delivered again.
With Requester Pays, the requesting AWS account pays the request and data-download costs instead. The original company still pays for storing the 3 TB in S3.
Replication incurs cross-Region transfer charges to the source bucket owner rather than shifting download costs.
Cross-account permission grants access but leaves normal request and download billing with the bucket owner.
Intelligent-Tiering reduces storage costs, not the source owner's cross-Region transfer costs for synchronization.
Versioning preserves previous audit-document versions. MFA Delete protects permanent version deletions and changes to versioning state; it does not require MFA for every ordinary delete request.
MFA for account sign-in does not enable S3 MFA Delete or retain recoverable object versions.
Lifecycle policies belong to buckets, not IAM users, and expiration rules do not deny deletion.
KMS restrictions protect decryption, not object deletion or recovery of accidentally deleted documents.
A conventional Multi-AZ standby does not serve the script's read queries to offload the primary.
A read replica moves the reporting script's read workload off the primary instance. It is asynchronous, so allow for replica lag in the report.
A manual end-of-day export misses the business-hours reporting deadline and adds operational work.
A cache requires application integration and invalidation; a read replica directly offloads the existing SQL workload.
An S3 gateway endpoint creates a VPC route to S3 over the AWS network without an internet gateway or NAT device.
S3 buckets are not deployed in VPC subnets.
Same-Region placement alone does not establish a private network route to S3.
A NAT gateway supplies internet connectivity rather than the required private S3 endpoint.
An S3 gateway endpoint provides a private route from the VPC to S3 without a NAT gateway.
Public bucket access violates protection of the sensitive user information.
A bucket policy limits authorization to the application role and, where required, the specified VPC endpoint; network connectivity alone does not grant access.
Copying long-lived IAM-user credentials creates secret-management risk instead of using scoped workload identities and policies.
A NAT instance adds server management and does not restrict bucket access to the application tier.
mysqldump still reads and copies the full database, preserving the latency and staging-refresh delay.
Aurora replicas handle read workloads, and Aurora cloning initially shares storage pages through copy-on-write. The staging clone remains independent without waiting for a full logical export.
A conventional RDS Multi-AZ standby is not an independently accessible writable staging database.
A full dump-and-restore still delays staging access and adds database-export load.
An EMR cluster and Aurora database add operational and idle-capacity overhead for tiny intermittent jobs.
EC2 queue consumers require server scaling and patching rather than execution only when work exists.

S3 events enqueue work in SQS and Lambda scales processing with demand without managing workers. DynamoDB stores the transformed JSON as document data; use S3 instead if a literal JSON file object is required.
Kinesis and Aurora introduce extra infrastructure for a simple one-time per-file transformation.
Reads served by the primary remain on the same instance as writes; Multi-AZ alone does not offload them.
A conventional Multi-AZ standby cannot serve application read traffic.
Undersized replicas can lag and become a new performance bottleneck under the existing read workload.
Read replicas offload eligible reads from the writer. The application must route reads to the replica endpoints and tolerate asynchronous replication lag.
The explicit deny blocks EC2 actions outside us-east-1, not inside it.
aws:SourceIp checks the caller's address, not the address of the instance being terminated.

The Allow applies only to TerminateInstances requests whose source IP is within 10.100.100.0/24. The explicit Deny blocks EC2 actions outside us-east-1. Therefore a request from 10.100.100.254 in us-east-1 can terminate an instance.
The caller address matches the allowed CIDR, and the outside-Region deny does not apply in us-east-1.
EFS provides NFS rather than the required Windows SMB filesystem and native AD integration.
S3 File Gateway is not the native multi-AZ Windows filesystem with full SharePoint-compatible filesystem semantics.
Mounting S3 objects does not provide native Windows file locking, SMB semantics, and AD integration.
FSx for Windows File Server provides managed Windows SMB storage with Active Directory authentication; choose Multi-AZ for the required high availability.
Long polling does not prevent redelivery; SQS also limits ReceiveMessage wait time to 20 seconds.
S3 event notifications cannot directly target FIFO queues, and FIFO alone does not make Lambda side effects idempotent.

choices.solution: Set the SQS visibility timeout to at least six times the Lambda function timeout, plus the maximum batching window. Make the function idempotent to tolerate redelivery.
choices.explanation: A sufficient visibility timeout prevents messages from reappearing while the first Lambda invocation is still running or retrying. AWS recommends at least six times the function timeout plus the batching window. SQS and Lambda still allow duplicate delivery, so email processing must be idempotent.
Deleting before successful processing loses the work if processing subsequently fails.
Storage Gateway shares use SMB or NFS, not the Lustre client protocol.
A self-managed Windows SMB server is neither managed Lustre storage nor protocol-compatible.
EFS supports NFS and cannot be configured as a Lustre filesystem.
FSx for Lustre provides a managed Lustre file system accessible to supported clients over private network connectivity from on premises.
Secret storage does not directly provide the requested managed encryption-operation interface for the application's data.
Custom cryptography introduces key-management code; storing function code in S3 does not establish durable encrypted-data storage.
EBS volumes are AZ-scoped; S3 provides the requested highly available encrypted-object storage with less volume management.
A NAT gateway in each public subnet provides IPv4 internet egress for private instances. Route each zone's private subnet through its local NAT gateway to avoid a cross-zone dependency.
A NAT instance in a private subnet has no direct route to the internet gateway; it must be in a public subnet to provide internet egress.
An internet gateway attaches to a VPC, not to an individual subnet, and does not provide NAT for instances with private IPv4 addresses.
An egress-only internet gateway provides outbound IPv6 connectivity, not IPv4 NAT.
Choosing an Availability Zone for the EC2 instance does not automate copying the NFS files into the regional EFS file system.
An on-premises DataSync agent reads the existing NFS file system and transfers its data to EFS.
An EBS volume is block storage for EC2, not the required EFS destination or an automated NFS migration service.
Manual copying does not meet the requirement for an automated transfer.

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync to configure the on-premises NFS file system behind the SFTP server as the source location and Amazon EFS as the destination location.
choices.explanation: Configure an NFS source location for the storage behind the SFTP server and an EFS destination. DataSync does not use SFTP as a source protocol.
Glue job bookmarks track previously processed input so later runs process new or changed data rather than repeating all prior work. Use a supported input format and stable transformation context.
Deleting source files changes data retention and requires additional handling; it does not track which files the Glue job already processed.
Reducing the worker count changes processing capacity, not the selection of previously processed files.
FindMatches identifies related records; it does not maintain incremental processing checkpoints.
Shield Advanced adds enhanced DDoS protection and response support for eligible protected resources.
GuardDuty detects suspicious activity but does not itself absorb or block a volumetric DDoS attack.
CloudFront distributes static and dynamic HTTP content through edge locations, helping absorb attacks and reduce load on the origin.
Adding individual attacker addresses to network ACLs is reactive and constrained by rule limits; thousands of changing addresses make this unsuitable.
Adding Spot capacity does not filter attack traffic, and interruptions make it unsuitable as the primary availability protection.
The function execution role governs what the function can do after invocation; it does not grant EventBridge permission to invoke it.
The Lambda service principal in the execution role does not authorize EventBridge to invoke the function.
Granting lambda:* gives more permissions than the required lambda:InvokeFunction action.
EventBridge invokes Lambda through a resource-based function permission for events.amazonaws.com and lambda:InvokeFunction. Scope the permission to the specific rule ARN for least privilege.
SSE-C requires the application to supply and manage the encryption key; it does not provide the requested managed rotation and KMS key-use auditing.
SSE-S3 does not expose a customer-managed KMS key whose usage can be audited and whose annual rotation can be configured.
Manual key rotation adds operational work when automatic annual rotation meets the requirement.
SSE-KMS provides encryption at rest and CloudTrail audit events for KMS usage. A customer managed symmetric KMS key supports automatic annual rotation.
Athena queries data in S3 for analysis; it is not the REST endpoint and transactional backend for storing and retrieving bicycle locations.

API Gateway exposes a REST API and Lambda implements reads and writes to the location data store. Kinesis analytics processes streams but is not a REST-accessible record store; add the required persistent data store to the implementation.
QuickSight and Redshift provide analytics and visualization, not the required location-management REST API.
Kinesis stream analytics processes event streams; it does not provide the requested REST storage and retrieval workflow.
RDS event notifications do not trigger Lambda for individual table-row updates, and one shared queue distributes messages rather than delivering every event to every consumer.
A single FIFO queue still distributes messages among consumers; it does not fan out each sale to all target systems.
RDS events describe database-instance operations, not individual sales, and placing SNS after a shared queue does not implement the proposed per-subscriber fan-out.

choices.solution: After an automobile sale is committed, have the application publish the sale event to an Amazon SNS topic. Fan out the topic to a separate SQS queue for each target system, and use Lambda consumers to update the targets.
choices.explanation: SNS fan-out with separate SQS queues gives each target an independent durable copy of the sale event. RDS service event notifications report database operational events, not row changes. Publish from the application after commit, preferably through a transactional outbox for reliable delivery.
Glacier Vault Lock applies retention policies to Glacier vaults; it is not an individually releasable, indefinite hold on S3 objects.
A fixed 100-year retention period is time-bound and does not model an indefinite legal hold that can be selectively released.
CloudTrail records access but does not prevent object modification or deletion.

A legal hold protects object versions indefinitely until an authorized user removes it. Removing a hold requires s3:PutObjectLegalHold, and permanent deletion also requires the relevant object-version deletion permission.
Glacier archival storage requires retrieval before normal processing and is unsuitable for immediately resizing uploaded images.
Routing uploads through the web servers preserves the upload bottleneck instead of offloading transfers to S3.
Presigned URLs let browsers upload original images directly to S3, removing upload traffic from the web servers.
S3 object-created notifications invoke Lambda to resize images asynchronously, removing image processing from the upload request.
Scheduled processing delays resizing and does not react immediately to each uploaded image.
Self-managed brokers and database instances require the team to configure replication, failover, and maintenance.
Keeping MySQL on EC2 retains the operational burden of database availability and failover.
Two fixed consumer instances do not provide the automatic replacement and capacity management supplied by an Auto Scaling group.
Amazon MQ active/standby ActiveMQ brokers, a Multi-AZ consumer Auto Scaling group, and RDS MySQL Multi-AZ remove the single-instance dependencies while keeping infrastructure managed.
ECS on Fargate runs the existing containers without host administration. ECS Service Auto Scaling adjusts tasks and the ALB distributes incoming requests.
A fixed pair of EC2 instances requires server management and does not automatically scale the container workload as demand grows.
Migrating containers to Lambda requires adapting the application to the function execution model.
An HPC configuration adds unnecessary infrastructure for ordinary application containers.
DataSync transfers data over a network connection; the available bandwidth cannot move this dataset quickly enough.
Snowcone has much less capacity than this 50-TB dataset and would require multiple devices and transfers.

Shipping the bulk data avoids the exhausted network connection. Glue supplies managed transformation after import. Snowball Edge is now restricted to eligible existing customers; a new customer needs another physical-transfer option.
Running custom transformations on EC2 requires managing processing infrastructure; Glue provides the managed transformation workflow.

114.question: A company has created an image analysis application in which users can upload photos and add photo frames to their images. The users upload images and metadata to indicate which photo frames they want to add to their images. The application uses a single Amazon EC2 instance and Amazon DynamoDB to store the metadata. The application is becoming more popular, and the number of users is increasing. The company expects the number of concurrent users to vary significantly depending on the time of day and day of week. The company must ensure that the application can scale to meet the needs of the growing user base. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.explanation: DynamoDB items have a 400-KB size limit, making it unsuitable for storing arbitrary photo files directly.
Firehose delivers streaming records to destinations; it does not replace the required image-processing application and photo storage.
S3 is durable object storage for images, DynamoDB stores metadata, and Lambda scales image processing without maintaining application instances.
A fixed EC2 fleet still requires server management and scaling, while attached EBS volumes do not provide a shared object store for the frames.
A NAT gateway provides internet egress; it does not create a private VPC endpoint route to S3.
Security groups control allowed traffic but do not change the network path to S3 into a private endpoint connection.
Private instances use an S3 VPC endpoint for S3 traffic without internet routing. A gateway endpoint is sufficient for same-Region access from the VPC.
Direct Connect is a connection from an external network to AWS and is unnecessary for private access from EC2 in the same AWS environment.

116.question: A company uses a popular content management system (CMS) for its corporate website. However, the required patching and maintenance are burdensome. The company is redesigning its website and wants a new solution. The website will be updated four times a year and does not need to have any dynamic content available. The solution must provide high scalability and enhanced security. Which combination of changes will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

choices.explanation: CloudFront provides HTTPS delivery for the static website. S3 website endpoints themselves support only HTTP.
AWS WAF filters HTTP requests; it does not provide the website's HTTPS endpoint and certificate termination.
Lambda adds application execution infrastructure that a static S3-hosted site does not need.
S3 static website hosting serves HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and images without server patching or instance management.
EC2 instances require patching and server maintenance for a website that can be served directly from S3 and CloudFront.
A custom Lambda integration requires implementing and maintaining delivery logic instead of using the supported CloudWatch Logs subscription integration.
Firehose does not automatically read a CloudWatch log group; a subscription must forward the records to it.
Retrofitting agents and configuring a separate streaming pipeline adds operational work compared with a log-group subscription.
EBS requires provisioned volumes and attached compute, making it a poor fit for a scalable 900-TB text-object repository.
EFS adds shared-file-system capabilities and cost that simple text-object storage does not require.
OpenSearch maintains search indexes and compute capacity; that is unnecessary expense when the requirement is storage.
S3 scales object storage independently of the application instances and stores a large document repository without provisioning file-system or block-volume capacity.
Configuring WAF separately in every account and Region requires more administration than centrally applying policies through Firewall Manager.
Firewall Manager centrally applies WAF policies across organization accounts and Regions. WAF filters SQL injection and cross-site scripting against the Regional API stages.

choices.solution: Set up AWS Shield in both Regions. Associate Regional web ACLs with an API stage.
choices.explanation: Shield provides DDoS protection; it does not replace WAF web ACLs for application-layer request filtering.
Shield alone does not centrally deploy and enforce the required WAF rules across accounts and Regions.
CloudFront serves HTTP and HTTPS content; it cannot proxy DNS traffic to the DNS servers.
CloudFront cannot accelerate the UDP and TCP DNS protocol used by these servers.
An Application Load Balancer handles HTTP-family traffic, not DNS over UDP or TCP; CloudFront does not resolve that limitation.
Encryption cannot be enabled in place on an unencrypted RDS instance. Copy its snapshot with encryption enabled and restore a replacement instance; subsequent snapshots inherit encryption.
RDS does not let you enable encryption in place by attaching an encrypted EBS volume; restoring an encrypted snapshot creates the replacement database.
An RDS snapshot cannot be restored over an existing DB instance; it must create a new instance.
Encrypting an exported copy in S3 does not encrypt the running RDS database or its future automated snapshots.
MFA strengthens authentication but does not provide scalable encryption-key creation, storage, and lifecycle management.
KMS manages encryption-key storage, permissions, and cryptographic operations without a custom key-management server fleet.
ACM manages TLS certificates; it is not a general-purpose service for application data-encryption keys.
An IAM policy controls access but does not supply the managed key infrastructure and cryptographic operations.
Changing the certificate on each instance leaves TLS encryption and decryption on the already overloaded web servers.
Storing a certificate in S3 does not perform TLS termination or offload cryptographic processing from EC2.
A self-managed proxy adds another server to maintain and a potential bottleneck instead of using managed ALB TLS termination.
An ALB HTTPS listener uses the imported ACM certificate to terminate TLS, moving handshake and encryption overhead away from the application instances.
Spot Instances reduce cost for stateless jobs that tolerate interruption. Save checkpoints or retry work so an interruption does not prevent completion.
Reserved Instances require a commitment to capacity usage; interruptible batch processing can use cheaper spare Spot capacity.
On-Demand pricing is higher than Spot pricing for a workload that can safely tolerate interruptions.
A single Lambda invocation is limited to 15 minutes, shorter than this job's roughly hour-long execution.
Private application instances behind the load balancer and a Multi-AZ RDS deployment provide application and database availability.
An internal ALB cannot accept public customer traffic, and NAT gateways providing internet egress must be deployed in public subnets.
Placing the application instances in public subnets does not meet the requested private web-tier placement.
An Application Load Balancer requires subnets in at least two Availability Zones; a single public and single private subnet also cannot support the proposed two-AZ NAT design.
An internet-facing ALB uses public subnets in two Availability Zones. A NAT gateway in each zone gives private application instances resilient outbound access to the payment service.
Deep Archive requires a restore before access, so immediately archiving objects violates immediate retrieval during the first two years.
Keep the recent two years in an immediately retrievable storage class and transition older objects to Deep Archive for lower long-term storage cost.
Access-based archival can move infrequently accessed recent objects out of immediate retrieval before they are two years old.
One Zone-IA stores data in one Availability Zone and does not meet the requested highly available storage for recent data.
EBS uses network-attached storage; local instance store is the intended choice for the highest temporary video-processing I/O performance in this scenario.
This selects network-attached EBS for temporary processing and pays for EFS file-system features when durable object storage is sufficient.
EFS adds file-system cost for media objects, while S3 Standard is more expensive than archival storage for the unused archive.

Local instance-store storage suits high-I/O temporary video processing; select instances with at least the required local capacity. Use S3 for durable media and S3 Glacier storage classes for archives. Instance-store data is ephemeral, so durable inputs and outputs must be stored elsewhere.
An EC2 Auto Scaling group alone does not manage container scheduling and orchestration; those operations remain the company's responsibility.
An EKS managed node group manages Kubernetes worker lifecycle; Spot reduces cost for stateless, interruption-tolerant workloads. Use diverse instance types and handle interruptions.
On-Demand instances cost more than Spot for disruption-tolerant containers and still require the company to operate the container platform.
Managed nodes reduce operational work, but On-Demand pricing misses the Spot savings available for this interruption-tolerant workload.
Aurora PostgreSQL provides a managed PostgreSQL-compatible database with replication and failover, reducing database administration.
Moving the containers onto EC2 retains server maintenance and capacity-planning responsibilities.
CloudFront can improve content delivery but does not remove the container-host or database administration burden.
ElastiCache can reduce database reads but introduces another component and does not manage the existing servers or database.
ECS on Fargate runs and scales the existing Linux containers without managing EC2 hosts.

130.question: An application runs on Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. The application performs best when the CPU utilization of the EC2 instances is at or near 40%. What should a solutions architect do to maintain the desired performance across all instances in the group?

choices.explanation: Simple scaling requires manually configured alarms and adjustment sizes; it does not automatically maintain a specified average CPU target.
A target tracking policy scales the EC2 group to maintain the specified CPU target, rather than using fixed capacity or a schedule for changing demand.
Custom Lambda capacity logic adds implementation and maintenance work when target tracking already maintains a 40% CPU target.
Scheduled scaling follows a timetable rather than responding to actual CPU utilization.
A policy must identify an authenticated CloudFront origin access mechanism; simply referring to CloudFront access without that identity is insufficient.
CloudFront does not use an arbitrary IAM user's credentials to authenticate S3 origin requests.
A CloudFront distribution ID is not a valid IAM Principal. OAI uses its identity; modern OAC uses the CloudFront service principal and a SourceArn condition.
An OAI authorizes CloudFront to read a private S3 REST origin while direct anonymous S3 requests remain denied. Origin access control is the recommended modern approach for new distributions.
S3 stores the downloadable reports and CloudFront caches them near users globally, reducing origin load and latency without maintaining web servers.
Lambda and DynamoDB add execution and database components rather than caching downloadable report objects near global users.
EC2 Auto Scaling and an ALB require running compute and do not provide CloudFront's global edge caching for static reports.
Internal ALBs are not publicly accessible, and DNS routing does not cache reports at global edge locations.
EC2 provides OS access but requires the company to manage Oracle installation, upgrades, replication, and recovery.
Standard RDS for Oracle does not provide the OS-level access required for the upgrade customization.
RDS Custom for Oracle allows supported operating-system and database customization. A cross-Region replica provides a recovery option with less administration than self-managed EC2 replication.
A Multi-AZ deployment does not grant OS access to standard RDS for Oracle.

134.question: A company wants to move its application to a serverless solution. The serverless solution needs to analyze existing and new data by using SQL. The company stores the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The data requires encryption and must be replicated to a different AWS Region. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Create a new S3 bucket. Load the data into the new S3 bucket. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to replicate encrypted objects to an S3 bucket in another Region. Use server-side encryption with AWS KMS multi-Region keys (SSE-KMS). Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
choices.explanation: Athena queries data in S3 without database servers. Configure S3 replication permissions and destination encryption for SSE-KMS objects; existing objects need Batch Replication or a deliberate initial load. S3 treats multi-Region KMS keys as regional keys rather than automatically reusing ciphertext.
RDS requires loading the S3 dataset into a database and does not provide Athena's serverless SQL queries directly over S3 objects.
SSE-S3 does encrypt the objects, but enabling replication on an existing bucket does not replicate its pre-existing objects; this proposal lacks a backfill such as S3 Batch Replication.
RDS is not the proposed serverless S3 query engine, and enabling replication alone does not backfill objects already present in the bucket.

135.question: A company runs workloads on AWS. The company needs to connect to a service from an external provider. The service is hosted in the provider's VPC. According to the company's security team, the connectivity must be private and must be restricted to the target service. The connection must be initiated only from the company's VPC. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.explanation: VPC peering connects networks rather than exposing only the specific provider service through a consumer-initiated endpoint.
A virtual private gateway supports VPN connectivity; it does not expose a narrowly scoped PrivateLink service.
A NAT gateway provides outbound connectivity, not private access to a provider's VPC endpoint service.
choices.solution: Create a NAT gateway in a public subnet of the company's VPC. Update the route table to connect to the target service.
Ask the provider to create a VPC endpoint service for the target service. Create an interface VPC endpoint in the company's VPC and use AWS PrivateLink to connect to the service.
choices.explanation: The provider publishes an endpoint service, and the consumer creates an interface endpoint. PrivateLink exposes only the designated service without opening general VPC-to-VPC connectivity.
A full-load and ongoing change-data-capture task keeps Aurora synchronized while the source database remains online.
A backup is a point-in-time copy and does not keep the target synchronized with subsequent source changes.
A DMS replication instance connects to the source and target and performs the migration task.
Schema Conversion Tool converts database structures and code; it does not continuously replicate changing table data.
EventBridge routes events but does not implement database change-data capture and replication.
Sending root-account notifications to all users exposes sensitive account communications beyond the administrators who need them.
