Using one person's address risks missed notifications when that administrator is unavailable or leaves the company.
AWS accounts require distinct root email addresses; reusing the same root email cannot establish the proposed separate accounts.

138.question: A company runs its ecommerce application on AWS. Every new order is published as a message in a RabbitMQ queue that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance in a single Availability Zone. These messages are processed by a different application that runs on a separate EC2 instance. This application stores the details in a PostgreSQL database on another EC2 instance. All the EC2 instances are in the same Availability Zone. The company needs to redesign its architecture to provide the highest availability with the least operational overhead. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.explanation: RabbitMQ on Amazon MQ uses a multi-AZ cluster deployment rather than ActiveMQ's active/standby model, and a DB Auto Scaling group does not configure database replication.

choices.solution: Migrate the RabbitMQ queue to an Amazon MQ cluster deployment across three Availability Zones. Create a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for the application. Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with Multi-AZ enabled.
choices.explanation: Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ uses a three-node Multi-AZ cluster for high availability, rather than the active/standby pair used for ActiveMQ. Multi-AZ application instances and RDS remove the remaining single-zone dependencies.
Auto Scaling EC2 brokers does not itself configure RabbitMQ clustering, replicated queues, or broker failover.
Auto Scaling groups do not automatically configure the stateful replication and failover required by RabbitMQ and PostgreSQL.
Custom copy code adds maintenance, and S3 event notifications cannot directly invoke SageMaker as a notification destination.
Maintaining a Lambda function to copy objects adds operational work that managed S3 replication avoids.
SageMaker is not a direct S3 event-notification destination; the proposed direct trigger cannot be configured.
Spot capacity reduces costs for the interruption-tolerant ingestion layer; jobs must handle interruption and retries.
On-Demand EC2 pricing misses the Spot discounts suitable for the sporadic, interruption-tolerant work.
Compute Savings Plans cover predictable eligible EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage under an hourly spending commitment.
Reserved Instances commit to EC2 usage that the sporadic workload cannot reliably sustain and do not cover Fargate or Lambda.
EC2 Instance Savings Plans cover EC2 usage in a particular instance family and Region, not the predictable Fargate and Lambda usage.

CloudFront delivers static and dynamic HTTPS content through nearby edge locations and optimized origin connections. Use the ALB as the origin and configure cache policies so personalized responses are not shared between users.
Regional DNS routing selects an origin but does not cache content or provide CloudFront's edge-to-origin acceleration.
Bypassing CloudFront for dynamic requests gives up its edge connection handling and optimized path to the origin.
Geolocation DNS routing does not provide global content caching or the same request acceleration as CloudFront.
An ALB does not support UDP, and Lambda does not provide control of a custom Linux kernel.
CloudFront does not proxy arbitrary UDP traffic, and Lambda cannot host the required modified operating system.
Global Accelerator supports UDP, static entry IPs, and regional failover. NLB distributes UDP traffic to EC2 instances that can run the modified Linux kernel.
API Gateway and an ALB do not expose the application's arbitrary UDP protocol.
Reworking the services into Lambda functions changes the execution model and requires more application changes than packaging services in containers.
Amplify and Lambda require adapting the application to their hosting and function models rather than running the existing services as containers.
Separate EC2 fleets require additional server management compared with a managed container platform.
ECS manages independently deployable container services, and ALB listener rules route requests to their target groups. Use Fargate if avoiding host management is required.

144.question: A company recently started using Amazon Aurora as the data store for its global ecommerce application. When large reports are run, developers report that the ecommerce application is performing poorly. After reviewing metrics in Amazon CloudWatch, a solutions architect finds that the ReadIOPS and CPUUtilization metrics are spiking when monthly reports run. What is the MOST cost-effective solution?

choices.explanation: Redshift requires a separate warehouse and data-loading workflow when an Aurora reader can run the existing report queries directly.
An Aurora Replica serves the reporting queries separately from the writer, reducing CPU and read load on the instance processing ecommerce transactions.
Increasing the writer's capacity costs more and leaves reporting CPU and read work competing with production transactions.
Aurora storage does not expose the proposed instance-level provisioned-IOPS adjustment, and extra storage IOPS would not isolate reporting CPU usage.
Weighted DNS routes clients according to cached DNS responses rather than balancing each web request or reacting immediately to unhealthy web servers.
Stopping and resizing the existing instance introduces downtime and does not provide horizontal scaling or separate the database tier.
A launch template does not run a Spot Fleet as proposed; the answer does not specify a valid Auto Scaling configuration for the web tier.
An entirely Spot-based fleet can lose the steady production baseline during interruptions.

Reservations discount steady baseline usage and Spot lowers the cost of additional stateless capacity. Maintain sufficient reliable baseline capacity and handle Spot interruptions to preserve availability.
Paying On-Demand prices for predictable baseline usage forfeits the savings available through a reservation.
Dedicated Instances incur a tenancy premium that this workload does not require.
AWS Backup retention settings do not perform lifecycle transitions of the live S3 log objects into archive storage.
Keep recent logs in S3 for troubleshooting and transition older logs to Deep Archive for lower long-term storage cost when restore delays are acceptable.
AWS Backup is not a backup and archival mechanism for CloudWatch Logs log groups.
S3 Lifecycle policies apply to S3 objects, not to CloudWatch Logs log groups.
Lambda already uses multiple Availability Zones; adding an availability configuration does not retain events whose processing ultimately fails.
More memory does not guarantee successful network calls or retain events after retry attempts are exhausted.
SNS delivery retries address delivery to Lambda, not execution failures after Lambda has accepted the event.

An SQS on-failure destination retains failed asynchronous Lambda invocation records after retries are exhausted. A replay consumer can retry them later; it must understand the destination record's envelope.
SQS FIFO preserves order within a message group and integrates with Lambda for managed processing. Configure message groups and idempotent processing to match the required ordering.
Standard SNS delivery does not guarantee processing in the original message order.
SQS Standard provides best-effort ordering and can deliver messages out of order.
Combining standard SNS and SQS does not add the ordering guarantee supplied by a FIFO queue.

A CloudWatch composite alarm combines child alarm states with a Boolean rule, allowing notification only when CPU and memory conditions occur together. Memory metrics require an agent or custom publishing.
A dashboard displays metrics but does not enforce the required condition that both alarms be in the alarm state.
Synthetics tests application behavior; it does not combine CPU and storage alarms into the specified condition.
Multiple thresholds on one metric do not combine the independent CPU and IOPS conditions.
Control Tower preventive controls can restrict allowed Regions and prohibit internet connectivity in governed accounts. Exempt global services where the Region restriction requires it.
WAF filters web requests, not VPC internet-gateway creation, and account settings do not provide the proposed blanket Region-denial control.
Organizations SCPs can deny internet-gateway operations and regional actions outside the approved Region across member accounts.
Administrators could change network ACLs, and per-user IAM policies do not centrally constrain every principal and account.
Config detects violations after resources are created; alerting does not prevent administrators from making the forbidden changes.
Session Manager manages interactive access to instances; its trust policy does not create a schedule for starting and stopping RDS.
An extra Redis cluster adds cost and does not provide a general replacement for the relational database while it is stopped.
The cron job starts and stops the EC2 instance, not the RDS database whose costs must be reduced.
EventBridge schedules Lambda calls to stop and start the RDS instance during predictable idle periods. Stopped instances still incur storage charges and restart automatically after seven days.
Initially using Standard-IA incurs retrieval charges during the first 90 days when downloads are frequent.
Intelligent-Tiering adds per-object monitoring charges, and its automatic access tiers do not use a configurable 90-day object-age transition to Standard-IA.

choices.solution: Configure S3 inventory to manage objects and move them to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 90 days.
choices.explanation: S3 Inventory produces object listings; it does not transition storage classes without additional processing.

choices.solution: Implement an S3 Lifecycle policy that moves the objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 90 days.
choices.explanation: A lifecycle transition after 90 days reduces storage cost for rarely accessed older files while Standard serves the frequently accessed recent files.
Privileged users can bypass governance retention, and a legal hold has no automatic one-year expiration.

Object Lock compliance retention prevents permanent deletion or alteration of protected versions for the configured year, including by administrators. Restrict write permissions separately if users must not create additional versions.
IAM permissions can be changed by administrators and do not enforce immutable, time-bound retention against every user.
Detecting changed hashes happens after modification and does not prevent deletion or enforce a retention period.
DataSync transfers datasets between storage locations; it does not provide an edge cache for global viewers.
Global Accelerator does not cache media and cannot use an S3 bucket directly as its endpoint.
CloudFront caches S3 content at edge locations close to viewers, providing global delivery with reduced origin traffic.
SQS queues messages; it does not serve or cache media content for users.
Athena queries the staged S3 data on demand, and QuickSight presents the results as dashboards without a dedicated warehouse.
Kinesis analytics processes streams; Athena is the query service for one-time SQL analysis of the staged S3 dataset.
Custom per-record Lambda ingestion and a Redshift cluster add maintenance and do not implement the requested S3 staging workflow.
Multiple OpenSearch clusters add managed-compute and indexing overhead and do not stage the consolidated dataset in S3.
Lake Formation blueprints generate Glue workflows to ingest database data into S3. Glue processes and catalogs data in Parquet format for efficient analytics.
A manual snapshot alone has no automatic five-year deletion policy and does not retain ongoing database audit logs.
Aurora automated backup retention cannot be extended to five years with the proposed lifecycle policy.
Aurora automated backups have a maximum retention period of 35 days, not five years.
Enable database audit logging and export the PostgreSQL logs to CloudWatch Logs. Set the log group retention to never expire; exporting logs alone does not enable auditing.
AWS Backup schedules Aurora backups and applies a five-year retention policy. Automated Aurora backup retention alone is limited to 35 days.

CloudFront is the CDN in these choices and can accelerate both live HTTP-based streaming and video-on-demand for a global audience. Global Accelerator improves network paths to regional endpoints but is not a CDN/cache for this use case.
Global Accelerator routes traffic but does not provide the edge caching and HTTP video distribution needed for both live and on-demand content.
Route 53 resolves and routes DNS queries; it does not deliver or cache video segments.
S3 Transfer Acceleration optimizes transfers to and from S3 rather than providing a video content-distribution cache.
API keys identify usage-plan consumers but are not an authentication or authorization mechanism.
Filtering inside Lambda allows malicious requests to consume API and function capacity before rejection.
IAM authorization and per-user roles authenticate API callers and enforce permissions before the Lambda integration runs.
A private API requires private network connectivity; changing DNS does not make it accessible to legitimate public users.
A WAF web ACL on the REST API stage blocks matching malicious requests and can rate-limit bot traffic before it reaches Lambda.
OpenSearch adds indexing and compute costs that are unnecessary for storing a small backup dataset.
Glacier archival tiers require retrieval before normal access and do not provide immediate millisecond reads.

S3 Standard is durable, low-cost object storage with millisecond access. Glacier does not meet the millisecond-access requirement, while OpenSearch and RDS are unnecessarily expensive for a 300 MB backup.
An RDS instance incurs database compute and administration costs when only JSON object backup storage is needed.
An EC2 fleet needs server maintenance and capacity management, increasing overhead relative to event-driven Lambda.
S3 events trigger managed Lambda document processing and Aurora stores results in a managed relational database. Size and configure the Lambda workload within its execution limits.
EBS Multi-Attach requires coordinated concurrent access and remains AZ-scoped; managing EC2 workers adds overhead.
The ECS EC2 launch type requires maintaining worker instances instead of using serverless execution for these small event-driven jobs.
FSx for Lustre supplies high-performance shared storage and can import and export data through linked S3 storage for persistent inputs and outputs.
FSx for Windows uses SMB and does not provide the Lustre parallel file system and S3-linked HPC workflow required here.
Glacier is archival storage requiring restoration, and EBS is not a shared parallel file system for hundreds of workers.
A VPC endpoint supplies connectivity, not a shared HPC file system; a gp2 EBS volume cannot supply the proposed distributed access.
ECR stores the container images, and ECS on Fargate runs them without host management. A Multi-AZ service and target tracking adjust capacity as demand changes.
The ECS EC2 launch type requires managing container-host instances and their capacity, increasing overhead relative to Fargate.
A self-hosted image repository and manually launched workers create infrastructure maintenance and scaling work.
Packaging containers into an AMI does not supply managed container scheduling and still requires maintaining EC2 hosts.
A self-managed Redis server requires implementing durable queuing, retries, failure isolation, and server availability.
Kinesis requires stream-consumer checkpoint and failure-handling logic; SQS directly supplies task queuing and a dead-letter queue.

SQS buffers messages durably and a dead-letter queue isolates repeated failures. Set message retention longer than the two-day backlog. A single SQS visibility timeout is limited to 12 hours, so a two-day uninterrupted processing task needs checkpoints or a different orchestration design.
SNS pushes notifications rather than providing a durable work queue that isolates failed messages for later processing.
WAF is not the identity making S3 requests, so its ARN cannot serve as the proposed authenticated S3 principal.
WAF must be associated with the distribution; forwarding alone also leaves direct S3 access available unless the origin is restricted.
S3 buckets do not have security groups, and allowing CloudFront IP ranges would not identify this particular distribution.
WAF inspects requests at CloudFront, while a private S3 REST origin accessible only through CloudFront prevents direct S3 access from bypassing inspection. OAC is preferred for new distributions.
Presigned URLs authorize downloads but do not cache reports near a worldwide audience.
Replicating to every Region adds storage and administration costs without providing CloudFront's edge cache.
Geoproximity DNS routing does not cache the HTML files or reduce origin requests by itself.
CloudFront caches popular images from the S3 origin at global edge locations, reducing latency and repeated origin requests.
Spot interruptions can remove all processing capacity, violating the continuous-processing requirement.
Reserving peak capacity wastes money during intermittent low-volume periods.
Reserved capacity serves the reliable baseline and Spot workers process additional durable SQS backlog at lower cost. Consumers must handle interruptions and redelivery.
On-Demand burst capacity costs more than interruption-tolerant Spot workers while the reserved baseline maintains continuous processing.
Network ACLs filter subnet traffic, not AWS service API actions across accounts.
Security groups control network connections and cannot be attached to IAM groups to constrain API permissions.
Separate cross-account roles do not impose a centrally maintained permission boundary on every principal in the organization.
An Organizations SCP sets centrally managed maximum permissions across member accounts. It does not grant permissions, and it does not restrict the management account.
Inspector scans workloads for vulnerabilities; an ALB cannot run the proposed Inspector agent.
Macie discovers sensitive data in S3 rather than blocking DDoS traffic.
Shield Advanced provides enhanced DDoS protection for eligible ALB resources and access to additional detection and response capabilities.
GuardDuty detects security threats but does not itself mitigate DDoS attacks against an ALB.
Security groups accept IP and port rules, not country-based geographic match conditions.
An ALB security group has no geographic-country matching capability.
A WAF geo-match rule on the ALB can allow the permitted country and block other source-IP geolocations. IP geolocation is not proof of a user's citizenship or physical location.
Network ACLs match addresses and ports, not a requester's country; maintaining national IP lists would also add considerable work.
One EC2 instance has fixed capacity and lacks automatic scaling for seasonal demand.
API Gateway exposes the REST API and Lambda scales the tax calculation code with demand, reducing idle server costs outside seasonal peaks.
A fixed pair of instances does not elastically add processing capacity as inquiries increase.
API Gateway scales the API front end, but the single EC2 computation backend remains a capacity bottleneck.
Signed URLs control who may request content; they do not encrypt sensitive fields through the application stack.
Signed cookies authorize content access but do not restrict decryption of individual submitted fields.
HTTPS protects transport connections, but data is decrypted at connection termination and is then readable by intermediaries without field-level encryption.
Global Accelerator does not cache images and videos or use the S3 bucket as a direct endpoint.
CloudFront caches media at nearby edge locations and serves repeated requests without repeatedly retrieving the same objects from the S3 origin.
Redis adds a regional application cache requiring integration; it does not directly supply a worldwide S3 media distribution network.
Memcached requires an application-managed cache and does not provide global edge delivery of S3 objects.
An Auto Scaling group and ALB are regional resources; a single group cannot span two Regions.
An Auto Scaling group spanning two Availability Zones retains application capacity if one zone becomes unavailable. The load balancer distributes traffic to healthy instances.
A launch template is a recovery recipe, not running capacity that can immediately survive an Availability Zone failure.
Changing load-balancing behavior does not protect servers that all reside in the same failing Availability Zone.
Provisioned concurrency can increase simultaneous database connections, and a global database does not pool connections to the writer.
RDS Proxy pools and reuses database connections, reducing connection churn from concurrent Lambda invocations. It does not increase the database's underlying query-processing capacity.
Order writes cannot be routed to a read replica, and an API query parameter does not implement database connection pooling.
Migrating to DynamoDB changes the data model and application significantly instead of addressing connection pressure with a proxy endpoint.
A DynamoDB gateway endpoint routes table calls privately without NAT or internet egress. IAM and endpoint policies still control authorization.
A NAT gateway uses the service's public endpoint and adds unnecessary internet-egress infrastructure instead of a private endpoint route.
A NAT instance must have internet connectivity in a public subnet; placing it in a private subnet cannot provide the proposed egress.
Private IPv4 instances cannot reach public endpoints directly through an internet gateway without public addressing or NAT.
Redis requires application-specific cache lookup, population, and invalidation logic rather than DynamoDB-compatible DAX access.

DAX supplies an API-compatible cache for eventually consistent DynamoDB reads, reducing read latency and table load. Strongly consistent reads bypass the cache, and applications need a DAX-compatible client.
Global tables improve geographic availability but do not cache repeated reads to reduce their latency.
Memcached requires explicit application cache integration; Auto Discovery discovers nodes, not DynamoDB records.
AWS Backup can centrally back up both EC2/EBS and RDS resources and copy recovery points across Regions. That is less operational work than managing separate snapshot and replication mechanisms.
DLM manages EBS snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs, not RDS backups.
Managing separate AMI copies and a continuously running database replica adds operations and cost compared with centralized backup copies.
Exported RDS snapshot data in S3 is not a directly restorable RDS snapshot, and the separate copy workflows add overhead.

Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance that permits reading the SecureString parameter and decrypting it with the KMS key. IAM policies are attached to identities/roles, not directly to an EC2 instance.
An IAM policy cannot be attached directly to an EC2 instance; an instance profile containing an IAM role supplies credentials.
A parameter is not a principal that can establish a trust relationship, and the RDS service principal does not grant the EC2 application parameter access.
Trust between the database and EC2 does not grant permission to read the secure parameter or decrypt its KMS ciphertext.
WAF cannot be associated directly with a Network Load Balancer.
Shield Advanced protects eligible NLB resources against sophisticated network and transport layer DDoS attacks.
WAF on the API Gateway REST API stage filters application-layer exploits such as SQL injection.
GuardDuty detects threats, and Shield Standard lacks the advanced DDoS protection and response capabilities requested.
Shield Standard does not replace WAF SQL-injection filtering or Shield Advanced protection for sophisticated DDoS attacks.
SQS decouples producers from consumers and durably holds work when a consumer is slow or unavailable. Consumers acknowledge successfully processed messages by deleting them.
SNS supplies push notifications and fan-out, not a pull-based work backlog that consumers can process at their own rate.
A custom forwarding Lambda function adds coupling and does not supply a durable queue for scaling independent workers.
Using a database and its change stream as a task queue adds data and checkpoint management that SQS already provides.
The proposed synchronous replication to all three nodes is not how an RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster works; its writer commits with acknowledgment from at least one reader.
An RDS MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance synchronously replicates to a standby in another Availability Zone and provides managed failover.
Cross-Region RDS read replicas replicate asynchronously and can lose recent transactions during a failure.
An EC2-triggered Lambda function does not implement MySQL synchronous commit replication and adds a self-managed database.
S3 and CloudFront serve static content, API Gateway and Lambda implement the dynamic API, and DynamoDB on-demand handles changing request rates without provisioned-capacity administration.
Aurora Auto Scaling scales reader instances, not the writer's read/write capacity in the manner provided by DynamoDB on-demand.
EC2 requires server maintenance, and fixed provisioned write capacity does not immediately adapt to changing demand.
EC2 adds server patching, while Aurora reader Auto Scaling does not elastically scale the writer's transaction capacity.
A Lambda function must be configured for VPC access so its ENIs can use the VPC routing to the virtual private gateway and existing Direct Connect path. No additional VPN or public IP is required.
Another VPN does not attach the Lambda function to the private network; the existing Direct Connect route can be used once Lambda is VPC-connected.
Changing VPC routes cannot give a function outside the VPC access to its private routing domain.
An Elastic IP cannot be assigned directly to a Lambda function; private connectivity requires VPC network interfaces and routing.
S3 has no generic ECS role that automatically grants container credentials; the application needs a task role assigned in its task definition.
The ECS task role, configured as taskRoleArn, gives the code in the container its S3 permissions. The execution role is used by ECS to start and manage the task.
Security groups control network traffic, not authorization for S3 API calls.
Logging in as an IAM user does not supply persistent, automatically rotated credentials to ECS tasks; a task role does.
Volume Gateway exposes iSCSI block volumes, not a managed shared Windows SMB file system.
EFS uses NFS and is not the native shared Windows SMB file service required here.
An ordinary EBS volume cannot be shared across Availability Zones, and concurrent block-volume access is not a managed Windows file share.
RDS Multi-AZ provides a managed standby and automatic database failover.
Read replicas primarily scale reads and use asynchronous replication; Multi-AZ provides the managed writer failover required here.
A self-managed Docker cluster requires maintaining its hosts, orchestration, and capacity.
An ECS service on Fargate runs containers without host maintenance; use tasks in multiple Availability Zones and service scaling for availability.
The ECS EC2 launch type retains host maintenance and capacity management that Fargate removes.
S3 File Gateway exposes NFS and SMB shares, not an SFTP server endpoint.
A single EC2 SFTP server and scheduled upload script require maintenance and lack the managed high availability of Transfer Family.
A load-balanced EC2 SFTP fleet still requires managing servers and copy scripts instead of writing directly through the managed SFTP service.
Authorized users can bypass governance-mode retention; compliance mode prevents that during the retention period.
Object Lock compliance retention prevents permanent deletion or alteration of protected versions for the required retention period, including by the root user.
SSE-S3 manages keys internally and does not expose a configurable annual rotation schedule for a customer-managed key.
SSE-KMS with a customer managed symmetric key and automatic annual rotation encrypts documents at rest while retaining older key material for decryption.
Imported KMS key material requires its own material-management workflow rather than the simple automatic rotation of an AWS-generated symmetric key.
Converting an existing Java/PHP application into static hosting plus Lambda requires application restructuring and does not preserve its existing runtime deployment.
Directly managing EC2 runtimes, scaling, and load balancing adds operations that Elastic Beanstalk manages.
Containerizing and operating an EC2 container fleet adds deployment and infrastructure work compared with Beanstalk's managed environments and URL swapping.
Move reporting reads to an RDS read replica so analytical queries no longer compete with order-processing traffic on the primary database.
A read replica cannot handle order writes; reporting should move off the writer rather than distributing writable application operations to a read-only endpoint.
Moving to DynamoDB requires a data-model and application rewrite rather than isolating reporting reads.
Moving reports to off-hours prevents employees from performing the required business-hours queries.
Self-managed MySQL on EC2 adds database operations and scaling work compared with S3 and serverless Athena queries.
Store the extracted structured medical data in S3 and query it with Athena.
A custom EC2 document-processing application requires maintaining both extraction logic and server capacity.
Transcribe Medical transcribes audio, not extracted document text; Textract and Comprehend Medical supply the intended document workflow.
S3 events invoke Lambda; Textract extracts document text and Comprehend Medical identifies medical entities and protected health information.
Read replicas distribute reads but still execute database queries; a cache avoids repeated database reads.
ElastiCache for Redis can cache frequently read database data and supports replication/Multi-AZ high availability. Memcached does not provide the same HA capabilities.
DNS caching caches name resolution, not application query results.
Memcached does not provide Redis-style replication and automatic failover for a highly available cache.

Two database EC2 instances in different Availability Zones with database-level replication and clustering provide redundancy and automatic failover. A single instance with recovery or AMI-based replacement is not highly available.
Rebuilding one instance from an AMI requires recovery time and can lose changes made since the backup; it is not live clustered failover.
Replication across Regions alone does not specify automatic failover or the clustered coordination included in the multi-AZ solution.
EC2 automatic recovery addresses supported underlying-host failures; it does not provide database replication or protection against an Availability Zone failure.
Auto Scaling replaces compute, but the proposed event rule does not durably retain unprocessed orders for retry.
An ALB forwards requests but does not retain them when every worker is unavailable.
SQS provides durable buffering between order submission and EC2 workers. If workers fail, messages remain available for retry, preventing users from having to resubmit orders.
SNS-to-Lambda-to-Run Command adds orchestration without giving the EC2 processors a durable, independently consumable order backlog.
Recreating the infrastructure every month risks deleting required recent data and incurs unnecessary deployment work.
A monitoring instance and custom deletion script add cost and maintenance for functionality supplied by DynamoDB TTL.
Deleting old items on every stream event requires custom querying and deletion logic; native TTL expires items without that worker.

DynamoDB TTL is purpose-built for automatic expiry. Store an expiration timestamp on each item and configure that attribute as the table TTL to remove data older than 30 days with minimal operational effort.
Rewriting the application as Lambda functions requires development changes that a Windows rehost avoids.
A load-balanced, Multi-AZ Elastic Beanstalk environment runs the existing .NET application with managed deployment and scaling.
An existing Windows Server .NET application cannot be assumed to run unchanged on Amazon Linux.
DynamoDB uses a different data model from Oracle and would require application and schema changes.
DMS migrates the Oracle data to RDS for Oracle; a Multi-AZ RDS deployment provides managed database failover.
ECS changes the Kubernetes deployment method, and MongoDB on EC2 requires operating database servers.
ECS changes deployment methods and DynamoDB requires database API and data-model changes.
EKS preserves Kubernetes, but DynamoDB is not a MongoDB-compatible replacement and requires application changes.

EKS preserves the Kubernetes deployment model, Fargate removes worker-node management, and DocumentDB provides MongoDB-compatible APIs. This combination minimizes code, deployment, and infrastructure changes.
Rekognition analyzes images and video, not the audio-to-text speaker diarization required for call transcripts.
Amazon Transcribe provides speaker diarization and transcription. Athena can query transcript files stored in S3, where lifecycle/retention policies can satisfy the seven-year retention requirement.
Translate translates text between languages; it does not transcribe audio or identify speakers.
Rekognition is not a call transcription service, and Textract extracts text from documents rather than querying transcript datasets.
A Lambda authorizer requires maintaining custom token-validation code that the built-in Cognito user-pool authorizer avoids.
API keys are not user authentication, and custom Lambda validation adds unnecessary development work.
An email header is caller-controlled and does not prove identity; custom validation duplicates managed Cognito authorization.
API Gateway has a managed Amazon Cognito user-pool authorizer. It validates Cognito tokens without custom Lambda authorization logic, minimizing operational overhead.
A contact flow alone does not implement the proposed two-way SMS campaign and year-long response archive.
SQS is a message queue, not an SMS delivery and reply service.
An SNS FIFO topic does not support SMS subscribers, and Kinesis Data Streams is not a direct SNS subscription endpoint.
SSE-S3 does not expose a configurable yearly key-rotation schedule, so its managed rotation cannot demonstrate this specific requirement.
Manual rotation violates the automatic-rotation requirement and adds operational work.
Imported key material does not support the proposed automatic rotation; client-side encryption also adds key-handling work.
DAX accelerates repeated DynamoDB reads, not the invitation worker's ability to drain the queue.
Adding an API front end does not increase the downstream invitation-processing capacity.
Caching the request-collection front end does not reduce the backlog of invitation jobs.
Moving all purchase data into RDS creates migration and database-capacity work rather than a centrally governed analytics data lake.
Custom copying and bucket policies require more implementation work and do not provide Lake Formation's centralized fine-grained data permissions.
A warehouse and custom copy jobs add compute and ingestion management compared with the managed data-lake integration.
A Lightsail server needs web-server maintenance and is a single hosting instance rather than resilient managed object storage.
An EC2 fleet and ALB incur ongoing compute and management costs for infrequently updated static files.
A public bucket permits origin access outside CloudFront, and an always-available SFTP service adds unnecessary cost for infrequent updates.
Polling and parsing CloudTrail logs requires custom code and scheduling instead of a direct EventBridge event pattern.
Notifications for delivered log files and Athena queries add processing stages and latency before identifying the specific API operation.
CloudTrail cannot use a FIFO queue as the proposed direct log target, and custom log parsing adds unnecessary maintenance.
Throttling rejects requests and impacts users instead of durably buffering accepted requests for later processing.
DAX is a read cache; it is not a durable write buffer that absorbs excess DynamoDB write demand.
A secondary index does not increase the base table's write capacity and can add further write consumption.

SQS buffers incoming requests so temporary DynamoDB write-capacity pressure does not lose requests. Lambda can drain the queue at a sustainable rate. DAX is primarily a read cache and API Gateway throttling would reject requests rather than preserve them.

An S3 interface endpoint provides private IP connectivity, and the bucket policy limits access to the instance role. A gateway endpoint is also valid with route tables, but it has no security groups and is not scoped to one Availability Zone as the other choice claims.

Gateway endpoints do not have security groups; their access is controlled with endpoint policies and routing. A correctly configured gateway endpoint could otherwise meet the private-access requirement.
Ordinary DNS lookup does not return a private endpoint for a bucket unless private endpoint infrastructure is already configured.
ip-ranges.json lists public AWS address ranges, not a bucket-specific private endpoint address.
Sticky sessions keep clients on one instance but do not share session data or preserve it when that instance is terminated.
Systems Manager Session Manager supplies administrative shell access, not web-user session storage.
STS GetSessionToken returns temporary AWS credentials; it does not store distributed application session state.
Sizing both fleets for peak demand wastes capacity and does not durably buffer work during worker replacement.
Creating extra Auto Scaling groups does not provide a durable order backlog or appropriately scale the existing independent worker tiers.
SQS does not directly send the proposed scaling notifications; a CloudWatch metric and scaling policy are needed to relate queue backlog to worker capacity.
SQS durably buffers orders and decouples collection from fulfillment. Scale each consumer Auto Scaling group on backlog per instance to match available workers to its queue.
CloudTrail records API activity rather than providing a current cross-Region inventory filtered by resource tags.
Querying every service and Region requires more implementation work than Tag Editor's cross-Region tag search.
Logs Insights queries log records, not a complete inventory of tagged resources across services.
Glacier Instant Retrieval has retrieval charges and a 90-day minimum duration, making rapidly changing access patterns less economical than automatic access tiering.
Standard provides immediate access but continues charging the frequent-access storage rate when objects become infrequently accessed.

S3 Object Lambda allows you to add custom code to process and transform data as it is requested by applications, without having to modify the original data stored in S3. By using S3 Object Lambda, you can process and remove the personally identifiable information (PII) on-the-fly before returning the data to the applications. This approach minimizes operational overhead because you don't need to create separate storage (buckets or tables) for each application, and you can apply the PII removal logic dynamically as the data is requested. Availability limitation: S3 Object Lambda is unavailable to new customers starting November 7, 2025; existing customers can continue to use it.

HDD storage does not provide the sub-millisecond latency of the required SSD-based parallel filesystem.
