Spot interruptions are unsuitable as the sole capacity for an uninterrupted legacy workload, and S3 is not a drop-in relational database.
On-Demand database pricing misses reservation savings for a database used continuously.
On-Demand application pricing misses reservation savings for the continuously running application tier.
An offline device requires delivery and return logistics, holds less than this dataset, and does not provide bandwidth-controlled online migration.
FSx File Gateway provides cached access to an existing FSx share, not a bandwidth-controlled bulk migration service.
Transfer Family supplies SFTP/FTP transfer endpoints rather than optimized SMB-to-FSx migration with DataSync's bandwidth controls.
CloudFront caches and delivers video through nearby edge locations, reducing origin load and download latency.
Regional replication duplicates raw videos but does not transcode them or provide global edge caching.

choices.solution: Use AWS Elemental MediaConvert to convert video files into appropriate encodings and adaptive streaming formats.
choices.explanation: MediaConvert creates device-appropriate video encodings and streaming renditions. Elastic Transcoder is a retired service.
Operating Local Zone web servers adds infrastructure management instead of managed CloudFront delivery.
A self-managed transcoding fleet requires maintaining servers and encoding software that MediaConvert manages.
EC2 Auto Scaling manages instances, not the number of Fargate service tasks.
A custom Lambda scaling controller duplicates functionality provided by Application Auto Scaling.
EC2 simple scaling policies cannot directly control Fargate task capacity.
Repeated device shipment adds logistics and delay for periodic transfers between online AWS filesystems.
An EC2 SFTP server requires maintenance and custom transfer scheduling.
DMS migrates databases, not arbitrary NFS filesystem contents.
DataSync transfers files; it does not expose a mountable SMB filesystem.
A Windows server on EC2 requires patching, management, and availability configuration.
S3 exposes object APIs rather than a native SMB share that the clients can mount.
Cross-AZ traffic introduces transfer charges and latency, and partition placement optimizes fault isolation rather than tightly coupled network performance.
Scaling across AZs incurs inter-AZ transfer charges and does not establish the low-latency cluster placement.
Step scaling across AZs changes capacity but adds cross-AZ data transfer rather than minimizing charges.
File Gateway presents NFS or SMB, not the required iSCSI block volumes.
Tape Gateway supplies a virtual tape library, not online iSCSI primary storage.
Stored volumes keep the full dataset locally rather than only recently accessed data.
The selected reservation analysis should use consolidated billing to account for pooled usage and reservation benefits, rather than examining one account in isolation.
Use the payer account to obtain organization-wide RDS reservation purchase recommendations based on consolidated usage.
The RDS reservation purchase recommendation check identifies potential savings for sustained On-Demand database usage; an idle-instance check addresses a different issue.
Idle-instance recommendations target little-used databases, not the active high-performance instances described.
Redshift Reserved Node Optimization applies to Redshift, not RDS for Oracle.
The basic S3 console overview does not supply the aggregated advanced activity analysis of Storage Lens.
BucketSizeBytes measures stored capacity rather than object access frequency; querying it cannot reveal unused buckets.
CloudTrail object events and custom log analysis add configuration and cost compared with the built-in Storage Lens activity dashboard.
Transfer Acceleration adds acceleration charges and does not cache repeated dataset downloads to reduce origin transfers.
Cross-Region replication adds storage and replication charges without edge caching repeated downloads.
Proxying large datasets through EC2 adds application bandwidth and compute load instead of economical edge delivery.
Kinesis requires consumer checkpoint and stream management when SQS supplies durable task queues directly.
Separate push topics and functions do not provide the existing backend servers with durable pull-based quote queues.

An SNS topic fans out requests to durable SQS queues. Subscription filters route each quote type to its appropriate queue, and independent consumers process requests without maintaining stream shards.
Firehose and OpenSearch add indexing and query management for work that should be routed into task queues.
Custom snapshot code must manage scheduling and copies and does not automatically preserve the instance configuration.
Backing up only the EBS volumes omits the complete EC2 instance configuration needed for efficient restoration.
EBS snapshots are regional resources; copying within another AZ does not provide recovery in another Region.
A public bucket bypasses authorization, and KMS encryption keys are not a scalable viewer-access mechanism.
Per-device IPsec connectivity adds user setup and network management instead of ordinary authorized HTTPS streaming.
Client VPN adds client configuration and infrastructure costs that signed CloudFront access avoids.
Provisioned Aurora requires selecting and managing DB instance capacity.
Redshift Spectrum queries analytical data in S3 and is not a MySQL transactional database replacement.
Provisioned RDS for MySQL requires choosing and resizing DB instance classes.
Shield mitigates DDoS attacks; it does not scan installed software for vulnerabilities.
Macie discovers sensitive S3 data, not EC2 software vulnerabilities.
GuardDuty detects malicious activity; Inspector performs the requested package vulnerability scanning.

Inspector scans EC2 software inventory for vulnerabilities and produces findings. Current scanning uses SSM-managed agents or eligible EBS snapshot-based agentless scanning; it does not require the old Inspector Classic agent.
choices.solution: Enable Amazon Inspector EC2 vulnerability scanning. Configure supported agent-based scanning with Systems Manager or eligible agentless scanning, and use Lambda to generate and distribute findings reports.

choices.explanation: A larger instance increases fixed operating cost and still requires server management.
Stopping the only consumer prevents message processing, and a separate restart mechanism would still be needed.
Run Command still requires EC2 capacity and custom scheduling instead of managed SQS-triggered execution.
A scheduled Glue ETL job transforms the CSV inputs and loads Redshift without maintaining a custom processing server.
Running custom EC2 scripts adds server maintenance, and SQL script files are not a substitute for loading queryable data into Redshift.
The COTS application supports Redshift and S3, not DynamoDB.
Scheduling and maintaining an EMR cluster adds infrastructure work compared with a managed Glue ETL job.
CloudTrail records AWS API activity for auditing, including who made an API call and when.
Data lifecycle policies manage retention of backups, not API auditing and resource configuration history.
Trusted Advisor recommendations are not a complete audit trail of who changed resource configurations.
Config records supported resource configurations and evaluates rules to detect noncompliance and configuration changes.
Restoring a template changes resources but does not record the inventory and configuration history for auditing.
STS generates temporary AWS credentials, not one-time SSH keys.
Shared keys on bastion hosts still violate the requirement to remove all shared keys.
A Cognito authorizer and custom key-generation function add unnecessary credential and access-management code.

choices.solution: Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to query the data.
choices.explanation: Kinesis Data Streams durably ingests the data, and Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink provides managed stream processing. Use Firehose where the design requires delivery to S3. The former Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL service was discontinued in January 2026.
Firehose buffers and loads data into Redshift, adding latency compared with directly analyzing the live stream.
Instance store loses buffered data on instance lifecycle events and therefore preserves the data-loss problem.
Redis Pub/Sub does not retain messages for disconnected consumers, and EBS staging adds a custom ingestion pipeline.
The ACL header controls permissions, not object encryption.
A private ACL does not select or enforce encryption.
SecureTransport controls HTTPS transport rather than encryption of the stored object.

To enforce server-side encryption on uploads, the bucket policy can deny PutObject requests that do not include the x-amz-server-side-encryption header (or otherwise fail the required encryption condition). ACL and SecureTransport conditions do not enforce encryption at rest.
Generating the thumbnail before sending the confirmation keeps the user waiting for processing to finish.
The proposed completion notification occurs after thumbnail generation, not immediately after receipt.
Notifying only after thumbnail generation does not meet the requested early upload acknowledgment.
A single EC2 endpoint is a failure point and requires server availability management.

API Gateway provides a managed HTTPS endpoint, Lambda processes each badge event without maintaining servers, and DynamoDB stores the results durably across Availability Zones for subsequent analysis.
DNS routing cannot directly invoke a Lambda function as an HTTPS service endpoint.
Writing directly to S3 through a private endpoint does not supply the required message-processing logic.
Changing applications to NFS adds changes, and a 10-TB cache cannot keep the full hundreds-of-terabytes dataset immediately local.
Tape backup requires a backup-software workflow and restores rather than supplying the existing primary volume's transparent snapshot integration.
A 10-TB cache keeps only part of the dataset locally; uncached reads introduce cloud retrieval latency.
An ACL does not exchange Cognito tokens for IAM credentials and risks granting access more broadly than the intended users.
S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency; redeployment does not resolve missing IAM permissions.
Attribute mappings alone do not grant S3 access; the assumed IAM role must carry the required bucket permissions.
Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves eligible objects between access tiers as access changes, avoiding manual access-pattern predictions.
A lifecycle AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload rule removes unused multipart parts that otherwise continue to incur storage charges.
Delete-marker cleanup helps versioned deletion bookkeeping, not the storage charged for incomplete multipart uploads.
Standard-IA has retrieval charges and does not automatically adapt to each object's inconsistent future access pattern.
One Zone-IA reduces AZ resilience, contrary to the requirement for highly resilient core assets.

Route internet egress through Network Firewall and enforce an allowlist of approved domains with stateful domain rules. Route both traffic directions consistently through the firewall and use NAT where needed.
WAF protects inbound HTTP requests to supported front ends; it is not a VPC-wide outbound domain filter.
Security-group rules accept IP ranges, prefix lists, and security groups, not arbitrary repository URLs.
An ALB routes inbound HTTP requests to targets and is not an outbound internet filtering proxy.
Adding a fixed number of instances does not retain orders if a sudden burst exceeds processing capacity.

Caching static content and scaling EC2 improves throughput, but does not durably buffer sales requests while a sudden surge exceeds available processing capacity. An SQS backlog preserves requests until workers can process them.

ElastiCache is not a transparent cache that can be placed in front of an ALB. Unique sales requests also require processing rather than cached responses, so this does not preserve requests during overload.

SQS durably buffers sales requests during the sudden surge so EC2 workers can process them asynchronously; CloudFront caches the static content. Workers should process orders idempotently and delete messages only after successful processing.
Macie discovers sensitive S3 data, not EC2 vulnerabilities, and per-instance cron jobs add management overhead.
GuardDuty is not the vulnerability scanner, and Session Manager does not schedule patch installation.
Detective investigates security findings rather than scanning packages; an EventBridge schedule alone does not perform patch management.
Inspector detects EC2 software vulnerabilities; Systems Manager Patch Manager applies updates on a schedule. Scanning and patching are separate functions.
Secrets Manager stores secrets but does not provide the KMS key integration used by RDS storage encryption.
TLS encrypts database network connections, not stored database pages and backups.
An IAM certificate does not configure RDS storage encryption; TLS addresses data in transit only.

AWS Snowball is a physical data transport solution that helps customers transfer large amounts of data into and out of AWS. It addresses challenges associated with large-scale data transfers, particularly when network constraints, transfer times, or security concerns make online data transfer less practical. Historical-service limitation: Snowball Edge is available only to eligible existing customers since November 7, 2025; new customers need a current physical-transfer or online-transfer alternative.
The usable bandwidth is only 10.5 Mbps, insufficient to transfer 20 TB within 30 days regardless of transfer optimization.
A VPN cannot increase the usable 10.5-Mbps capacity and adds protocol overhead.
Transfer Acceleration cannot overcome the local bandwidth limit required to meet the deadline.
A public file server increases exposure and requires server management; IP filtering alone does not preserve AD-based file authorization or secure remote connectivity.
A signed URL is a transferable bearer credential, and a private endpoint also requires a network path for remote employees; this does not preserve Windows AD file-share access.
There is no public VPC endpoint of the proposed type, and IAM Identity Center login alone does not authorize arbitrary S3 downloads.
CloudFront does not offload the application's internal month-end calculation batch.
Reactive CPU scaling begins after the predictable spike has already disrupted the application.
A cache does not necessarily remove this calculation workload and does not proactively add the known monthly capacity.
DMS migrates databases; it does not present an AD-authenticated SFTP interface to S3.
DataSync runs managed transfers rather than exposing the unchanged client's SFTP download endpoint.
A self-managed SFTP server requires maintenance, and IAM integration alone does not preserve the customer's AD authentication.
Registering a snapshot as an AMI does not eliminate lazy loading of the resulting EBS volumes.
Automating AMI lifecycle management does not pre-initialize volumes restored from snapshots.
Backup lifecycle and scaling-limit events do not enable fast snapshot restore or otherwise remove volume initialization latency.
Parameter Store requires custom password-rotation code and scheduling compared with Secrets Manager's rotation integration.
An EFS credential file adds filesystem access management and custom rotation/synchronization work.
An S3 credential file requires custom refresh and rotation logic and risks stale downloaded credentials.
Adding a cache and replacing stored procedures with Lambda require more application changes and do not directly improve replica replication.
Self-managed MySQL replication on EC2 increases database maintenance and does not inherently provide Aurora's low-lag shared-storage architecture.
DynamoDB changes the data model and stored-procedure execution and cannot combine provisioned RCUs with on-demand mode as proposed.
Binary-log replication adds overhead compared with Aurora global database's storage-level replication.

An Aurora global database continues storage-level replication to a headless secondary cluster after its DB instance is removed. This avoids secondary compute charges and is the least-cost replication option here. Recovery requires creating secondary compute before promotion.
DMS needs a reachable database instance in the target cluster; removing all target compute prevents it from applying changes.

Keeping a DB instance in the secondary Region adds compute charges when the requirement asks only for the least-cost replicated DR copy and specifies no immediate recovery-time target. A headless secondary keeps receiving storage replication.
KMS rotates encryption-key material, not database passwords, and is not a database-credential storage service.
Writing a custom rotation function adds work when Secrets Manager supplies the RDS rotation workflow and scheduling.
Parameter Store has no native database-password rotation schedule; implementing it requires additional automation.
ALB listener rules do not implement SQL-injection payload inspection as a WAF managed rule does.
Shield Advanced is DDoS protection; it does not automatically block every SQL-injection attempt.
Inspector reports vulnerabilities rather than filtering incoming SQL-injection requests.
An EMR ingestion pipeline adds infrastructure and does not provide centralized column-level permissions for the lake.
IAM policies control AWS resource access, not individual columns within the lake's tables.
An S3 bucket policy cannot authorize individual table columns inside object contents.

A Lake Formation blueprint ingests Aurora data into the S3 lake using Glue. Lake Formation enforces column permissions when QuickSight queries through Athena; S3 bucket policies cannot restrict individual table columns.
Dynamic scaling responds after utilization rises and cannot pre-launch the predicted capacity 30 minutes early.
Scheduled scaling automates timing but still requires operators to determine the changing desired capacity.
Custom Lambda scaling is reactive and adds code without forecasting the capacity required before the batch starts.
Operating replicated MySQL instances on EC2 requires managing replication, patching, and recovery.
Multi-AZ replicas remain in one Region and do not provide the required multi-Region DR design.
Aurora Global Database provides cross-Region replication with typically low lag and supports managed promotion of a secondary cluster during regional recovery.
Backup copying protects data but requires restoring and provisioning database compute during recovery rather than managed ongoing replication.

The SQS Extended Client Library stores large message payloads in S3 and sends an S3 reference through SQS, supporting the required 50 MB payloads with limited application changes. The application's 256 KB limit in the question is not the current SQS service payload quota.
EventBridge does not support a 50-MB event payload as proposed.
The SQS native payload quota cannot be raised to 50 MB; the extended client stores the payload in S3 and queues a reference.
An EFS pointer workflow requires custom producer/consumer code and shared filesystem access rather than the supported extended SQS client.
Managed Microsoft AD adds directory capacity costs for a small user base, and a regional ALB does not provide global edge delivery.
S3 Transfer Acceleration optimizes object transfers rather than serving the application with a global authorization and content-cache layer.
AD and Elastic Beanstalk add running infrastructure and do not provide the fully serverless global serving architecture requested.
Volume Gateway exposes iSCSI block storage rather than the clients' existing NFS and SMB shares backed by S3 objects.
Tape Gateway presents a virtual tape library, not a live NAS filesystem interface.
FSx File Gateway caches an FSx filesystem rather than migrating the repository into S3 with S3 Lifecycle policies.
EC2 Instance Savings Plans bind the discount to a selected family and Region, so a later family change loses that flexibility.
Zonal reservations constrain capacity to a specific AZ and instance configuration rather than permitting the planned family changes.
Standard reservations do not provide Compute Savings Plans' flexibility across instance families.
Standard-IA increases per-request charges and targets storage-heavy, infrequently accessed tables, which is not established for this constant analysis workload.
On-demand capacity does not use configured RCUs and WCUs as proposed; predictable traffic is more economical with provisioned capacity.
Reserved capacity applies to provisioned mode, not on-demand billing.
An encrypted Aurora snapshot cannot be copied into an unencrypted snapshot, and sharing plaintext would defeat secure sharing.
AWS managed KMS keys cannot have their policy edited for this cross-account sharing, and adding an account to an alias does not grant key use.
RDS snapshots cannot be downloaded and uploaded as ordinary restorable snapshot files through S3.
A Multi-AZ DB instance deployment provides a synchronous standby and automatic failover; the standby does not serve reporting queries.
A restored snapshot is a point-in-time separate database and does not provide automatic synchronized failover.
A separate read replica offloads reporting queries from the writer and can reside in another Availability Zone.
RDS Custom changes the management model but does not by itself isolate reporting reads or configure automatic failover.
RDS Proxy pools connections; it does not schedule SQL reports into maintenance windows or remove their database read load.
Glue is a data-integration service, not the general workflow state machine for coordinating application steps.
Keeping the application on EC2 retains host management rather than adopting serverless execution.
Scheduled EventBridge invocations do not themselves maintain workflow state, sequencing, retries, and branching.
Transit gateways connect private networks but do not provide the global edge entry points and user-path optimization of Global Accelerator.
CloudFront does not support arbitrary UDP traffic; there is no UDP enablement option.
VPC peering connects private VPC networks rather than accelerating internet users into the nearest healthy regional game endpoint.
Provisioned io2 storage is unnecessary expense for this IOPS target; a 1-TB gp2 volume provides a 3,000-IOPS baseline.
RDS MySQL Multi-AZ provides a standby and failover while General Purpose SSD avoids the cost of unnecessary provisioned IOPS. Validate that baseline storage performance meets the workload.
S3 object storage cannot replace the MySQL database's writable block storage and relational engine.
Self-managed EC2 database clustering retains maintenance and failover work, violating the fully managed requirement.
Reducing concurrency can throttle legitimate requests rather than efficiently sharing database connections.
A larger instance increases ongoing cost without pooling the burst of short-lived Lambda connections.
DynamoDB requires changing the data model and application instead of adding a proxy to the existing database.
Lambda is limited to 15 minutes and much less compute and memory per invocation; splitting this legacy job requires redesign.
A Fargate task cannot provide the stated 64-vCPU and 512-GiB configuration for the unchanged CPU-intensive job.
Lightsail lacks the required large batch-compute configuration and managed batch scheduling.
Deep Archive requires restoration before reads, violating immediate accessibility.
One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ and reduces resilience compared with Standard.
One Zone-IA reduces AZ resilience and incurs retrieval costs even during the initial frequent-access period.
S3 stores static files durably and CloudFront caches them near users.
ElastiCache is a regional application cache, not an edge content-delivery network.
EFS is an NFS service and is not the native shared Windows SMB filesystem required here.
FSx for Windows File Server provides a shared SMB file system for server-side files used by multiple Windows instances.
A gp2 EBS volume is not a concurrently shared multi-instance Windows filesystem.
A standalone EC2 image processor requires server scaling and maintenance.
An origin request policy controls forwarded request information; it does not execute image transformation code.
A response headers policy changes headers, not image dimensions or encoding.
An ACM certificate cannot be attached to the S3 service endpoint as proposed; enforce S3 HTTPS with a bucket-policy condition.
SSE-S3 keys are controlled by S3 and cannot be administered by the hospital's compliance team.
Macie discovers sensitive data but does not encrypt stored objects or give the team control of encryption keys.
An API key does not change the network route or provide private connectivity.
API Gateway uses interface endpoints; gateway endpoints are for S3 and DynamoDB.
Introducing a queue changes the synchronous API interaction and does not itself supply a private API endpoint.
RDS alone does not supply sub-millisecond cached reads, and a custom export script adds maintenance.
S3 is not a sub-millisecond operational database, and Deep Archive objects must be restored before Athena can query them.
DynamoDB without DAX does not supply the requested sub-millisecond read cache, and this option omits a historical SQL query engine.
A table partition key groups data but does not guarantee consumers receive events in their original sending order.
A Kinesis partition key based on payment ID places related records in the same shard, preserving their order; consumers must process each key in order.
Memcached is a cache rather than an ordered durable message stream.
A message attribute in an unspecified standard queue does not enforce FIFO ordering for a payment.
An SQS FIFO message group based on payment ID serializes related messages while allowing different payments to be processed in parallel.
EventBridge does not guarantee ordered delivery of events.
SNS standard topics do not guarantee ordering or deduplicated delivery.
One FIFO queue distributes work among consumers rather than broadcasting each event concurrently to all three services.
This does not enforce encrypted transport or explicitly select a customer-managed key whose policy the hospital controls.
SNS server-side encryption with a customer managed KMS key protects message data at rest and gives control over key use.
An AWS-managed/default key policy cannot be customized as proposed; choose a customer-managed KMS key for explicit principal restrictions.
SQS SSE-KMS protects queued message data at rest. A queue policy that denies aws:SecureTransport=false enforces TLS in transit.
An IAM allow policy alone does not establish the key's permitted principals and cannot override other key-policy grants; the selected design directly configures the KMS key policy.
Read replicas also replicate accidental changes and do not supply historical point-in-time restoration.
Manual snapshots recover only to their capture times, not arbitrary points five minutes before an incident.
A Multi-AZ standby replicates the accidental edit rather than preserving the earlier logical database state.
Caching and throttling control performance and request rates, not subscription entitlement.
WAF inspects request patterns; it does not natively verify a user's subscription record.
DynamoDB IAM permissions alone do not enforce the subscription check at this Cognito-authenticated application API.

Cognito verifies the user token and API Gateway enforces the required premium scope. Subscription state must govern which users receive that scope. API keys and usage plans can meter usage, but must not be used as the sole authentication or authorization mechanism.
choices.solution: Use a Cognito user-pool authorizer in API Gateway and require a premium-content OAuth scope that is issued only to users with an active subscription. Enforce subscription entitlement when issuing or refreshing tokens.

Configure an NLB in each of three AWS Regions with supported UDP relay targets inside its VPC. Have the relays forward traffic over private connections to the on-premises application servers. Register the NLBs with Global Accelerator and point a CNAME to the accelerator DNS name.
choices.explanation: Global Accelerator and Regional NLBs support UDP routing, but an NLB UDP target cannot be an on-premises IP outside its VPC. This imported answer is incomplete: use supported in-VPC UDP relay targets with private connectivity to the on-premises servers, or revise the architecture.
An Application Load Balancer does not support UDP traffic.
CloudFront cannot proxy this application's arbitrary UDP protocol even if NLBs are used as origins.
Neither CloudFront nor an ALB supports the required UDP application traffic.
IAM password complexity and expiration settings are an account-level policy, not individual per-user policies.
Third-party software adds unnecessary management when IAM provides the password policy directly.
Custom event automation is unnecessary and does not establish the account's ongoing password complexity and expiration requirements.
App Runner hosts request-driven services rather than acting as a scheduled one-hour batch-job engine.
Lambda's maximum invocation duration is 15 minutes, shorter than these one-hour tasks.
Duplicating the whole instance requires custom scheduling and task placement and does not supply Batch's job queue and resource management.
A NAT instance requires patching and capacity management instead of the requested managed service.
A NAT instance in a private subnet has no direct internet egress and still requires server maintenance.
A NAT gateway must be in a public subnet with internet-gateway routing to provide public internet egress.
A filesystem plugin adds custom encryption management instead of using native EBS encryption.
Encryption cannot be enabled in place on an existing unencrypted EBS volume; new encrypted volumes must be created.
Enable EBS encryption by default in the target Region and select the customer managed key before creating the managed node group.

choices.solution: Create the EKS cluster and managed node group. Grant the node group's Auto Scaling service-linked role the required permissions and grants for the customer managed KMS key.
choices.explanation: Authorize the managed node group's Auto Scaling service-linked role to use the KMS key, including grant creation. Attaching a KMS policy only to the EKS cluster role is insufficient for encrypted node volumes.
KMS key material is not exported into Kubernetes secrets; applications use KMS permissions and key identifiers.
Keeping large image binaries in Oracle adds database storage and compute cost that scalable S3 object storage avoids.
DynamoDB's 400-KB item limit is unsuitable for high-resolution images, and DAX does not fix that storage limit.
S3 separates images efficiently, but a provisioned Oracle database adds licensing and capacity costs for a simple key-to-object lookup.
Monitoring trillions of objects incurs Intelligent-Tiering per-object charges when the access timeline is already predictable.
Per-object monitoring adds cost, and Intelligent-Tiering's optional archive tiers can archive by inactivity before the required immediate-access year ends.
Immediate Standard-IA placement incurs retrieval charges during the first month of daily model-training reads.
Separate VPNs use internet paths with less predictable latency and do not directly connect the three VPCs to each other.
Virtual appliances add server maintenance and three separate internet VPN paths.
Three physical Direct Connect connections cost more than sharing one connection through a transit gateway.
Glue orchestrates data-integration jobs rather than general application tasks with human approval callbacks.
SQS provides queues but requires custom orchestration for state transitions, branching, retries, and approvals.
Custom functions and events require implementing workflow state and approval coordination that Step Functions supplies.
Memcached caches application data; it does not pool relational database connections.
Higher I/O capacity does not directly resolve connection exhaustion or efficiently reuse connections.
A Multi-AZ standby does not accept application connections as a second writer; it is for failover.
Scheduled polling is delayed and may miss information from an instance that has already terminated.

Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks can run custom audit work during launch or termination, but they pause the lifecycle transition until completion or timeout. Use EventBridge notifications when pausing is unacceptable.
User data runs at launch and does not provide a termination lifecycle hook.
An ordinary startup/shutdown script lacks the explicit Auto Scaling wait-and-complete lifecycle coordination needed to send reports before termination.
DNS does not provide per-flow UDP load balancing, and Aurora is a relational database rather than the requested non-relational store.
An Aurora global database targets cross-Region relational replication and does not automatically scale non-relational capacity.
An ALB cannot handle arbitrary UDP traffic.
Bypassing the API changes security and business logic and exposes the database to clients without addressing Lambda initialization.
An S3 query-result cache requires application changes and does not remove library-loading latency for uncached requests.
A larger database does not eliminate Lambda cold-start initialization.
Elastic resize is not EC2 instance scheduling, and provisioned RDS instances cannot be scaled to zero as proposed.
A partner solution may work but adds acquisition, configuration, and possible licensing cost compared with native scheduled Lambda automation.
An extra always-running EC2 scheduler adds server cost and maintenance.
DocumentDB changes the database interface and data model, requiring significant application-query changes.
The standby in a traditional RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment cannot serve reporting queries.
DynamoDB requires a different data model and queries and does not preserve the PostgreSQL reporting code.
Shield protects against DDoS rather than encrypting connections, and WAF cannot be directly associated with an NLB.
WAF filters requests but does not by itself configure TLS encryption for the application's traffic.
EBS encryption protects data at rest, not data traveling between clients and application tiers.
On-Demand Dedicated Hosts cost more than host reservations for predictable continuous usage.
Dedicated Instances do not provide the same host/socket/core visibility and placement control needed for this licensing model.
Dedicated Instances lack explicit host-level licensing control, and On-Demand pricing misses predictable-usage reservation savings.
S3 exposes object APIs rather than a POSIX filesystem, and Glacier archival access requires restoration.
S3 Standard-IA remains object storage rather than the shared POSIX filesystem required by the application.
One Zone EFS places data in one AZ and reduces resilience compared with the required regional filesystem.
Allowing HTTPS from every address admits sources beyond the load balancer and violates least privilege.
Network ACLs cannot reference a security group as a source, and the broad HTTPS rule does not restrict traffic to the load balancer.
Security-group references restrict HTTPS to traffic from the load balancer and MySQL to traffic from the web tier, instead of opening database ports to arbitrary hosts.
Network ACLs cannot use security-group references; security groups can identify the application tiers directly.
SNS distributes notifications; it does not cache query results.
A read replica executes the repeated queries again rather than caching identical datasets.
Firehose delivers streaming data; it does not cache database calls or query responses.
Root credentials grant unrestricted account access and violate least privilege.
PowerUserAccess grants far broader permissions than the particular stack deployment requires.
AdministratorAccess grants unrestricted permissions rather than narrowly scoped stack operations and a service role.

choices.solution: Grant the deployment engineer only the required CloudFormation stack actions and narrowly scoped iam:PassRole permission for the stack's service role.
choices.explanation: Give the deployment identity only the required CloudFormation stack actions and narrowly scoped iam:PassRole permission.

choices.solution: Create a CloudFormation service role with only the permissions needed for the stack's resources, and specify that role when launching the stack.
choices.explanation: Use a CloudFormation service role with only the permissions needed to create stack resources. CloudFormation assumes this role instead of requiring broad permissions on the deployment user.
The default network ACL already permits traffic, so an additional ACL rule does not fix the missing database security-group permission.
The VPC's local route already connects its subnets; no additional intra-VPC route is needed.
Splitting the tiers into separate VPCs adds complexity and does not remove the need for the database ingress rule.
An ELB does not horizontally replicate an RDS writer or turn copies into synchronized reporting databases.
Vertical scaling leaves reporting queries competing with production writes on the same instance.
A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance standby is for failover and cannot serve reporting queries.
Sticky sessions keep users on one instance but lose local session state if that instance terminates.
DynamoDB stores sessions centrally so requests can reach any application instance without losing session state.
A Cognito user pool manages identity tokens rather than arbitrary durable shopping-session state.
ElastiCache for Redis provides a shared low-latency session store; replication and Multi-AZ failover improve availability.
Application Manager manages application resources and operations, not per-customer session data.
RDS storage is managed and cannot be backed up through customer EBS snapshots; repeatedly snapshotting stateless workers also wastes resources.
Snapshotting every stateless instance adds unnecessary storage and scheduling compared with retaining the deployment AMIs.
Per-instance snapshots every two hours are redundant for stateless compute that can be recreated from its current AMI.
Public HTTPS access reaches the web tier, while a security-group reference permits MySQL access only from the web servers.
A static customer IP allowlist fails as globally distributed customers' addresses change.
Customer IP allowlists are unsuitable for dynamic addresses, and customers should not connect directly to the database.
Allowing MySQL from every IPv4 address exposes the database beyond the application tier.
Kinesis Video Streams transports media but does not itself transcribe speech or redact PII.
Textract extracts text from documents, not speech from audio recordings.
A contact flow is not the proposed batch-file transcription mechanism, and custom PII pattern scanning adds work compared with Transcribe redaction.
Magnetic storage provides lower performance and is unsuitable for this high-IOPS database.

Increasing provisioned gp3 IOPS can be a valid remedy under current RDS capabilities; the original single-answer key is ambiguous unless the needed latency or IOPS exceeds gp3's supported performance.
RDS manages its underlying storage layout; customers cannot split the database into two separately attached gp3 volumes as proposed.
GuardDuty detects suspicious activity but is not the authoritative API audit trail identifying the principal for this change.
Inspector reports workload vulnerabilities, not the user who changed a security-group rule.
Config records configuration history; CloudTrail directly records the API caller and change request.
Shield Advanced protects supported public-facing resources such as the accelerator and EC2 Elastic IPs, not arbitrary EC2 instance IDs as proposed.
WAF cannot be associated directly with Global Accelerator and does not inspect DNS UDP traffic.
WAF cannot be directly associated with EC2 instances and is not a DNS protocol DDoS filter.
The job can run for an hour, exceeding Lambda's 15-minute invocation limit.
Adding API Gateway does not extend Lambda's 15-minute execution limit.
An EventBridge schedule launches an ECS Fargate task without managing a scheduler or worker hosts. Fargate supports long-running container jobs beyond the Lambda execution timeout.
The EC2 launch type retains host capacity and maintenance work that a scheduled Fargate task avoids.
A 100-Mbps link transfers at most roughly 15 TB in two weeks before overhead, far below 600 TB.
A VPN does not increase the limited upload bandwidth enough to meet the deadline.

Transferring 600 TB of data over a 100 Mbps connection would take a very long time. AWS Snowball Edge devices allow for offline data transfer, and you can transfer the data to the devices at your location before shipping them to AWS. This way, you are not constrained by the upload speed during the 2-week period. Historical-service limitation: Snowball Edge is available only to eligible existing customers since November 7, 2025; new customers need a current physical-transfer or online-transfer alternative.
Provisioning a new 10-Gbps circuit adds substantial cost and lead time compared with an offline-device migration.
A long cache TTL neither rate-limits malicious requests nor reliably serves current stock prices.
Monitoring and alerting detect the flood but do not automatically block it.
Custom edge rate-limit code adds development and operational work compared with a managed WAF rate-based rule.
DynamoDB transactions do not directly publish notifications to the teams.
Publishing to four topics modifies and adds network work to the current application; a stream-triggered single-topic fan-out avoids that coupling.
Repeated table scans consume capacity and add polling delay; SQS also distributes messages rather than broadcasting each event to all teams.
A single AZ remains a common failure point, and EC2 recovery does not replicate database data or handle an AZ-wide outage.
A same-AZ read replica shares the AZ failure risk and asynchronous replication can lose recent writes; manual promotion adds recovery work.
EBS Multi-Attach works only within one Availability Zone and cannot supply the proposed shared cross-AZ volume.
Kinesis Data Streams retains data for 24 hours by default. Increase retention beyond the every-other-day consumer interval, with recovery margin, so records are not expired before consumption.
KPL optimizes producers but does not extend the default 24-hour retention that expires before the two-day consumer interval.
More shards improve throughput but do not prevent records aging out before consumption.
S3 Versioning cannot recover records that already expired in Kinesis before they reached S3.
The Lambda resource policy controls invocation of the function, not its outgoing S3 permissions.
Using a user's credentials embeds long-lived secrets instead of the execution role's temporary credentials.
Creating another user does not provide the function with automatically managed role credentials and increases credential-management work.
A longer timeout does not create a durable backlog or solve concurrent processing limits.
Replication copies documents but does not ensure failed processing requests are retried by workers.
Adding a second function requires custom routing and does not supply a durable, controlled processing queue.
ALB capacity is managed by AWS; the proposed policy does not scale the application instances.
An internet gateway has no user-configurable Auto Scaling capacity.
A single Auto Scaling group is regional, and a multi-Region deployment adds unnecessary complexity for this capacity requirement.
Target tracking adjusts application instance capacity to maintain the chosen utilization metric.
Scheduled scaling sets capacity to zero when the application is not needed and restores it before work resumes.
Denying outbound MySQL traffic from the web subnet prevents the required database connections.
A subnet-wide source permits other resources in the subnet instead of only the web servers.
The web-server security group permits inbound HTTPS on port 443 from the internet.
The database security group permits MySQL on port 3306 only from the web-server security group.
Security groups support allow rules only; explicit deny rules cannot be configured.
DataSync copies files but does not expose a managed mountable Lustre filesystem.
File Gateway supports NFS/SMB file shares, not the Lustre client protocol.
EFS uses NFS and cannot be configured as a Lustre server.
An NLB cannot use Lambda as its UDP processing target, and DNS failover is affected by cached resolutions.

choices.solution: Use AWS Global Accelerator with an NLB endpoint in each of two Regions. Run the processing application as an ECS service on Fargate and register the tasks in each NLB's UDP target group.

choices.explanation: An ALB does not support arbitrary UDP traffic.
An ALB cannot handle UDP, and DNS failover does not provide Global Accelerator's rapid endpoint rerouting.
RDS is a relational database, not a Windows file-share replacement.
Storage Gateway adds an appliance and cache layer rather than directly providing the managed multi-AZ Windows filesystem for the AWS servers.
EFS provides NFS rather than the Windows SMB filesystem expected by this IIS application.
An IAM role controls permissions; attaching it does not change an EBS volume's encryption state.
An Encrypt tag is metadata and does not activate storage encryption.
A KMS key policy controls use of that key; it does not force every new EBS volume to use encryption.
DynamoDB uses a different data model and APIs from MySQL and requires application changes.
Provisioned RDS capacity must be sized and paid for despite highly variable usage; Aurora Serverless adjusts compute capacity.
An EC2 Auto Scaling group does not safely implement MySQL database replication and scaling without custom management.
Detecting and remediating public access after a change leaves an exposure window instead of preventing the change.
Manual remediation is delayed and permits public exposure until someone responds.
RAM shares supported resources; it is not the proposed S3 public-access detection and enforcement service.
Dedicated email servers retain mail delivery, patching, and capacity-management work.
SNS email subscriptions are notification delivery, not a transactional and marketing email platform like SES.
An Auto Scaling email fleet still requires managing mail servers and deliverability instead of using managed SES.
A daily transfer waits until day-end rather than making new reports available in near-real time.

the business system already writes CSVs to a network share. S3 File Gateway exposes an SMB/NFS share, but files written there are asynchronously uploaded into S3, so the application can keep behaving like it is writing to a normal file share.
A custom DataSync automation application adds development and administration work.
A polling script and SFTP uploads add custom transfer maintenance compared with writing directly to a File Gateway share.
Analyzing and manually moving objects adds management work when Intelligent-Tiering adapts automatically.
A fixed archival-class choice incurs retrieval charges and does not adapt to unknown access patterns.
One Zone-IA reduces AZ resilience and does not adapt when frequently accessed data changes.
Redshift is an analytics warehouse and does not directly improve the transactional website's existing query path.
CloudFront caches static content at edge locations, reducing latency and web-server load.
S3 cannot execute the dynamic server-side web application.
An RDS read replica offloads read-only queries from the primary database; route eligible queries to it explicitly.
A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance standby improves availability but does not offload application reads.
EC2 Instance Savings Plans do not discount Lambda usage.
The plan excludes Lambda, and placing a Lambda interface in a public subnet does not itself give the function public internet access or lower latency.

Compute Savings Plans cover both eligible EC2 and Lambda usage. Configure Lambda VPC access to the private subnets so it can reach the EC2 instances directly; a public subnet does not give Lambda a public IP.
Keeping Lambda outside the customer VPC prevents direct access to the instances' private addresses.
AdministratorAccess grants far more permissions than the bucket-access and role-assumption requirements.
Disabling Block Public Access does not authenticate team members and risks exposing the bucket.
Duplicating IAM users creates another set of long-lived credentials instead of using the existing identities to assume a scoped role.

choices.solution: In each member account, enable EBS encryption by default in ap-southeast-2 and select a default KMS key.
choices.explanation: Enable EBS encryption by default in ap-southeast-2 in each member account and choose a default KMS key.
A permissions boundary attaches to an IAM user or role, not an Organizations OU, and does not constrain member-account root users.

choices.solution: Create an SCP. Attach the SCP to the root organizational unit (OU). Define the SCP to deny the ec2:CreateVolume action when the ec2:Encrypted condition equals false.
choices.explanation: An SCP denies unencrypted CreateVolume requests in member accounts. Add appropriate RunInstances protections where needed; an SCP does not affect the management account.
Per-identity IAM policies do not constrain root users and add maintenance across accounts and identities.
Default EBS encryption is configured per account and Region; enabling it in the management account does not enable it for member accounts.

420.question: A company wants to use an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB cluster to simplify time-consuming database administrative tasks for production database workloads. The company wants to ensure that its database is highly available and will provide automatic failover support in most scenarios in less than 40 seconds. The company wants to offload reads off of the primary instance and keep costs as low as possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.explanation: A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance can take longer to fail over and requires an extra read replica beyond its unreadable standby.
The cluster already includes two readable instances; creating two more replicas adds unnecessary capacity and cost.
The standby in a Multi-AZ DB instance pair cannot serve application reads.
Transfer Family does not use EBS as an SFTP backend, and its public endpoint does not expose the proposed security-group IP allowlist.
Transfer Family provides a managed SFTP endpoint with EFS storage. An internet-facing VPC-hosted endpoint uses Elastic IPs and security groups to limit clients to trusted source addresses.
A public Transfer Family endpoint does not support the proposed security-group source filtering, and S3 does not preserve POSIX user permissions like EFS.
An internal-only endpoint cannot accept the required trusted internet clients, and S3 does not preserve the existing filesystem permission model.
An NLB cannot invoke Lambda targets, and the direct endpoint lacks a durable batch-request buffer.
App Mesh handles service networking; it does not scale ECS capacity based on queue depth as proposed.
AWS Auto Scaling cannot dynamically adjust the vCPU allocation of Lambda functions based on SQS backlog; Lambda compute is tied to configured memory.
An identity-based IAM policy can be attached to a role and applies to sessions that assume it.
An identity-based IAM policy can be attached to an IAM group and supplies permissions to users in the group.
An organization is not an IAM identity to which this identity policy can be attached.
An ECS resource does not receive identity-based policies directly; use its task or execution role.
An EC2 instance receives role credentials through an instance profile rather than an identity policy attached directly to the instance.
Fargate requires containerization and does not supply the same EC2 Spot pricing for the existing short-lived backend nodes.
Spot can interrupt the continuously required front end, while reservations are inefficient for short-lived variable backend capacity.
Spot is unsuitable as the sole guaranteed front-end baseline, and Fargate requires changing the backend deployment.
gp2 performance scales with volume size rather than allowing independent IOPS provisioning.
io2 can provide the performance but has higher provisioned-IOPS costs than gp3 for this moderate IOPS requirement.
io1 adds provisioned-IOPS cost when gp3 meets the stated performance more economically.
Management events do not audit individual S3 object reads and writes, so this misses the required data-level access trail.
Transfer Acceleration can speed object uploads but lacks DataSync's managed dataset transfer, verification, and incremental synchronization workflow.
CloudTrail management events omit object-level data access, regardless of how the files reach S3.
Lambda does not provide the existing Tomcat application-server deployment model without restructuring the application.
ElastiCache is not a MySQL relational database replacement.
Duplicating an AMI containing MySQL does not configure replicated database state and adds self-managed application-server work.
Environment-variable user keys are long-lived credentials that require manual rotation and are exposed to principals allowed to read configuration.
Encrypted stored user keys still require credential retrieval and rotation instead of automatically managed execution-role credentials.
The role must trust Lambda to assume it; trusting DynamoDB does not allow Lambda to use it as an execution role.
IAM evaluates all applicable statements; an explicit deny overrides an allow regardless of statement order.
Only StopInstances and TerminateInstances have the MFA-related deny, not every EC2 action.
The allow applies only in us-east-1; satisfying MFA does not create permissions in other Regions.

The Allow statement permits EC2 actions only in us-east-1. The explicit Deny blocks StopInstances and TerminateInstances when MFA is absent or false. Therefore those two actions are allowed in us-east-1 only when MFA is present, while other EC2 actions remain allowed there.
Hourly polling delays images and requires maintaining a worker instead of reacting immediately to each upload.
S3 object-created notifications invoke Lambda to convert each uploaded CSV into an image without waiting for a polling schedule.
Use prefix or tag filters to archive the CSV files and expire images after 30 days. Glacier Flexible Retrieval is suitable when training and audits are planned ahead.
Lifecycle transitions into One Zone-IA require objects to be at least 30 days old, so the proposed one-day transition is invalid.
Standard-IA transitions require a 30-day object age, and retaining images in RRS misses the requested inexpensive expiration after one month.
Memcached lacks Redis sorted sets and persistent backup/restore capabilities for preserving the scoreboard.
An edge-cached page can be stale and does not maintain or restore live score state.
A read replica executes ranking queries and can lag; it does not provide Redis's low-latency sorted-set scoreboard and cache persistence.
Glue ML transforms target data preparation such as record matching, not the general model-development and BI integration requested.
A marketplace AMI requires managing training servers, while OpenSearch adds a separate visualization platform instead of native BI integration.
QuickSight calculated fields do not train arbitrary custom ML models as SageMaker does.
Config detects and reports changes after they occur rather than denying unauthorized tag modification.
CloudTrail records changes but does not prevent the API actions.
CloudWatch logs observe activity; they are not an authorization boundary preventing tag changes.

434.question: A company hosts its application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancer in an Auto Scaling group and with an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company wants to ensure the application can be made available in another AWS Region with minimal downtime. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of downtime?

choices.explanation: A secondary application fleet and DynamoDB global table keep both application capacity and data available in the recovery Region. DNS failover switches traffic; plan for the chosen global-table consistency mode.
Creating the entire environment during failure takes longer and does not continuously replicate the existing table data.
Replicated data helps, but launching compute only after failure increases downtime compared with pre-provisioned standby capacity.
A custom alarm/Lambda DNS update adds reaction steps and maintenance compared with configured Route 53 health-based failover.

This is a cost-effective solution for shipping large amounts of data to AWS. Snowball Edge devices are designed for efficient data transfer, and they can handle the 20 TB database. AWS DMS is a managed service for migrating databases to AWS, and AWS SCT can assist in converting the database schema. Using these tools in combination allows for a smooth migration process. Historical-service limitation: Snowball Edge is available only to eligible existing customers since November 7, 2025; new customers need a current physical-transfer or online-transfer alternative.
A Snowmobile is designed for vastly larger migrations and is disproportionate for a 20-TB database.
A GPU compute device adds unnecessary compute capability and cost when the requirement is bulk storage transfer.

choices.solution: Order a 1 Gbps dedicated AWS Direct Connect connection to establish a connection with the data center. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with replication of ongoing changes.
choices.explanation: Provisioning a new dedicated circuit adds lead time and ongoing cost for a one-time migration with a two-week deadline.
A Multi-AZ DB instance standby improves availability, not the writer's processing capacity.
A separate database adds infrastructure and does not transparently increase capacity of the existing writer.
Changing the purchasing model without increasing capacity does not accommodate the larger workload and misses reservation savings.
Inspector detects vulnerabilities; it does not rate-limit requests arriving at an ALB.
Static address-block rules require continuous updates as attacker IPs change and cannot inspect HTTP request rates.
GuardDuty detects threats but has no native rate-limiting protection setting.
A read replica remains associated with the company's environment rather than providing the auditor its own independently restored copy.
Text exports require reconstructing the database and create another IAM credential instead of scoped encrypted snapshot sharing.
An RDS snapshot cannot be copied into S3 as an ordinary restorable file, and sharing long-lived user keys is unnecessary.

Share a manual encrypted RDS snapshot and its customer managed KMS key with the auditor's account. The auditor copies the snapshot using a key it controls and restores an independent database. Snapshots encrypted with the default AWS managed RDS key cannot be shared directly.
A second VPC and peering require additional network resources and routing that a secondary CIDR in the existing VPC avoids.

choices.solution: Use AWS Transit Gateway to add a transit gateway and connect a second VPC with the first VPC. Update the routes of the transit gateway and VPCs. Create new resources in the subnets of the second VPC.
choices.explanation: A transit gateway adds cost and configuration for an address-capacity issue solvable inside the existing VPC.
Self-managed VPN connectivity adds servers, routing, and failure points unnecessarily.

440.question: A company used an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance during application testing. Before terminating the DB instance at the end of the test cycle, a solutions architect created two backups. The solutions architect created the first backup by using the mysqldump utility to create a database dump. The solutions architect created the second backup by enabling the final DB snapshot option on RDS termination. The company is now planning for a new test cycle and wants to create a new DB instance from the most recent backup. The company has chosen a MySQL-compatible edition of Amazon Aurora to host the DB instance. Which solutions will create the new DB instance? (Choose two.)

choices.explanation: A compatible RDS for MySQL snapshot can be migrated to a new Aurora MySQL cluster.
An RDS snapshot cannot be uploaded to S3 as an ordinary snapshot file; Aurora supports migration from eligible RDS snapshots directly.

choices.solution: Create a new Aurora MySQL cluster. Download the mysqldump backup from Amazon S3 and restore the SQL dump into the cluster with a MySQL client.
choices.explanation: Create an Aurora MySQL cluster and replay the mysqldump SQL through a MySQL client. A logical SQL dump is not a Percona physical backup for Aurora's native S3 restore.
DMS consumes running database sources or supported data formats, not an RDS snapshot as its source.
DMS's S3 source expects supported record files, not a mysqldump SQL script; restore that dump with a MySQL client.
Reservations discount compute but do not remove the unnecessary web-server work for static objects.
Spot lowers some instance cost but still routes static downloads through compute and introduces interruption handling.
Lambda and API Gateway add execution and request-processing layers when S3 and CloudFront directly serve static objects.
Copying petabytes duplicates storage and requires ongoing synchronization across accounts.
Individual resource/user grants require more repeated administration than tag-based policies across many datasets.
Data Exchange adds data-publication workflows when Lake Formation already governs the shared lake.

S3 Transfer Acceleration routes uploads and downloads through nearby edge locations and the AWS network to improve long-distance transfers. Store the application files in S3 and use the accelerated endpoint for object transfers; acceleration does not itself execute a dynamic application backend.
choices.solution: Store application files in Amazon S3 and use S3 Transfer Acceleration for uploads and downloads.

choices.explanation: Cache-Control affects caching behavior, not long-distance upload acceleration for unique large files.
CloudFront caching helps repeated downloads but does not accelerate the large uploads through the EC2 application as specified.
ElastiCache caches application records, not global multi-gigabyte uploads and downloads.
One web instance remains a failure point even with termination protection, and it cannot elastically scale.
Custom dual database writes require coordination, failure handling, and consistency logic instead of managed Multi-AZ replication.
Using only interruptible Spot instances weakens guaranteed web-tier availability, and this option omits the ALB for balanced healthy-target access.
Offline copying requires another strategy for changes made while devices are shipped; mounting S3 is not a native NAS replacement.
rsync does not write directly to an S3 bucket without an additional interface or tool.
Shipping tapes does not provide continuous synchronization of updates or a natively mountable S3 filesystem.
Versioning and MFA Delete do not enforce an immutable seven-year retention period against authorized permanent deletion.
Governance retention can be bypassed by privileged users, and recopying everything adds unnecessary work.
Compliance mode is appropriate, but manually recopying existing objects adds work compared with a Batch Operations retention job.
Object Lock compliance retention protects the retained S3 versions for seven years. Batch Operations applies retention to existing versions; default retention applies only to newly written versions.

choices.solution: Create a Route 53 latency or weighted routing policy for the Regional API endpoints and associate health checks with each record so unhealthy Regions are excluded.
choices.explanation: Latency or weighted routing with health checks supports active-active Regional routing and excludes unhealthy records. Route 53 failover routing is active-passive, so "active-active failover" is not a failover policy setting.
CloudFront does not provide the proposed periodic origin health-check routing; origin-group failover also has method and failure-condition limitations.
Transit gateways connect private networks and cannot attach directly to API Gateway endpoints.
An ALB target group does not accept arbitrary API Gateway endpoint hostnames as targets.
Additional connections between VPCs do not remove the single on-premises customer gateway device.
Another AWS gateway does not eliminate failure of the one customer gateway device, and a VPC cannot attach multiple virtual private gateways as proposed.
VPC peering is already managed and redundant; a second connection between the same VPCs does not fix the customer gateway failure point.
Standard RDS restricts privileged access; replacing the third-party features requires application changes and delays the migration.
RDS Custom for Oracle provides managed automation while allowing supported host and database customization needed for third-party features.
Oracle on EC2 supports customization but leaves database backup, patching, and infrastructure administration to the company.
Rewriting Oracle dependencies for PostgreSQL requires substantial development instead of a quick compatible migration.
Replicating the original single-server stack keeps the tiers coupled and does not establish managed database replication.
A single database instance remains a failure point despite network access controls.
Separate the application tiers into private subnets across two Availability Zones and scale the web and application tiers independently.
Restricting database access is good practice, but a single-instance database lacks the required Multi-AZ resilience.
An internet-facing load balancer in public subnets fronts the private web tier; security-group references restrict traffic between tiers.
An RDS Multi-AZ database in private subnets provides failover and accepts database traffic only from the application tier.
AWS manages the RDS infrastructure and operating system; customers configure and use the database service.
The customer selects RDS configuration and schedules maintenance within the options provided by the managed service.
The customer configures application monitoring, logging, and security tools. With ECS on EC2, the customer also manages and patches the container hosts.
AWS performs RDS engine patch installation; customers choose maintenance settings and approve or schedule applicable upgrades.
AWS is responsible for physical security of its data centers.
Direct Connect does not encrypt traffic by default; the customer configures TLS, a VPN, or supported MACsec encryption as required.
A Fargate task has container startup and minimum billing overhead that is unnecessary for a ten-second hourly function.
Stopping a container does not stop billing for the EC2 instance that hosts it.
Repeated instance startup adds boot time and scheduling work compared with billing only for Lambda execution.
Privileged users can remove a governance-mode vault lock; compliance mode provides the required immutable retention after its grace period.
DLM manages EBS snapshots but does not supply immutable backups across both EC2 and S3.
File Gateway and S3 Lifecycle do not implement immutable retention for the combined EC2 and S3 backup strategy.
Systems Manager Inventory focuses on managed-node configuration, not complete multi-account workload relationship diagrams.
Custom collection and manually drawn diagrams require substantially more ongoing work.
X-Ray traces instrumented application requests; it does not automatically inventory every resource and relationship across accounts.
Cost and Usage Reports is an export/reporting configuration, not the place to establish the proposed AWS Budgets budget.
AWS Budgets tracks costs against the configured account budget threshold.
Budgets actions assume an IAM role, not a user's long-lived credentials.
A Budgets action role provides permissions to apply the chosen corrective action.
Config rules detect compliance states after provisioning; an SCP supplies the preventive API permission boundary.
An alert notifies the company, and a budget action applies an SCP to restrict further provisioning. Budget evaluation is delayed, so it is not a hard real-time spending cap.
Keeping a comparable fleet running in the second Region incurs unnecessary compute cost for backup-based recovery.
Separate snapshot copy schedules require custom orchestration and omit centralized full-instance backup management.
A duplicate running fleet and DataSync add compute and synchronization operations rather than managed backup copies.
DataSync does not provide the required AS2 business-to-business transfer protocol.
AppFlow integrates SaaS data flows but does not supply an AS2 endpoint.

choices.solution: Authenticate application users with the company's existing IdP. Use AWS Transfer Family AS2 servers or connectors with trading-partner profiles and certificates for the data transfer.
choices.explanation: Transfer Family provides managed AS2 exchange. The application handles end-user IdP authentication separately; an AS2 server does not support a Lambda custom identity provider like an SFTP server. AS2 certificates and trading-partner agreements secure the transfer.
Storage Gateway presents storage interfaces, not AS2 transfers or the proposed application IdP integration.
EC2 requires server provisioning, patching, and capacity management.
Lambda runs the API business logic without provisioning or patching application servers.
RDS provides a managed relational database, reducing database infrastructure administration.
DynamoDB is a non-relational database and does not meet the relational-format requirement.
An EKS cluster introduces Kubernetes platform management unnecessary for this small API compute workload.
department is a company-defined tag, not an AWS-generated cost-allocation tag.
Organization-wide cost allocation tags are activated through the management account, not separately through this member account.
The tag is user-defined, and a member-account report does not provide centralized organization-wide activation and reporting.
Custom Lambda integration requires maintaining authentication, API pagination, transfers, and error handling.
Step Functions requires implementing the actual Salesforce transfer tasks and connector logic.
Salesforce has a managed AppFlow connector, so building a custom connector adds unnecessary development work.
An ALB cannot handle the required arbitrary UDP traffic.
Global Accelerator supplies stable entry IPs and optimized routing to NLB endpoints. NLB supports both TCP and UDP and integrates with the application Auto Scaling group.
CloudFront handles HTTP/HTTPS, not arbitrary TCP and UDP game traffic.
Both CloudFront and an ALB lack support for the game's arbitrary UDP traffic.
An Aurora database endpoint cannot subscribe directly to an SNS topic to insert orders.
SNS cannot be polled as a work queue, and Aurora does not accept an SNS subscription as a database ingestion interface.
Waiting until overload to queue requests risks losing earlier work, while scheduled scaling does not respond to unpredictable demand.
A Glue Scala job has startup and execution overhead unnecessary for a small 30-second event-driven task.
An EMR cluster adds compute and cluster management for processing just 2 MB per event.
Glue PySpark adds distributed ETL startup and billing overhead compared with a short Lambda function.
Restoring into a new deployment requires coordinating cutover and can introduce more downtime than modifying the existing instance's deployment.
A read replica is not writable, and weighted DNS does not perform safe database failover for order writes.
RDS instances cannot be placed into an EC2 Auto Scaling group, and independent instances would not share a consistent writer state.
gp3 does not support EBS Multi-Attach.
st1 does not support EBS Multi-Attach.
gp2 does not support EBS Multi-Attach.
A Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group provides redundant instances and automatic replacement, while an ALB routes requests only to healthy application targets.
Snapshots provide recovery artifacts, not a running application tier able to survive an AZ outage immediately.
DNS routing cannot compensate for all application instances residing in one failed AZ.
A multi-AZ ALB does not make single-AZ application instances highly available; the compute fleet must span AZs too.
The Organizations management account controls consolidated discount sharing; the purchasing member account cannot enable the organization-wide setting itself.
Savings Plans and reservation discount sharing are controlled through the management account's billing preferences and apply to eligible usage under consolidated billing.
Moving workloads between accounts adds migration work when shared discounts can cover eligible usage in existing accounts.
Savings Plans cannot be resold in the Reserved Instance Marketplace.
A WebSocket API does not meet the specified REST API interface.
An API Gateway VPC link connects the public API integration to a private load balancer serving ECS tasks, leaving the application infrastructure private.
A WebSocket API is the wrong interface, and a security group alone does not connect API Gateway to private container targets.
A security group does not establish API Gateway's private integration path; a VPC link is required.
Replication creates object copies; it does not automatically tier the originals according to access patterns.
A fixed Standard-IA transition cannot adapt to unpredictable access and can incur retrieval charges when data becomes hot again.
Inventory lists objects and metadata; it does not track last-access patterns or transition objects by itself.
NAT gateways provide IPv4 translation or IPv6-to-IPv4 NAT64; they are not the native outbound-only IPv6 internet gateway requested.
An internet gateway permits bidirectional routing unless additional security rules restrict it; it does not inherently enforce outbound-only IPv6 connections.
A virtual private gateway terminates private VPN connectivity, not general IPv6 internet egress.
Intelligent-Tiering changes storage pricing, not the network path used by containers.
Transfer Acceleration adds transfer charges and is unnecessary for private access from the VPC.
Interface endpoints incur hourly and data-processing charges and use endpoint interfaces/DNS rather than gateway-style route-table association.
DynamoDB does not expose conventional read-replica endpoints that can be added as proposed.
More RCUs help throttled reads but do not provide DAX's sub-millisecond cached-read latency.
Redis requires custom cache population, lookup, and invalidation logic instead of using the DynamoDB-compatible DAX client.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to cache static files at edge locations.

choices.explanation: An ALB cannot directly connect to ElastiCache to serve files; this requires application-managed caching logic.
WAF filters requests and has no rule that caches static content.
Another ALB adds cost and does not cache static files or reduce repeated origin processing.
An all-to-all peering mesh requires many connections and individual routes as the VPC count grows.
Direct Connect gateways connect external networks to AWS resources; they are not the proposed transitive VPC-to-VPC routing fabric.
PrivateLink exposes specific services rather than providing general bidirectional connectivity among all VPC networks.
FSx for Windows does not provide an EFS-style mount target in each AZ of the Region.
FSx for ONTAP uses its filesystem endpoints and HA topology, not a mount target in each AZ as specified.
Regional EFS Standard supplies shared file access across Availability Zones, unlike a single-AZ block volume or local instance store.
FSx for OpenZFS does not provide EFS's regional mount-target model across all required AZs.
SCPs limit maximum permissions but do not grant the new users permission to perform actions.
IAM roles cannot be attached to IAM groups as permission policies.
A permissions boundary limits a role's maximum permissions but does not grant department users access through their groups.

choices.solution: { "Action": ["s3:*Object"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/*"], "Effect": "Allow" }
choices.explanation: s3:*Object permits additional object actions beyond the required DeleteObject permission.

choices.solution: { "Action": ["s3:*"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/*"], "Effect": "Allow" }
choices.explanation: s3:* grants more object permissions than the group's listing and deletion requirements.

choices.solution: { "Action": ["s3:DeleteObject"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/*"], "Effect": "Allow" }

Restoring objects after deletion leaves an exposure window and does not prevent the prohibited operation.

TTL bounds the lifetime of stale entries but does not immediately update them when the database changes.
AppConfig manages application configuration, not transactional database-cache synchronization.
