Lambda container images must use Linux; Windows container images are not supported.
AWS Batch does not run Windows containers on Fargate as proposed.
Keeping a standalone Windows task running between jobs incurs ongoing capacity costs instead of launching a scheduled task for each run.
An organization with all features enabled provides centralized multi-account management and policy controls.
A Cognito identity pool is not the centralized workforce access configuration for AWS Organizations accounts.
SCPs constrain permissions but do not authenticate users or establish corporate directory federation.
Organizations does not itself provide direct directory authentication; IAM Identity Center supplies that integration.
IAM Identity Center integrates with the corporate identity source and assigns access across organization accounts.

choices.solution: Store the video archives in Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and use Expedited retrievals with provisioned retrieval capacity.
choices.explanation: For the archive retrieval tiers in these choices, Glacier Flexible Retrieval Expedited retrievals typically take 1-5 minutes for objects smaller than 250 MB. Provisioned retrieval capacity makes expedited capacity available predictably. The question must assume appropriately sized archives; five minutes is not a universal completion guarantee for large videos. Glacier Standard retrievals take hours. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is a current alternative with millisecond access but is absent from these choices.
Standard Glacier Flexible Retrieval restores typically take hours, exceeding the five-minute maximum.
Standard-IA provides immediate access but has higher storage cost for rarely restored archives.
One Zone-IA has higher archive storage cost and lower AZ resilience than the selected Glacier storage.
CloudFront needs an origin rather than hosting source files itself, and ECS on EC2 retains host management.
EKS on Fargate can work but adds Kubernetes control-plane cost and management when ECS meets the container requirements more simply.
EC2 static hosting and EC2-backed Kubernetes add unnecessary server and cluster management.
FSx filesystems require provisioned capacity and a selected filesystem type; EFS has no minimum provisioned storage size.
EBS Multi-Attach is AZ-scoped block storage, not a native shared filesystem reachable from on premises.
A single mount target remains AZ-dependent for connectivity; multiple access points do not create additional AZ mount targets.
Granting the finance team billing access does not deny access to member-account users or roots.
IAM identity policies cannot be attached to a root user.
Changing the Organizations feature set does not impose the required permission denial and removes SCP capability.
An SNS subscription dead-letter queue must be an SQS queue, not a Kinesis data stream.
A queue before SNS does not capture messages whose delivery from SNS to the HTTPS subscriber ultimately fails.
DynamoDB cannot be configured as an SNS subscription dead-letter queue.
An EMR scan-based export consumes table reads and requires cluster and job management.
DynamoDB point-in-time recovery enables managed exports of a selected table state to S3 without consuming table read capacity. An export is a point-in-time operation, not continuous streaming.
A stream consumer can export changes but requires custom batching, failure handling, and file-writing code.
A custom export function adds code and scheduling; PITR plus native exports avoids scanning table data through RCUs.
An SQS standard queue provides durable at-least-once delivery with low operational overhead. The Lambda execution role requires queue permissions and kms:Decrypt for the encrypted messages.
SSE-SQS does not require a KMS invocation permission, and FIFO adds ordering overhead that is not required.
FIFO is more expensive than Standard when only at-least-once processing is needed; Lambda processing still requires idempotency.
The consumer needs kms:Decrypt on its execution role, not an undefined encryption-key invocation permission.
Approved templates alone do not prevent users from launching disallowed instances through other APIs.
Stopping instances after launch is reactive and leaves a provisioning and billing window.
Service Catalog needs product setup and tightly scoped provisioning permissions; an SCP directly constrains instance types across the accounts.
Comprehend analyzes text; it neither transcribes audio nor translates it into English.
Lex builds conversational interfaces, not written sentiment-analysis reports from recordings.
Polly converts text to speech, the opposite of the required transcription.

Translate converts supported source-language text into English.
Comprehend evaluates the English text for sentiment and produces results that can be aggregated into reports.
EC2 instances do not expose the proposed resource policy; the shown identity policy already contains the relevant conditional deny.
Identity-based policies omit Principal because the attached role is the identity receiving permissions.
ec2:TerminateInstances is the correct action; the source-IP condition causes the denial.

Audit Manager gathers compliance evidence; it does not inspect S3 content for passport or credit-card numbers.
S3 Inventory lists object metadata rather than examining object contents for PII.
S3 Select is a per-object query facility, not automated bucket-wide sensitive-data discovery.
S3 is object storage and does not directly provide the applications' existing local cached NFS interface.
S3 File Gateway exposes NFS or SMB file shares backed by S3 with a local cache.
Snowball Edge is a transfer/edge device rather than the long-term managed gateway for this hybrid storage architecture.
Volume Gateway exposes iSCSI block volumes and stores managed backups in AWS.
EFS access over the network does not provide local caching or solve the block-storage requirement.
A NAT instance adds compute and maintenance cost when an S3 gateway endpoint has no hourly or processing fee.
A private NAT instance lacks direct internet access, and changing the public subnet route does not route the private workers' traffic correctly.
An S3 gateway endpoint installs a service-prefix route in the private subnet's route table, allowing S3 traffic to bypass a NAT gateway.
Another NAT gateway preserves per-GB processing charges rather than removing them with an S3 gateway endpoint.

Retain the current version and one newer noncurrent version with NoncurrentVersionExpiration, using NewerNoncurrentVersions=1 and a noncurrent-age threshold. Older versions are removed asynchronously only after both conditions are met; lifecycle rules do not impose an instantaneous two-version limit.
Custom Lambda enumeration and deletion require code, scheduling, and failure handling compared with native Lifecycle retention.
Batch Operations requires creating and maintaining manifests and jobs; Lifecycle automatically handles future versions.
Suspending versioning does not prune older versions or automatically retain exactly the two most recent versions.
Another full-size dedicated connection does not reduce the underutilized connection's base cost.
Dedicated 200-Mbps connections are not provisioned directly through the console; a partner supplies hosted connections at that capacity.
A shared 1-Gbps connection retains unnecessary capacity and requires coordinating sharing instead of purchasing the right-sized hosted connection.
A Direct Connect Partner can provision a hosted connection at supported sub-1-Gbps bandwidth such as 200 Mbps; dedicated connections have different capacity options.
DataSync copies SMB file data to FSx for Windows File Server and can preserve Windows ACLs when the required permissions are configured.
Ordinary CLI S3 copies do not preserve Windows security descriptors and ACLs required at the FSx destination.
Shipping bare drives to AWS is not the supported managed import workflow, and S3 staging does not preserve the required Windows ACLs.
Historically, a Snowcone device could run a DataSync agent for an online SMB transfer that preserves ACLs. This is an older alternative; use a supported DataSync agent host for new deployments.
CLI copying through Snowball's S3 interface does not retain the Windows security metadata as DataSync's SMB-to-FSx transfer does.
Custom Lambda analysis requires implementing stream processing and S3 delivery rather than using managed analysis and delivery services.
Glue is not the proposed real-time ingestion endpoint, and this option does not specify delivery of analyzed data into the S3 lake.

choices.solution: Ingest data into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink for real-time analysis and Amazon Data Firehose to deliver the stream or analysis output into the S3 data lake.
choices.explanation: Kinesis Data Streams durably ingests the data, and Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink provides managed stream processing. Use Firehose where the design requires delivery to S3. The former Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL service was discontinued in January 2026.
API Gateway and custom Lambda processing require implementing ingestion handling and reliable S3 delivery.
S3 is object storage rather than the existing shared POSIX filesystem; using a mount adapter can change filesystem semantics.
An NFS share hosted on the original instance preserves that instance as a single failure point.
EFS provides one shared image repository that all application instances can mount concurrently.
Global Accelerator routes traffic but does not cache website content to offload repeated image requests as CloudFront does.
A Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group replaces failed instances and scales the website behind an ALB; CloudFront improves delivery and reduces origin load.

A customer-created cross-account role provides temporary read-only permissions for EC2 and CloudWatch. Use an external ID in the trust policy for a third-party service to prevent the confused-deputy problem.
A custom token-vending service adds credential-handling code; each customer still needs a trusted scoped IAM role.
Stored customer access keys are long-lived secrets requiring rotation instead of temporary AssumeRole credentials.
Cognito usernames do not directly authorize service API calls and add unnecessary stored credentials.
A peering mesh across hundreds of accounts requires many connections and individually maintained routes.
NAT and internet gateways expose an internet path and do not supply centralized private inter-VPC routing.
A transit VPC and VPN gateways require managing appliances and tunnels instead of a managed transit gateway.
A continuously billed commitment is inefficient for six hours of daily interruption-tolerant work compared with Spot capacity.
A reservation commits to instance usage beyond this short nightly window and misses available Spot savings.
Increasing instance size keeps On-Demand pricing and does not exploit the job's retry tolerance.
Proxying uploads through application servers creates a bandwidth and compute bottleneck.
File Gateway supplies NFS/SMB interfaces, not a public browser upload endpoint.
Browsers cannot directly upload over the EFS NFS protocol; an application intermediary would still be required.

DynamoDB global tables support multiple regional deployments, but the default eventually consistent mode does not meet globally consistent reservation semantics. This answer is only valid with a supported strong-consistency configuration and deliberate single-Region writes. Aurora Global Database is the single-writer alternative; no configuration guarantees subsecond latency between arbitrary Regions.

Aurora global database retains one primary writer and replicates to Regional readers with typically sub-second lag. All reservation writes use the primary to preserve a single authoritative database. Replication latency is not a guaranteed sub-second bound; reads requiring the latest committed reservation must also use the writer.
choices.solution: Migrate the reservation database to an Aurora MySQL global database with one primary writer and read-only secondary clusters in the application Regions. Direct reservation writes to the primary writer and reads to the appropriate Regional endpoint.

choices.explanation: Cross-Region RDS MySQL read replicas are asynchronous and read-only; each Regional endpoint cannot accept reservation updates.
Independent databases synchronized with Lambda require custom conflict and consistency logic and do not establish one globally consistent primary.
Copying only on demand leaves no automatic second-Region copy if the source Region fails.
Data Lifecycle Manager can create tagged EBS-backed AMIs on a schedule and copy them to the recovery Region.
A custom Lambda copy scheduler adds code when AWS Backup supports copy actions natively.
AWS Backup schedules tagged EC2 backups and cross-Region copies, preserving recovery points outside the primary Region.
Manual on-demand copying does not guarantee the required up-to-date recovery copy in the second Region.
Security groups do not support explicit deny rules.
A network ACL can explicitly deny the abusive source IP ranges. Put deny rules before matching allow rules and account for stateless return-traffic rules.
Security groups do not support deny rules, and filtering after traffic reaches the application tier misses the front-end resource consumption.
Behind the ALB, network traffic reaches targets from ALB addresses; blocking original client addresses in target subnet ACLs does not reliably block the public requests.
The rule is on the application side rather than permitting database ingress, and the option omits the required peering routes.
Security-group references across VPC peering are supported within the same Region, not this inter-Region peering connection.

choices.solution: Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPC. Update the subnet route tables. Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that allows traffic from the eu-west-1 application server IP addresses.

choices.explanation: Transit-gateway peering does not allow cross-Region security-group references as proposed.

choices.explanation: A dedicated Aurora cluster adds storage and compute cost for an environment used only a few hours daily.
On-Demand Aurora still requires a provisioned cluster; Single-AZ RDS is sufficient for these nonproduction databases.
S3 Select does not host a PostgreSQL database or support the developers' PostgreSQL schema.
Running state does not determine whether persistent resource data needs backup; stopped resources can still require protection.
Manual reviews across account owners add ongoing effort and risk missing resources.
Inspector discovers vulnerabilities, not completeness of backup resource tagging.
CloudFront needs a content origin, Step Functions needs an actual image-processing task, and RDS adds unnecessary image-storage overhead.
One EC2 web and resizing server is a failure point and lacks elastic processing capacity.
An independently scaling front end does not remove the single EC2 image processor's capacity and availability bottleneck.
IAM permissions alone do not create network access to the private API and required AWS service endpoints.

choices.solution: Create the interface VPC endpoints required for private node access to AWS services, including ECR and EC2, plus an S3 gateway endpoint for image layers. Verify private Kubernetes API endpoint DNS and security-group access.
choices.explanation: The private Kubernetes API endpoint is managed by EKS and is different from the EKS management API PrivateLink endpoint. Nodes also require IAM permissions, DNS, security-group access to the private API, and connectivity to services such as ECR, S3, and EC2 when no internet egress exists.
Public nodes violate the required private data-plane placement.
Outbound allow rules do not create routes or private endpoints where no egress path exists.
The Redshift Data API provides SQL access for traditional, containerized, and event-driven applications without persistent client connections.
Redshift supports encrypted storage and TLS connections. An application can encrypt sensitive fields before ingestion, though this limits server-side analytics on those fields.
Redshift supports scheduled analytical workloads and can pause eligible provisioned clusters between runs to reduce compute costs.
Redshift is an analytics warehouse, not a cache for a transactional backend database.
Globally distributed millions-per-minute low-latency key access is not Redshift's analytical query workload model.
Redshift does not expose a simple cluster secondary-replica creation option as a general migration use case.
An ECS service requires task and capacity management when provisioned Lambda concurrency supplies ready compute for the API.
EKS adds Kubernetes platform and workload administration.
Reserved concurrency allocates a concurrency limit but does not pre-initialize functions to eliminate cold starts.
Installing an agent and exporting log groups adds steps compared with Session Manager's native S3 session logging.
A daily document to collect all server logs adds custom handling and is less direct than native session logging.
A log subscription and Firehose pipeline add services and configuration when Session Manager can write directly to S3.
Changing the instance class increases compute and memory, not the allocated database storage.
Changing storage type does not itself add the required disk capacity.
Backup/restore and database cutover add work and downtime risk compared with online storage autoscaling.
Templates describe deployments but do not supply the centralized governed self-service portfolio of Service Catalog.
Systems Manager documents automate operations rather than exposing governed infrastructure products to customers.
Config items record resource configurations; they are not self-service deployment products.
Provisioned autoscaling reacts after demand changes and remains bounded by the chosen maximum, risking throttling during unpredictable surges.
Standard-IA has higher read/write request pricing and provisioned scaling limits for this moderate-to-high access workload.
Standard-IA trades cheaper storage for higher request charges and is unsuitable for the stated high access rate.
DynamoDB uses IAM-signed requests, not a database password supplied by Secrets Manager.
Long-lived cross-account user keys require storage and manual rotation instead of scoped temporary role credentials.

In the inventory account, create a role named APP_ROLE that allows access to the STS AssumeRole API operation. Configure the application to use APP_ROLE and assume the cross-account role BU_ROLE to read the DynamoDB table.

ACM certificates are not a supported replacement for IAM authentication to DynamoDB.
A custom Lambda cluster scaler adds code and duplicates Kubernetes autoscaling components.
The Kubernetes Metrics Server supplies CPU and memory metrics to the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, which changes pod replica counts. Custom metrics require a separate metrics adapter.
Cluster Autoscaler changes EC2 node-group capacity when pods cannot be scheduled or nodes are underutilized.
API Gateway does not scale Kubernetes pods or worker nodes.
App Mesh observes and controls service networking, not the number of pods or cluster nodes.

Lambda@Edge requires custom orchestration and remote database calls. CloudFront does not itself retrieve and combine records from multiple DynamoDB tables; AppSync pipeline resolvers provide that coordination with less application code.
API Gateway plus Lambda can work but requires custom multi-table orchestration code that AppSync pipeline resolvers provide declaratively.
Athena federation targets analytical queries and adds query startup and connector overhead to an interactive application.
Custom Glue scripts add processing and development work compared with directly querying the CloudTrail dataset with Athena.
Batch requires writing and running custom log-processing jobs.
QuickSight needs a queryable data source and visualization setup; Athena directly searches the required error fields.
CSV downloads require report generation and ingestion instead of directly retrieving and forecasting costs through an API.
Budgets actions do not provide the proposed FTP usage-data export or forecasting API.
Email reports require parsing and do not provide the desired programmatic historical and forecast retrieval.
Additional readers do not prevent writer connections from dropping or resolve reconnection delays during failover.
A separate cluster requires replication and custom cutover handling rather than a stable managed proxy endpoint.
Memcached cannot serve database writes or preserve database connection continuity during writer failover.
An Auto Scaling group cannot extend into another Region; separate regional groups are required.
Cross-Region replica replication has more overhead and slower recovery characteristics than Aurora global database's storage-level replication.
DMS adds a replication service and operational complexity compared with Aurora's integrated global database replication.
Nightly processing violates immediate handling, and Glacier adds restore delays plus a self-managed FTP server.
The workflow still waits for nightly processing and retains an EC2 FTP server to maintain.
Transfer Family does not use EBS as its managed backend, and S3 event notifications cannot arise from EBS file creation.

Transfer Family provides a managed FTP endpoint backed by S3. Object-created events invoke Lambda immediately; the stated 3-8 minute processing duration fits Lambda's 15-minute timeout. Delete the input only after successful, idempotent processing.
EC2 databases retain operating-system, database maintenance, and backup responsibilities.
S3 object storage is not a transactional database replacement, and Macie discovers sensitive data rather than supplying database functionality.
CloudWatch Logs records events but does not encrypt stored database data.
CloudFront does not proxy arbitrary TCP and UDP game protocols.
An ALB cannot support UDP or arbitrary TCP game traffic.
API Gateway handles supported API protocols, not the game's arbitrary UDP communications.
An ALB adds load-balancer resources and configuration when a function URL directly supplies the webhook endpoint.
An SNS topic endpoint requires AWS Publish API authentication; it is not a generic HTTPS webhook receiver.
An SQS endpoint requires signed queue API requests rather than accepting an ordinary webhook callback.
Register the domain and configure a Route 53 wildcard DNS record pointing to the Regional API Gateway custom domain endpoint.
A Regional API custom domain uses an ACM certificate in the same Region; an arbitrary other Region is not supported.
Separate hosted zones for each customer add administration compared with one wildcard domain and certificate.
Request an ACM wildcard certificate in the same Region as the Regional API endpoint.
Separate API deployments for every customer add unnecessary duplication and management.
Associate the ACM certificate with an API Gateway wildcard custom domain and configure the API mapping; the certificate is referenced, not imported from ACM.
GuardDuty detects threats rather than inspecting object contents for PII; the proposed CRITICAL filter is not the Macie sensitive-data finding.
A finding delivered to SQS still needs a consumer to notify human recipients; SNS directly supplies security-team notifications.
GuardDuty does not perform the required PII discovery, and SQS does not directly notify human recipients.
Keeping the logs at Standard pricing after day 30 misses savings during their infrequent-access period.

choices.solution: Store logs in S3 Standard initially. Transition them to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days and expire them after 90 days. Do not transition them to Glacier at the same time they expire.
choices.explanation: Standard serves the first month's frequent analysis, then Standard-IA reduces storage cost for the next 60 days. Glacier Flexible Retrieval has a 90-day minimum storage duration, so a 60-day archive incurs early-deletion charges; a transition at expiration adds no useful retention.
Glacier Flexible Retrieval has a 90-day minimum storage duration; deleting only 60 days after transition incurs early-deletion charges.
One Zone-IA reduces resilience, and transitioning to Glacier on the same day as expiration incurs unnecessary operations and minimum-duration charges.
Storing secrets in Secrets Manager does not configure encryption of Kubernetes secrets already stored in etcd.

EKS provides default KMS-backed envelope encryption for Kubernetes API data on clusters running Kubernetes 1.28 or later. A customer-managed KMS key can be configured when customer control is required. Earlier supported configurations explicitly enabled KMS secrets encryption; creating a customer key is not required merely to obtain encryption on modern clusters.
The EBS CSI driver manages workload volumes, not encryption of the managed control-plane etcd store.
EBS defaults do not configure EKS control-plane encryption, and the AWS-managed aws/ebs alias cannot be used for a newly created customer key.
A larger writer still executes the complex analysis alongside production work and does not add database high availability.
A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance standby cannot serve reads and cannot be separately sized as proposed.

A traditional Multi-AZ instance pair plus two separate read replicas provisions four database instances. The selected Multi-AZ DB cluster integrates one writer and two readable standbys, supplying availability and analytical read capacity without the extra instance.

An RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB cluster includes one writer and two readable standbys across three Availability Zones. Its reader endpoint isolates analytical reads, and integrated failover supplies high availability without adding separate replicas.
Memcached lacks Redis replication and automatic failover needed for reliable shared session state.
Migrating MySQL to DynamoDB requires a different data model and query implementation rather than preserving relational compatibility.
The single-AZ database remains a failure point despite multi-AZ compute and caching.
Signed access grants are not geographic allowlists; authorized links could still be used from excluded countries without an additional location restriction.
Encryption does not determine the viewer's country or enforce a country rollout.
Time-based URL expiration limits when content is accessible, not the countries from which it can be viewed.
SQL Server Enterprise licensing and a continuously active second site add unnecessary cost compared with replication to a small DR staging area.
A warm RDS target incurs continuous database compute cost and database-only CDC does not recover the complete source VM.

AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates block-level changes to a low-cost staging area in AWS and can launch recovery instances during a disaster. This is designed for low RPO/RTO DR while avoiding the cost of a continuously running warm standby. Nightly backups cannot meet an RPO of 30 seconds.
Nightly backups allow up to a day of data loss, far exceeding the 30-second RPO.

540.question: A company has an on-premises server that uses an Oracle database to process and store customer information. The company wants to use an AWS database service to achieve higher availability and to improve application performance. The company also wants to offload reporting from its primary database system. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

choices.explanation: Custom DMS replication to separately created databases adds management compared with native RDS replication and failover.
The primary and replica share one AZ and do not provide the requested higher availability across failures.

choices.solution: Migrate the Oracle database to Amazon RDS for Oracle with a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Create an Oracle read replica and direct reporting queries to that replica.
choices.explanation: RDS for Oracle Multi-AZ provides failover, and a separate Oracle read replica offloads reporting. Oracle does not use the RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster reader architecture; Oracle read replicas require the supported Enterprise Edition and Active Data Guard licensing.
Aurora is not Oracle-compatible, so replacing the engine requires application and schema changes.
API Gateway and Lambda implement the API, while DynamoDB stores user data without database server management.
An always-running ECS/ALB and RDS stack adds idle-period costs, and the proposed integration inconsistently refers to a Lambda function.
A Cognito user pool provides user registration and authentication.
A Cognito identity pool supplies AWS credentials for already authenticated identities; a user pool provides the sign-in directory.
Amplify Hosting publishes the static frontend through CloudFront for scalable global delivery.
S3 static hosting cannot execute PHP server-side code.
S3 has presigned URLs, not the proposed viewer signed cookies; CloudFront signs the private distribution's access grants.
OAC restricts origin access to CloudFront, not access by premium versus non-premium viewers.
Field-level encryption protects request data fields; it does not authorize customers to download private content.

Consolidated discount sharing is controlled from the Organizations management account after accounts are joined.

Immediately merging and deploying definitions to production sends every user to the new behavior without a controlled canary trial.
Overwriting and deploying the production API gives no gradual traffic exposure or easy canary rollback.
A DNS endpoint switch can be affected by cached records and does not provide API Gateway's controlled percentage-based rollout.

Active-active routing sends normal traffic to both endpoints and adds an unnecessary EC2 server for the error page.
Multivalue routing returns healthy records without modeling the required primary/secondary preference, and it cannot use S3 website aliases in the proposed way.
NFS changes the existing tape-backup interface instead of preserving the virtual tape library workflow.
EFS is a filesystem, not a virtual tape library compatible with the existing tape backup application.
EFS does not expose an iSCSI interface.
Glue streaming jobs need a streaming source and job configuration; Firehose directly supplies managed ingestion and S3 delivery.
Custom Lambda delivery requires implementing buffering, retries, and failure handling supplied by Firehose.
DMS streams database changes, not arbitrary sensor ingestion as a general-purpose streaming receiver.
Systems Manager templates do not prevent users from invoking disallowed services outside the templates.
CloudFormation provisioning does not impose a permission boundary on other API calls.
Service Catalog controls product provisioning but requires additional IAM restrictions to prevent direct use of other services.
A NAT instance requires patching, scaling, and availability management.
An internet gateway does not translate private IPv4 addresses; the private database still needs NAT for public access.
A virtual private gateway routes VPN/Direct Connect connections, not general public internet egress.
A Lambda resource policy grants invocation access; it does not authorize the function to decrypt with KMS.
Grant the Lambda execution role kms:Decrypt on the specific key used for encrypted values.
The function's incoming resource policy is not its execution identity for KMS operations.
The KMS key policy must also permit the execution role directly or enable IAM delegation; IAM permission alone cannot override a restrictive key policy.
A resource policy is not an IAM principal that can be granted key use; grant the execution role in the key policy.

choices.solution: Use S3 Standard initially. Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition reports to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 7 days, explicitly allowing objects smaller than 128 KB.
choices.explanation: Glacier Flexible Retrieval standard restores typically complete within 3-5 hours, while Deep Archive cannot meet a six-hour requirement. The 50 KB reports need an explicit lifecycle size-filter or transition-default override because current lifecycle defaults block transitions below 128 KB. Assess per-object request and metadata overhead for small files.
