Deep Archive standard retrieval generally takes around 12 hours, exceeding the six-hour requirement.
Standard reservations lack the required freedom to change instance families regularly, and a three-year commitment is less flexible.

A Compute Savings Plan provides flexibility across EC2 instance families, sizes, Regions, operating systems, and compute services while still providing a commitment discount. A 1-year No Upfront plan best matches the need to change instance type and family every few months.
An upfront Standard reservation still constrains the instance configuration rather than allowing repeated family changes.
EC2 Instance Savings Plans are tied to a selected family and Region, even with an upfront payment.
Security Hub aggregates security findings, while a Config rule does not inspect S3 object contents for PII.
Inspector scans supported compute artifacts for vulnerabilities, not S3 objects for PII.
GuardDuty detects malicious activity, not sensitive data within S3 object contents.
Compute-optimized application instances do not address the application's measured high memory utilization.
Storage-optimized instances target local disk I/O rather than the memory bottleneck in both components.
HPC-optimized application instances target specialized compute workloads instead of the identified high memory demand.
An SQS interface endpoint provides private connectivity. Allow HTTPS from application instances in the endpoint security group and restrict access through IAM and endpoint policies.
Public-subnet endpoint placement can still be private, but the proposed endpoint policy alone omits the endpoint security-group rule needed to allow instance connections.
An SQS resource policy belongs on the queue, not on the interface endpoint; the endpoint needs its own policy and security group.
SQS does not support gateway endpoints, and a NAT gateway for internet egress belongs in a public subnet.
Read-only permissions omit the application's required DynamoDB writes.
Template parameters introduce long-lived access keys instead of automatically supplied instance-role credentials.
Embedding generated access keys in user data exposes long-lived credentials and adds rotation work.
Athena and a separate Glue enrichment stage can work, but split processing across services instead of one parallel EMR job reading and joining both datasets.
EMR runs distributed processing for the S3 dataset and can join it with Redshift-derived data through supported connectors and permissions.
Moving the S3 dataset into Redshift through Kinesis adds ingestion infrastructure instead of enriching it in the existing parallel processing job.
Lake Formation governs data access; it does not execute the proposed Redshift enrichment transformation.
Transit Gateway adds attachment and data-processing charges unnecessary for connecting just two VPCs.
A VPN requires gateways or appliances and tunnel management that direct VPC peering avoids.
Direct Connect connects an external network to AWS, not a physical connection directly between two AWS VPCs.
A product-line tag applied by the teams is user-defined, not AWS-generated.
Choose the user-defined resource tag that identifies the product line for cost allocation.
Resource Groups organizes resources but does not activate the tag for billing cost allocation.
The management account activates consolidated cost-allocation tags for organization reporting.
Activate the tag in the Organizations management account so consolidated billing can attribute eligible resource costs by product line.
Config aggregators combine resource compliance information; they do not supply Control Tower's direct managed OU drift notifications.
Custom account products and CloudTrail event analysis add provisioning and detection work.
CloudFormation drift detects changes to stack-managed resource properties, not every organization-wide hierarchy change.
Redis requires explicit cache population and invalidation code rather than DynamoDB-compatible cached requests.
Memcached requires custom cache integration and does not directly implement the DynamoDB API.
A stream-to-cache Lambda pipeline adds custom synchronization and failure-handling work.
Associate the DynamoDB gateway endpoint with the relevant route tables so the service prefix-list route is installed.
A DynamoDB gateway endpoint provides access from the VPC without an internet gateway or NAT gateway.
An EC2 interface endpoint provides private EC2 API access, not DynamoDB API connectivity.
A DynamoDB gateway endpoint uses route-table entries rather than endpoint network interfaces in each subnet.
Gateway endpoints have no security group; access uses routing, endpoint policies, and relevant instance security rules.
Container Insights provides telemetry but is not the direct unified EKS console registration and workload-view mechanism.
Systems Manager manages nodes and operations rather than registering arbitrary Kubernetes clusters for the EKS console.
EKS Anywhere manages deployment of clusters and does not act as a native central control plane for all other independent clusters.
EBS encryption protects physical storage but a database administrator can read plaintext through the database engine.
Server-side S3 encryption decrypts data for authorized readers and is not the transactional relational storage requested.
File permissions do not cryptographically protect sensitive fields against privileged administrators.
RDS storage autoscaling grows disk space, not database compute or read capacity for increased demand.
Redshift is an analytical engine rather than a compatible MySQL transactional replacement; mysqldump cannot directly restore it.
DynamoDB requires a different data model and APIs, violating compatibility with the existing MySQL applications.
S3 object APIs do not provide the shared directory filesystem expected by the unchanged applications.
EBS Multi-Attach is limited to one AZ and requires coordinated block access, not cross-AZ shared filesystem access.
Separate replicated filesystems require custom synchronization and concurrent-write conflict handling.
An EC2 fleet requires server management, and S3 does not directly supply tenant usage aggregation as a database.
Self-managed SQL Server on EC2 retains patching, backup, and capacity-management responsibilities.
EC2 and EFS add running infrastructure and custom file-based aggregation instead of managed API and database services.
Glacier requires restore operations, while ElastiCache is not a global object content-delivery cache.
EBS is provisioned block storage rather than an economical petabyte-scale object origin directly usable by CloudFront.
Storage Gateway adds an appliance and hybrid storage layer unnecessary for components entirely in AWS, and ElastiCache is not a global CDN.
EventBridge publishes matched-event, invocation, and failed-invocation metrics in the AWS/Events CloudWatch namespace, distinguishing rule matching from target delivery failures.
A dead-letter queue shows exhausted delivery failures only if configured; it does not reveal unmatched events or every invocation.
EventBridge does not automatically place all rule matches and invocations into CloudWatch Logs without a configured logging target.
CloudTrail audits EventBridge API operations rather than supplying the rule's matching and target-invocation metrics.
A reminder still requires manual scaling or custom action wiring.
Manual scaling requires operator intervention every Friday.
Reactive automatic scaling waits for load rather than provisioning for the known recurring workload; scheduled scaling is more direct.

Importing an externally issued certificate preserves the required CA. For current API Gateway REST APIs, the SecurityPolicy_TLS13_1_3_2025_09 policy rejects TLS 1.2 and accepts TLS 1.3; configure it on the applicable endpoint and custom domain. Merely using an HTTP API does not establish the stated TLS-1.3-only requirement.
choices.solution: Obtain a certificate signed by the required third-party CA and import it into ACM. Create an API Gateway Regional REST API with a custom domain using the certificate and a TLS-1.3-only enhanced security policy.

choices.explanation: ACM-issued public certificates use Amazon's CA; obtaining a specific third-party CA signature requires issuing externally and importing the certificate.
ACM cannot issue from an arbitrary external public CA, and Lambda function URLs do not support attaching a custom certificate.
A Lambda function URL cannot be configured with this custom domain certificate, and ACM does not issue through an arbitrary external CA.
DynamoDB is not a MySQL-compatible relational database.
A provisioned Aurora instance is sized by DB instance class, not a minimum Serverless ACU setting.
A fixed 2-GiB RDS instance does not automatically adjust database compute capacity as workload changes.
Provisioned concurrency incurs standing charges for ready execution environments that the relaxed latency requirements do not justify.
A larger timeout does not reduce initialization latency.
More memory can improve CPU-dependent initialization but increases execution cost and does not reuse a SnapStart initialized snapshot.

Use a compatible Aurora Serverless v2 MySQL engine version with minimum capacity set to zero ACUs and automatic pause/resume. The database scales for its short weekly workload and incurs no instance-capacity charges while paused; storage charges remain. A nonzero minimum would continue incurring idle compute cost.
Provisioned Aurora incurs idle compute charges unless explicitly stopped; compatible Serverless v2 auto-pause can reduce compute to zero between uses.
An EC2 reservation commits to usage despite the database running only two hours weekly and leaves database administration to the company.
Operating MySQL containers requires database persistence, backup, and availability management instead of a managed database.
DynamoDB does not provide a PostgreSQL engine.
A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance standby cannot serve reads, so it does not add readable capacity.
Cross-Region read replicas are asynchronous and require promotion for writer failover; a Multi-AZ cluster directly provides managed HA and readable standbys.
A private API endpoint is reachable through private VPC connectivity, not globally distributed public users.
A Regional endpoint enters through its Region rather than CloudFront edge locations unless a separate distribution is added.
An interface VPC endpoint supplies private API connectivity rather than global public edge acceleration.
A security policy selects TLS versions and ciphers; it does not issue certificates.
OAC authenticates origin requests and does not create viewer TLS certificates.
Email validation requires domain-owner email approval and renewal handling; persistent DNS validation enables simpler automated renewal.
Redshift changes the database model and targets analytical queries rather than cached DynamoDB key reads.
RDS requires changing the application's database engine and does not provide the DAX cache integration.
Redis requires custom cache population and invalidation rather than DynamoDB-compatible cached access.
Disabling backups risks data protection and does not remove idle database compute charges.
A custom CPU-based scheduler adds code and can misinterpret a temporary low-utilization interval; the usage timetable is already known.
An upfront reservation commits to usage outside business hours rather than removing unnecessary running time.
Lustre changes local block-storage access into a network filesystem and adds unnecessary filesystem cost.
gp2 generally costs more per GB and ties IOPS to volume size, whereas gp3 provides a predictable baseline independently.
OpenZFS introduces a network filesystem and managed-filesystem charges instead of preserving simple attached block storage.
Losing either AZ leaves only one instance, below the required two-instance minimum.

Four On-Demand instances, with two in each of two Availability Zones, preserve the required two running instances if one entire zone fails. Two instances total would leave only one after a zone failure.
All instances share one AZ failure risk and Spot interruptions can also remove them.
If the On-Demand AZ fails, only interruptible Spot capacity remains, which cannot guarantee two running production instances.
Simple routing cannot choose records based on the user's geographic proximity.
A latency policy associated only with us-west-1 omits the European endpoint; a complete two-endpoint latency configuration would be another valid design.
An even weighted split sends some users to the distant site regardless of latency.

583.question: A company has 5 PB of archived data on physical tapes. The company needs to preserve the data on the tapes for another 10 years for compliance purposes. The company wants to migrate to AWS in the next 6 months. The data center that stores the tapes has a 1 Gbps uplink internet connectivity. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? [Historical question: Tape Gateway on Snowball Edge is no longer available; the listed offline option cannot be deployed today.]

choices.explanation: Even an ideal 1-Gbps link needs substantially more than six months to transfer 5 PB.
Reading and uploading tapes through the existing 1-Gbps connection cannot meet the migration deadline.

This is the historical offline-transfer answer, but Tape Gateway on Snowball Edge was discontinued in March 2024. None of the listed choices currently solves the stated 5 PB migration in six months over a 1 Gbps link: transferring 5 PB continuously would take roughly 463 days before overhead. Use a current physical-transfer service or increase network capacity.
An online Tape Gateway still sends the dataset through the insufficient 1-Gbps uplink.

choices.solution: Run the EC2 instances in a partition placement group, placing each node group in a separate logical partition.
choices.explanation: Partition placement ensures that node groups in different partitions do not share the same underlying hardware. This supports large distributed deployments with hundreds of instances. Spread placement is intended for small groups and has a seven-instance-per-AZ limit for rack-level spread.
Account boundaries do not control which physical hosts the instances share.
Dedicated tenancy isolates hardware from other customers but does not separate the company's own node groups into distinct failure domains.
Shared tenancy supplies no guarantee that node groups avoid shared hardware.
Unreserved On-Demand capacity is subject to availability at failover time.
Savings Plans provide billing discounts but do not reserve physical capacity.
Regional Reserved Instances provide discounts without guaranteeing capacity in a selected failover AZ.
An AWS account can belong to only one organization at a time.
An AWS account can belong to only one organization at a time. Leave the previous organization before accepting the new organization's invitation.
Creating a replacement account and migrating resources adds unnecessary work when the existing account can join the new organization.
The new management account cannot also act as a member of the previous organization while managing its own organization.
Gateway Load Balancer is for network appliances and does not provide the proposed application authorization and HTTP ingestion interface.
Data Streams does not directly write records into S3; it requires a delivery consumer that this option omits.
A GWLB is not a user-authorized HTTP API endpoint, and the proposed Lambda authorization integration is not a GWLB capability.
A continuously running cross-Region replica incurs compute and storage costs beyond what the 24-hour recovery objectives require.
DMS adds a continuously running replication service and target database for a backup-based recovery requirement.
Automating native SQL backup export and S3 copies adds more operations than managed cross-Region snapshot copies.
Memcached does not replicate cached session records or provide automatic failover preserving them after a node failure.
A cached block-storage gateway is intended for hybrid volumes, not a low-latency distributed web session service.

A highly available RDS database can store shared sessions, but adds relational query and connection overhead compared with the intended Redis session store; it is not inherently incapable of meeting availability.
A restored backup is a point-in-time dataset and requires repeated backup, restore, and synchronization work.
Exporting to S3 requires a new reporting pipeline and queries instead of reusing the existing MySQL reports on a replica.
A larger writer increases ongoing cost and leaves reporting queries competing with the daily transactional workload.
An NLB cannot inspect HTTP paths to route customer and order requests to different services.
Custom Lambda routing adds invocation cost and development work compared with ALB path rules.
API Gateway adds API configuration and integration overhead when an ALB ingress directly supplies the required routing.
Public bucket access bypasses paid authorization, and MFA does not add geographic viewer restrictions.
Per-customer IAM users add credential administration and do not provide edge caching or country restrictions.
Regional web-server placement does not prevent users in excluded countries from accessing public ALB URLs and adds compute costs.
ElastiCache Redis does not expose the proposed Redis AOF persistence configuration, and multiple same-AZ nodes alone do not provide Multi-AZ resilience.

A Multi-AZ replication group with multiple readers can provide HA too; this wording does not explicitly include sharding for the selected solution's distributed capacity, so the original single-answer distinction is incomplete.
Autoscaling adjusts capacity but does not by itself distribute replicas across AZs or enable automatic failover.
Keeping full running instances ready incurs ongoing compute charges instead of retaining initialized state in a hibernated warm pool.
Spot pricing does not shorten initialization and interruptions can remove prepared capacity.
Capacity Reservations guarantee capacity availability but do not pre-initialize the application or restore its loaded memory.
Manual scaling reacts only after an operator intervenes and adds operational work.
Predictive scaling relies on learned recurring patterns; random sudden increases need reactive demand-based scaling.
Scheduled scaling cannot anticipate traffic spikes on random days.
An EC2 Auto Scaling group does not automatically configure shared PostgreSQL state and elastic database compute.
A fixed larger RDS instance incurs idle capacity cost and still needs manual resizing for unpredictable demand.
Redshift is an analytics warehouse, not a compatible PostgreSQL transactional application database.
A higher throttling limit does not remove Lambda cold starts at the beginning of the day.
An alarm is not a daily prewarming schedule, and a one-time invocation does not guarantee sufficient initialized environments.
More memory can speed execution but does not proactively create initialized environments before employees arrive.
S3 File Gateway exposes an on-premises file share backed by S3 for collecting the CSV files.
FSx File Gateway uses an FSx Windows backend rather than writing CSV objects into S3 for Athena queries.
A Glue crawler discovers the CSV schema and creates Data Catalog tables.
An EMR cluster adds compute and management overhead for periodic SQL queries that Athena runs serverlessly.
A Redshift cluster adds warehouse compute cost for occasional queries directly over the S3 dataset.
Athena queries the CSV data in S3 using the cataloged schema without provisioning database servers.
The customer provides the site power and network connectivity needed by Outposts.
AWS operates the Outposts virtualization, underlying storage systems, and managed AWS service infrastructure.
The customer controls physical security and access to the data center housing the racks.
AWS maintains the hardware components within the racks; the customer supplies facility power and network connections.
Physical maintenance and replacement of Outposts components are AWS responsibilities.
The customer plans sufficient application capacity to tolerate server failures and maintenance; AWS manages the Outposts hardware itself.
choices.solution: Providing extrafficapacity for Amazon ECS clusters to mitigate server failures and maintenance events

choices.explanation: An ALB handles HTTP-family requests, not arbitrary TCP protocol traffic on the application port.
CloudFront supports HTTP/HTTPS on its supported ports, not this arbitrary high-throughput TCP endpoint.
API Gateway does not expose arbitrary TCP listeners and cannot act as the proposed TCP load balancer.
A snapshot is a point-in-time copy and does not continuously catch up with new writes before cutover.

A compatible Aurora PostgreSQL read replica follows the RDS PostgreSQL source until cutover. Stop source writes, wait for replication to catch up, and promote the replica into an independent cluster; this minimizes data loss and downtime.
S3 import requires an export/import workflow and does not provide automatic live replication of subsequent changes.
Dump and restore take additional time and leave changes after the dump unsynchronized unless extra replication is added.
Separate snapshots and custom instance-recreation templates require more orchestration than EC2-level managed backups.
Elastic Beanstalk is not a general restoration service for every existing EC2 instance configuration.
Custom backup and restore functions add scheduling, error-handling, and maintenance work.
Inline Map supports at most 40 concurrent iterations, below the requested thousands of parallel items.
Glue suits ETL processing but does not directly provide per-item distributed workflow orchestration for all these heterogeneous tasks.
Manually coordinating many functions requires custom fan-out, tracking, and retry handling.
The usable 400-Mbps link cannot transfer 10 PB in six weeks, even with optimized managed transfers.
rsync does not directly target S3, and the network bandwidth remains far too low.
Parallel copies cannot increase the total 400-Mbps bandwidth available for this enormous dataset.

With only a 500 Mbps uplink bandwidth shared among other on-premises applications, transferring 10 PB of data over the internet would be impractical and time-consuming. AWS Snowball provides a physical device that can be shipped to the company to facilitate faster initial data transfer. Historical-service limitation: Snowball Edge is available only to eligible existing customers since November 7, 2025; new customers need a current physical-transfer or online-transfer alternative.
File Gateway supplies NFS/SMB rather than preserving the applications' iSCSI block interfaces.
EBS is attached to AWS compute and does not directly supply a locally cached on-premises iSCSI storage interface.
Stored volumes retain the entire primary dataset locally, so they do not reduce local storage dependency as much as cached volumes.
Glacier archival access requires restoration and does not keep objects immediately available.
One Zone-IA reduces resilience to an AZ loss, contrary to maximum durability for these objects.
Intelligent-Tiering adds monitoring fees before a fixed 30-day transition when the access pattern is already known.
A smaller instance and magnetic disks reduce processing and I/O capacity while keeping large binaries in expensive database storage.
Increasing compute and provisioned IOPS increases cost without removing document binaries from the database.
DynamoDB's 400-KB item limit cannot hold the average 6-MB documents directly.

608.question: A company has an application that serves clients that are deployed in more than 20,000 retail storefront locations around the world. The application consists of backend web services that are exposed over HTTPS on port 443. The application is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The retail locations communicate with the web application over the public internet. The company allows each retail location to register the IP address that the retail location has been allocated by its local ISP. The company's security team recommends to increase the security of the application endpoint by restricting access to only the IP addresses registered by the retail locations. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the ALB. Use IP-set rules to allow only registered retail-location IP addresses and update the sets as registrations change. Split the addresses across multiple IP sets as required by quotas.
choices.explanation: WAF IP-set rules filter HTTP requests at the ALB. More than 20,000 addresses require multiple IP sets under the standard per-set quota; configure the web ACL to block requests that match none of the approved sets.
Firewall Manager centrally manages policies but still needs an actual WAF policy/web ACL; it does not directly inspect ALB requests through unspecified firewall rules.
choices.solution: Deploy AWS Firewall Manager to manage the ALB. Configure firewall rules to restrict traffic to the ALB. Modify the firewall rules to include the registered IP addresses.

choices.explanation: ALBs do not provide an arbitrary Lambda request-authorizer hook as proposed.
A rule per location exceeds practical network ACL limits and requires extensive rule administration.
IAM table permissions do not by themselves restrict particular rows or cells containing sensitive information.
Pre-ingestion redaction adds transformation code and removes data rather than selectively restricting its visibility.
Deleting sensitive content with a periodic function creates an exposure window and custom data-maintenance work.
An EC2 API endpoint does not supply private S3 access, and Site-to-Site VPN traffic still traverses public internet paths.
A transit gateway does not attach directly to S3 buckets, and an internet VPN does not meet the no-public-internet path requirement.
Proxy servers and NAT add operations and public endpoint routing instead of direct private S3 connectivity.
A usage quota rejects excess data submissions rather than retaining them for processing when capacity becomes available.
SNS pushes requests and does not provide the durable replayable streaming backlog needed to absorb ingestion bursts.
Containerization and EC2 scaling still require startup time and do not independently buffer requests arriving faster than workers can process them.
An internet gateway uses public routing and cannot be named as the authenticated source identity in an S3 bucket policy.
A bucket cannot terminate a VPN connection; a VPN alone does not create the private AWS service endpoint.
NAT uses the public service endpoint and does not establish the requested private endpoint path.
Application encryption requires changing code rather than enabling managed encryption for the secrets store.

Use EKS managed KMS-backed envelope encryption for Kubernetes secrets. Clusters running Kubernetes 1.28 or later provide this by default, with an optional customer-managed key. This avoids application-side encryption code and external secret migration.
A custom encryption function adds invocation and secret-handling orchestration.
Moving secrets to Parameter Store changes the application retrieval model and does not encrypt existing Kubernetes secret objects in etcd.
PrivateLink adds service-endpoint infrastructure unnecessary for simple tier isolation within the VPC.
An endpoint alone does not provide application-layer load balancing or the intended tier-specific ALB routing.
Subnet ACLs identify IP ranges rather than dynamic web-tier security-group membership, adding maintenance as Auto Scaling changes instances.
A generic agent installation alone lacks Container Insights' Kubernetes discovery and curated aggregation of container metrics and logs.
App Mesh is a service networking layer; it does not independently provide the requested metrics/log storage dashboard.
CloudTrail records AWS API activity, not all application metrics and logs from the containers.
Macie discovers sensitive S3 data rather than comprehensively detecting malicious workload and account activity.
Inspector discovers software vulnerabilities, and CloudTrail is not a security-findings dashboard.
Config tracks resource configuration compliance rather than detecting malicious access patterns and runtime threats.
Lustre requires its own client protocol rather than providing the requested NFS interface.
EFS provides managed shared NFS storage that multiple Linux EC2 instances can mount concurrently.
S3 is object storage rather than a natively mountable shared NFS filesystem.
Manual copying requires custom scheduling and verification and does not provide managed incremental synchronization while source services continue running.
An on-premises DataSync agent transfers the existing NFS data to EFS without writing a custom migration tool.
Single-AZ storage lacks Multi-AZ synchronous failover, and daily backup copies cannot meet a five-minute cross-Region RPO.
Governance Vault Lock can be removed by authorized administrators, and daily backups cannot supply a five-minute cross-Region recovery point.

Multi-AZ FSx synchronously replicates within its Region and can preserve recent writes during local maintenance or an AZ failure. Compliance Vault Lock protects the copied backups for five years. However, daily cross-Region backups allow approximately 24 hours of data loss; this option does not meet a five-minute cross-Region RPO. No listed choice meets that interpretation of the requirement.
Single-AZ storage lacks Multi-AZ resilience, governance retention can be bypassed, and daily copies cannot satisfy a five-minute cross-Region RPO.
An IAM identity policy cannot be attached to an account root user.
Member-account roots cannot create an organization trail; the organization trail is managed centrally from the authorized organization account.
A service-linked role does not impose a deny on all developer and root API calls that could change their trails.
Instance store is ephemeral and loses data during relevant instance lifecycle events.
Memcached is an in-memory cache without the durable block-storage guarantee required here.
Throughput-optimized HDD targets large sequential transfers rather than consistent low-latency transactional I/O.
CORS controls which browser origins may read responses; it does not replicate objects to another Region.
S3 Lifecycle transitions or expires objects within a bucket; it does not copy them into a second bucket.
Custom copy Lambda code adds retry, permissions, and monitoring work compared with managed Cross-Region Replication.

DynamoDB supports evolving item attributes, and on-demand capacity adapts to changing request volume without provisioning throughput. CloudFront and S3 independently scale delivery of the static application.
choices.solution: Deploy Amazon DynamoDB as the database solution using on-demand capacity mode.

choices.explanation: Aurora Serverless retains a relational schema and database engine. DynamoDB better fits rapidly evolving item attributes and highly scalable key-value or document access for this application.

Provisioned DynamoDB autoscaling can lag abrupt traffic increases and requires configured capacity limits. On-demand mode avoids managing provisioned throughput and better matches the requested scalability during the large daily demand swing.
S3 hosts the static content and CloudFront caches it globally without operating web servers.
Serving static files from EC2 and EFS adds server capacity management when S3 and CloudFront scale directly.
Shield addresses DDoS protection rather than SQL-injection and cross-site-scripting request inspection.
Adding CloudFront and Shield does not supply the missing WAF application exploit rules.
A separate CloudFront distribution and WAF association add configuration when a Regional WAF web ACL can protect the REST API stage directly.
Creating 1,500 IAM users duplicates the existing workforce identities and adds password and lifecycle management.
Cognito has no native Active Directory user-pool type; workforce SAML federation preserves the existing directory identities.
Cross-account role trust alone does not authenticate the on-premises AD users; a federation provider must issue the trusted identity assertions.
CloudFront and WAF can block countries, but this option does not specify routing each location to the ALB serving its licensed content.
WAF can filter access but does not provide the global DNS selection of the correct regional content endpoint.
Geoproximity routes by distance and adjustable bias, not the explicit country or geographic boundaries used for distribution rights.
Snowball's standard workflow is offline device shipment, not the specified managed online migration and validation task.
File Gateway supplies cached file access; it does not provide DataSync's migration task and source/destination verification workflow.
Transfer Acceleration is enabled on an S3 bucket, not an on-premises accelerator, and does not manage end-to-end dataset validation.
One DNS instance is a failure point, and alarms do not supply redundant authoritative DNS.
Migrating servers retains operating-system and DNS server management instead of using managed Route 53 hosting.
Desired capacity one leaves one running server; CPU scaling does not provide continuous redundant authoritative DNS service.
Config rules do not supply the built-in organization-wide incomplete multipart-upload count dashboard.
An SCP controls permissions and cannot generate metrics or cost-compliance reports.
A Multi-Region Access Point routes requests to buckets; it does not report incomplete upload counts.
Upgrading production directly provides no isolated validation environment and makes rollback depend on snapshot restoration.
Manual backup and restore add transfer work and cutover coordination.
DMS requires operating a separate replication workflow instead of the integrated Blue/Green test and switchover mechanism.
RDS Blue/Green Deployments creates a separate synchronized environment for testing supported production changes, then switches over with reduced downtime. Confirm engine and feature support.
A reservation incurs a long-term commitment for a job running only two hours daily and requires server management.
Lambda cannot run a single two-hour job because its invocation limit is 15 minutes.
EC2-backed ECS requires operating the worker instances and their capacity instead of paying for an isolated scheduled Fargate task.
Neptune Streams already captures graph changes; introducing Kinesis requires another forwarding and processing integration.
QLDB is a ledger database rather than a graph database optimized for relationship traversal and recommendations.
Neptune Streams captures Neptune changes, not QLDB changes, and QLDB is not the graph database requested.
Glacier archival data must be restored before frequent analysis and cannot be modified as a shared live filesystem.
An ordinary EBS volume cannot be concurrently shared by instances across Availability Zones.
Provisioned IOPS does not remove EBS Multi-Attach's same-AZ restriction or provide a managed concurrent shared filesystem.
A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance standby is not available for read queries.
Transfer Acceleration is an S3 feature, not an RDS query-performance setting.
Firehose does not act as a database query proxy or scale RDS read execution.
S3 does not have a global tables feature; DynamoDB global tables are unrelated to this object-sharing requirement.
A public bucket exposes telemetry to anyone who discovers it, not just the agencies.
Separate analyst users require managing long-lived credentials in the source account instead of trusting scoped identities in agency accounts.
S3 copies do not expose the required CIFS/SMB and NFS interfaces without additional filesystem infrastructure.
Backup copying and restoration require recovery operations rather than maintaining an already replicated ONTAP filesystem.
EFS supplies NFS, not CIFS/SMB, and migrating filesystem platforms changes the existing protocol support.
ECS is not a direct SNS subscription endpoint; adding a container processing stage requires more integration.
EKS is not a direct SNS subscription endpoint and introduces Kubernetes processing infrastructure.

choices.solution: Create an SNS subscription that sends the event to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Configure the SQS queue to trigger a Lambda function.
choices.explanation: An SNS subscription to SQS durably buffers the notifications. A Lambda event source mapping polls SQS and retries failures, decoupling publication from processing.
Server Migration Service is unrelated to event buffering and cannot be polled as the proposed SNS event queue.
Fargate containers require service/task orchestration and startup capacity compared with request-driven Lambda for this small key-value service.
Lambda scales application code with request-driven invocations without maintaining compute hosts.
DynamoDB provides a managed key-value database; use on-demand capacity for unpredictable traffic.
EC2 scaling requires host maintenance and launch time during sudden spikes from zero.
Aurora adds relational database capacity and schema management unnecessary for simple unpredictable key-value requests.
A presigned S3 URL grants temporary access to a specific operation without distributing AWS credentials. Its effective permissions and expiry are bounded by the signing identity and credentials.
Per-employee IAM users and policies create unnecessary identity and credential administration.
File Gateway requires network mounts and appliance management across globally distributed employee devices.
SFTP endpoints and custom identity-provider credentials add protocol and authentication administration compared with scoped expiring links.

639.question: A company is building a new furniture inventory application. The company has deployed the application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. The EC2 instances run behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in their VPC. A solutions architect has observed that incoming traffic seems to favor one EC2 instance, resulting in latency for some requests. What should the solutions architect do to resolve this issue?

choices.explanation: Changing load-balancer type does not directly address persistent session affinity and may change supported application features.
Additional instances can remain underused if sticky sessions continue pinning traffic to the favored instance.
Health-check frequency affects failure detection, not the allocation of healthy clients bound by sticky sessions.
The Lambda resource policy controls who can invoke the function, not its permission to decrypt data.
Authorize the Lambda execution role in the KMS key policy to decrypt with the key.
A resource policy is not an IAM principal to name in the KMS key policy; use the execution role.
IAM permission policies attach to the function's execution role, not directly to the Lambda resource.

choices.solution: Create a Lambda execution role with kms:Decrypt on the specific KMS key and s3:GetObject on the required objects, and attach the role to the function.
choices.explanation: Attach an execution role with kms:Decrypt and the required S3 read permissions to the function.
Cost and Usage Reports are delivered to S3, not directly to Kinesis, and EMR adds unnecessary cluster cost.
Per-member reports and a Redshift warehouse add management and running cost compared with querying the consolidated S3 report.

choices.solution: Enable Cost and Usage Reports for member accounts. Deliver the reports to Amazon Kinesis. Use Amazon QuickSight for analysis.
choices.explanation: The reports are not delivered directly to Kinesis, and QuickSight still needs a queryable data source.
An ALB does not support arbitrary UDP traffic.
DNS weighting does not track individual dynamic targets with NLB-style flow distribution and health checks.
A NAT instance with forwarding is a self-managed bottleneck and does not automatically track the elastic target fleet.

choices.solution: Store the logs in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena for analysis.

choices.explanation: A continuously provisioned relational database adds ingestion and compute cost for weekly analytical queries over raw logs.
Maintaining search indexes and cluster capacity costs more for occasional SQL analysis directly over stored objects.
An EMR cluster requires execution and lifecycle management when Athena provides serverless on-demand SQL.

choices.solution: Request an ACM public certificate with example.com and *.example.com as subject alternative names, and associate it with the ALB HTTPS listener.
choices.explanation: Request an ACM public certificate covering example.com and *.example.com. A wildcard does not cover the apex domain or multiple subdomain levels.
Private certificates are not trusted by ordinary public browsers without distributing the private CA trust chain.
A certificate only for the apex does not cover country subdomains, and a private certificate does not add public browser trust.
An issued certificate cannot switch validation method in place; requesting DNS validation initially avoids duplicate validation work.

DNS validation proves domain ownership and supports automated renewal while the validation records and certificate usage remain valid. ACM also supports email validation for public wildcard certificates.
CloudHSM key material resides inside AWS, violating the requirement to retain keys in the external on-premises manager.

A KMS external key store keeps key material and cryptographic operations in an external key manager while retaining compatible KMS integrations. The customer is responsible for external availability and latency.
The default KMS store retains key material in AWS rather than the mandated external key manager.
A CloudHSM-backed custom store still uses HSMs hosted in AWS rather than the external vendor key manager.
EFS supplies a general-purpose NFS filesystem rather than Lustre's parallel HPC architecture and sub-millisecond target performance.
S3 object storage is not a native shared parallel filesystem, and mount adapters cannot guarantee the required semantics and latency.
RAM does not turn an S3 bucket into a mountable low-latency parallel filesystem.
Geolocation DNS depends on resolver caching and does not provide rapid health-based rerouting over a global accelerator path.
CloudFront serves HTTP/HTTPS content rather than arbitrary real-time VoIP traffic.
A regional ALB cannot provide automatic multi-Region endpoint failover and does not handle arbitrary VoIP transport.
Scratch filesystems lack the replicated storage and automatic recovery of persistent Lustre filesystems.
EFS bursting depends on filesystem throughput credits and does not target this sustained sub-millisecond parallel HPC workload.
Provisioning EFS throughput does not provide Lustre's optimized sub-millisecond parallel access architecture.
gp2 IOPS scale with storage size and cannot be independently provisioned as proposed.
io1 can meet the performance but costs more than gp3 for this IOPS target.
Magnetic storage cannot provide the required predictable 15,000-IOPS performance.

choices.solution: Migrate to Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server. Use read replicas for reporting purposes

choices.explanation: SQL Server on EC2 retains operating-system, backup, patching, and replication administration.
DynamoDB requires a different data model and has no proposed conventional on-demand SQL reporting replicas.
Aurora MySQL requires converting SQL Server schema, code, and application queries rather than preserving the existing engine.
One Zone-IA can lose data if its AZ is destroyed, violating the requirement that the images not be lost.
One Zone-IA reduces resilience, and Glacier Flexible Retrieval does not provide instant access after day 360.

S3 Standard-IA keeps multi-AZ durability for the infrequently accessed period. Glacier Instant Retrieval meets the instant-access requirement after 360 days, and Deep Archive is the lowest-cost tier that still supports retrieval within 12 hours for long-term audit data.
Glacier Flexible Retrieval requires restoration, violating instant availability during years one through five.
A long-running cluster incurs instance costs during the 18 hours each day when the workload is idle.

A transient EMR cluster avoids paying for idle capacity between six-hour daily runs. Keep primary and core nodes on On-Demand instances so data is not lost, and use Spot only for replaceable task nodes.
Core nodes store HDFS data; Spot interruption of core capacity creates data-availability and loss risk.
The cluster remains billed while idle, and interruptible core nodes expose its stored data to failure risk.
An SCP denies API operations but does not look up the creator's cost center or add tags to resources.

CloudTrail events can trigger EventBridge, which invokes Lambda immediately after resource creation. Lambda can look up the creator's cost center in RDS and apply the correct tag. SCPs cannot dynamically derive tag values from a database.
A scheduled rule cannot invoke a CloudFormation stack as the proposed resource-tagging target and does not react directly to each creation event.
A default tag value does not identify the creating user's actual cost center from RDS.
A single public Beanstalk instance does not supply redundant application capacity or a highly available shared session store.
Moving an existing PHP server directly to Lambda requires runtime packaging and application changes, and serving static content through functions is unnecessary.
The original backend EC2 instance remains a single failure point even after static content and Redis are moved.

Use CloudFront + S3 for highly available static content, an ALB + ECS Fargate for the PHP application, and Multi-AZ ElastiCache for Redis sessions. This removes the single EC2/Redis failure point and uses managed services.
WAF cannot be associated directly with an NLB; its transport-layer stickiness also differs from ALB cookie-based sessions.
Gateway Load Balancer serves network appliances rather than a public application endpoint with WAF and HTTP session affinity.
An ALB provides a public HTTP endpoint and supports sticky sessions when configured on the target group.
A second target group and public instance addresses do not provide the required WAF-protected sticky-session endpoint.
A WAF web ACL associated with the ALB filters application-layer threats before requests reach the instances.
EBS plus an EC2 web server adds provisioned storage, compute, and maintenance costs for rarely accessed images.
EFS and an EC2 server add filesystem and compute costs unnecessary for simple image objects.
Standard has a higher storage rate than Standard-IA when images are requested only once or twice annually.
S3 Standard-IA is highly available and cost-effective for objects read only once or twice per year. EBS/EFS require servers or file-system capacity, and S3 Standard costs more for infrequent access.
A security group is VPC-scoped and does not automatically update independent security groups in every account.
A customer-managed VPC prefix list centralizes the office CIDRs. Sharing it through AWS RAM lets security groups in multiple accounts reference the same list, so a CIDR change is made once.
AWS-managed prefix lists cannot be edited with the company's office CIDRs, and Security Hub does not enforce this rule-update workflow.
Firewall Manager can manage common security groups but adds policy administration and cost when a shared customer-managed prefix list directly solves CIDR maintenance.
A cluster placement group places compute instances close together within one Availability Zone to reduce inter-instance network latency.
Partition placement favors hardware fault isolation rather than the tightly packed lowest-latency networking of a cluster placement group.
Lustre does not provide the required SMB and NFS multiprotocol interface.
FSx for OpenZFS provides NFS access, not the required SMB interface.
FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides shared NFS and SMB access to the same storage, meeting the multiprotocol requirement.
A private endpoint does not increase the available bandwidth of the nearly saturated VPN connection.
A new Direct Connect circuit requires provisioning lead time and cost for a one-time two-week transfer deadline.

A Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device avoids consuming the already 90%-utilized VPN and is designed for secure offline transfer of tens of terabytes within a migration window like this. Historical-service limitation: Snowball Edge is available only to eligible existing customers since November 7, 2025; new customers need a current physical-transfer or online-transfer alternative.
Storage Gateway adds hybrid storage access but does not overcome the saturated transfer path.
Load balancing distributes existing capacity but does not launch enough instances before the predictable peak.
Memory-based scaling is reactive and needs custom metrics; it does not guarantee capacity before peak hours.
CPU-based scaling begins after demand increases, leaving a startup interval with insufficient capacity.
Scheduled scaling launches instances before the predictable peak, giving initialization time and avoiding a delay while reactive policies detect traffic.
DynamoDB is not an RDS connection-pooling proxy and requires a different database model.
RDS Proxy pools application connections and reduces database connection overhead during bursts. It does not independently scale database compute or solve query bottlenecks.
A self-managed EC2 proxy requires patching, availability, and connection-management operations.
A Lambda function is not a persistent managed database connection-pool endpoint and requires custom proxy logic.
EBS Elastic Volumes cannot shrink existing volumes, and storage utilization does not explain accumulating snapshot retention.
Custom monitoring adds work, and EBS volume size cannot be reduced in place.
One-time deletion reduces current cost but does not automate retention to prevent continued snapshot accumulation.

Delete nonessential snapshots and use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager to automate snapshot creation and retention. EBS volumes cannot simply be shrunk with Elastic Volumes, and manual cleanup has more operational overhead.
The execution role is for ECS infrastructure operations, not the application task's data access; encryption alone does not restrict MySQL connections.
AWS managed key policies cannot be customized this way, and granting an execution role does not establish application task and database network isolation.

The ECS task role supplies application AWS permissions; the task execution role is used by ECS to launch tasks. Restrict S3 authorization to the task role and RDS network access to the tasks' security group. An RDS API interface endpoint does not provide private database SQL connectivity.
choices.solution: Restrict S3 bucket access to the ECS application task role. Place the RDS database in private subnets and allow MySQL traffic only from the ECS tasks' security group. Give tasks only the required S3 and database credentials or IAM permissions.

choices.explanation: An RDS API endpoint does not provide private MySQL SQL connectivity, and restricting S3 to a VPC endpoint still allows other authorized clients using that endpoint.

The workload has rare, abrupt CPU spikes. Burstable instances in unlimited mode can absorb short spikes cost-effectively, and request-based scaling reacts automatically to actual demand. Scheduled scaling cannot predict irregular twice-monthly events.

Compute-optimized instances can scale and are technically viable, but provision their compute continuously rather than exploiting the low baseline with occasional unlimited bursting. The prompt does not provide enough sizing data to prove one family always performs better.
Scheduled scaling cannot respond to an issue's actual start unless its timing is known in advance.
Predictive scaling depends on learnable recurrence and does not react directly to the unpredictable request surge.
Organizations manages accounts and policies, not deployment of the application's network and resource infrastructure.
CloudFormation defines reproducible infrastructure deployments. Config records supported resource configuration history and evaluates compliance rules to audit changes.
Organizations does not deploy arbitrary infrastructure, and Service Catalog is not a configuration-change audit recorder.
Service Catalog governs provisioning products; Config records ongoing resource configuration changes.
An internet gateway attaches to a VPC, not separately to each AZ, and does not replicate the application or database.
RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ provides database failover without changing the application to a different database engine.
DynamoDB requires data-model and query changes, violating the unchanged application-code requirement.
DataSync copies files and objects; it is not a transaction-consistent MySQL replication and failover service.
An ALB and an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones provide redundant application instances and automatic replacement.
S3 gateway endpoints cannot be accessed directly from on-premises networks over Direct Connect.
Transit Gateway alone does not expose an S3 service endpoint to on-premises clients.

S3 interface endpoints are reachable from on-premises networks over Direct Connect. Gateway endpoints cannot be used from on premises; ensure private routing, DNS resolution, and endpoint policies are configured.
KMS provides encryption operations and authorization, not the private network path to S3.
Identity Center users assume roles rather than IAM groups, and the policy checks only tag presence rather than approved values.
Denying any tagged resource blocks compliant requests as well as incorrect ones.
Resource Groups organizes resources but does not prevent creation requests with missing or invalid tags.

An enforced tag policy validates values on supported tagged resources, but does not block all untagged creation. Pair it with request-tag conditions in an SCP for supported creation APIs to require the tag across accounts.
choices.solution: Use an enforced Organizations tag policy for approved application-name values and an SCP that denies supported resource-creation requests when the required application-name tag is missing or invalid.

choices.explanation: A custom rotation function and schedule add code and password synchronization work.
An ad hoc CLI password change does not provide automatic secure 30-day rotation.
AWS Secrets Manager integrates with RDS and can rotate database credentials automatically on a schedule, avoiding custom Lambda scheduling or manual CLI changes.
Parameter Store does not natively rotate RDS passwords; additional automation is required.
On-demand mode does not accept provisioned RCU/WCU settings; known throughput can be scheduled in provisioned mode for the test window.

Provisioned capacity fits the known request rate. Schedule capacity increases before each weekly test and reduce capacity to the supported minimum afterward. Year-long reserved capacity is poorly utilized by a workload running only four hours per week; compare actual on-demand prices for the workload.
A one-year reservation commits to capacity far beyond four hours of weekly testing.
A three-year capacity commitment is even less suited to the infrequent test schedule.
A zero-spend budget alerts on any spending, which is unsuitable for an existing application with legitimate recurring cost.
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection is designed to identify unusual spend and send alerts to stakeholders. A zero-spend budget is for detecting any spend, not anomalies in an existing workload.
Pricing Calculator estimates planned cost rather than detecting anomalous actual spending.
CloudWatch billing thresholds are not the usage-pattern anomaly model provided by Cost Anomaly Detection.
Glue Spark jobs add processing-job configuration for quick exploratory SQL that Athena executes directly.
AWS Glue can crawl the S3 data to build metadata, and Athena can query the files directly in S3 without provisioning a cluster. This is the lowest-operational-overhead path for quick ad-hoc analysis.
An EMR cluster and Hive metastore add infrastructure and management for a simple on-demand S3 analysis.
Kinesis analytics processes streaming sources rather than querying a static S3 dataset directly as proposed.
Copying older files alone does not specify the storage class, ongoing SMB interface, or retrieval workflow needed to meet the requirement.

S3 File Gateway preserves the SMB interface and caches recent files locally. An S3 Lifecycle rule can transition older objects to Deep Archive for low-cost retention. Archived objects must be explicitly restored before the gateway can read them; use standard retrieval and an operational restore process consistent with the 24-hour window.
FSx File Gateway uses FSx storage, so an S3 Lifecycle rule cannot transition its filesystem data.
Direct S3 access changes the existing SMB workflow and requires per-user access configuration.
RDS storage autoscaling does not scale DB instance compute or offload read queries.
An RDS read replica serves read-only queries separately from the writer; the application must direct eligible reads to it.
A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance standby cannot serve application reads.
ElastiCache stores reusable query results to reduce database reads; configure cache invalidation and expiry to meet freshness requirements.
Moving clients into the DB's AZ does not add database read capacity and reduces application AZ resilience.
An EC2-attached role does not prevent the existing storage administrator from deleting snapshots.
A deny policy changes the administrator's existing rights, contrary to the requirement.
Recycle Bin allows deletion followed by possible recovery; snapshot locking directly prevents deletion during the retention period.

EBS Snapshot Lock prevents deletion of a locked snapshot without changing the storage administrator's IAM rights. Compliance mode enforces the retention period after any cooling-off interval; governance locks can be removed by authorized users.
Data Streams requires a consumer to deliver records into OpenSearch; Firehose supplies that managed destination delivery.

VPC Flow Logs can publish to CloudWatch Logs, and Kinesis Data Firehose can deliver the log stream to OpenSearch Service with minimal custom processing. CloudTrail is not a destination for VPC Flow Logs.
VPC Flow Logs cannot send network flow records into a CloudTrail trail.
CloudTrail records API activity and cannot serve as the proposed VPC Flow Logs destination.

For an infrequently used development cluster, a managed node group consisting only of Spot Instances is the most cost-effective choice while still letting EKS manage the nodes. Mixing in On-Demand capacity adds cost that the requirement does not justify.
An On-Demand baseline adds cost that is unnecessary for infrequent interruption-tolerant development resiliency tests.
A separately created Auto Scaling group is self-managed rather than an EKS managed node group.
All On-Demand nodes miss the Spot savings appropriate for this nonproduction test workload.
SSE-S3 keys are managed by S3; the company cannot create, disable, and rotate them itself.

A customer-managed KMS key gives the company control over key policies, enable/disable state, and rotation while keeping key management managed by AWS. SSE-S3 and AWS-managed keys do not provide the same control.
AWS managed keys do not give the company full lifecycle and rotation control.
Downloading and reuploading every object adds transfer and encryption-code work compared with native SSE-KMS.
Object Lock requires versioning and prevents permanent deletion of protected backup versions during retention.
Versioning alone does not prevent authorized permanent deletion during the mandatory retention period.
A default compliance retention period protects new backup versions for 30 days.
choices.solution: Configure a default Object Lock compliance-mode retention period of 30 days for new backup objects.

choices.explanation: Lifecycle expiration schedules deletion but does not prevent users from deleting an object before day 30.
Lifecycle expiration hides current objects with delete markers. Also configure noncurrent-version expiration and delete-marker cleanup for permanent removal after retention; deletion is asynchronous.
choices.solution: Configure S3 Lifecycle expiration after 30 days, noncurrent-version expiration for eligible unlocked versions, and expired delete-marker cleanup. Allow asynchronous deletion after retention expires.

choices.explanation: An object tag is metadata and does not itself enforce retention or automatic deletion.
AWS DataSync supports S3 and EFS locations and can transfer only changed data. That avoids custom Lambda/EC2 synchronization logic and prevents unchanged destination files from being overwritten.
Custom Lambda copying requires code, retries, EFS connectivity, and handling object sizes and function execution limits.
Transferring all data adds unnecessary scanning and rewriting work when only changed files should be copied.
An EC2 synchronization script requires server maintenance and custom scheduling and error handling.
A customer-managed KMS key can encrypt EBS volumes and gives the company control over key rotation. AWS-owned keys are not customer-controlled, and imported key material adds operational overhead.
AWS controls rotation of AWS managed keys; the company cannot configure its own rotation policy.
Imported material adds external generation and rotation operations rather than the simple automatic rotation of an AWS-generated customer-managed key.
AWS owned keys are controlled by AWS and do not provide customer lifecycle or rotation control.

Use IAM conditions to prevent unencrypted volume creation and Config rules with Systems Manager Automation for detection and remediation. Existing EBS volumes cannot be encrypted in place; remediation creates an encrypted snapshot copy and replacement volume, then arranges a safe cutover.
KMS permissions do not ensure newly created volumes are encrypted, and custom event detection/remediation adds more code than Config and Systems Manager integration.
Macie discovers sensitive S3 data, not unencrypted EBS volumes; existing EBS volumes also cannot be encrypted in place.
Inspector detects vulnerabilities, not EBS encryption compliance; encryption remediation requires replacing unencrypted volumes with encrypted copies.
An ALB and Multi-AZ EC2 Auto Scaling group provide a resilient web tier while preserving the application runtime.
An Auto Scaling group and NLB do not implement MySQL replication, shared state, or safe database failover.
RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ provides a managed database standby and failover while retaining MySQL compatibility.
Moving the existing web tier into Lambda functions changes the execution and deployment model and requires application refactoring.
DynamoDB requires converting the MySQL schema and queries into a different data model and API.
CloudFront edge locations do not host arbitrary EC2 application workloads or extend VPC subnets, and the application remains in the prohibited Region.

Local Zones extend an AWS Region to locations closer to users and can provide single-digit millisecond latency. The selected Local Zone must satisfy the regulation and support the needed services; placing compute in a Local Zone does not automatically remove all dependency on its parent Region.
Regional edge caches cache HTTP content; they do not host application servers or accept extended VPC subnets.
Wavelength is designed for applications at participating mobile-carrier 5G edges, not a general low-latency local deployment for the company's location.
